author: sameenhewage
body:
## Summary

Adds the non-secret routing **lookup foundation** for Bloomwire-managed WhatsApp integrations: a small, read-only resolver that maps Meta routing identifiers (`phone_number_id` / `business_account_id` / `routing_key` / `provider`) to the owning `BloomwireChannelIntegration`, plus a DB-level uniqueness guarantee so that lookup is deterministic. This is the groundwork the future Bloomwire Global Meta/WhatsApp webhook router (ADR 0004, Phase 8) will build on.

**This is not the Phase 8 global webhook router. No webhook endpoint or message ingestion behavior changed. No secrets are copied or exposed.**

## What changed

- **New** `Bloomwire::ChannelIntegrations::WhatsappResolver` (`app/services/bloomwire/channel_integrations/whatsapp_resolver.rb`) — a deterministic, tenant-safe, read-only resolver over **managed WhatsApp** integrations only.
- **New migration** (`db/migrate/20260624000000_...`) replacing the non-unique `phone_number_id` lookup index with a partial **UNIQUE** index `index_bw_channel_integrations_on_managed_phone_number_id` (`WHERE managed_by_bloomwire`), so no two Bloomwire-managed integrations can claim the same Meta number.
- **New** resolver spec (`spec/services/bloomwire/channel_integrations/whatsapp_resolver_spec.rb`) — 12 examples.
- `db/schema.rb` and the model's schema annotation regenerated to match.

## Routing metadata / resolver behavior

- **Scope:** only `managed_by_bloomwire` + `app_kind = 'whatsapp'` rows are considered; non-managed and non-WhatsApp rows are ignored.
- **Lookup keys:** `provider`, `phone_number_id`, `business_account_id`, `routing_key`. All supplied identifiers must match the **same** row (AND), so mismatched identifiers from two integrations resolve to `nil` (tenant-safe).
- **Deterministic + ambiguity-safe:** returns the single matching row, or `nil` when there is no match **or** more than one row matches (e.g. a `business_account_id` alone, which can cover many numbers in one WABA). It never picks a row arbitrarily.
- **Secret-free / read-only:** queries only the Bloomwire ownership table; never reads `Channel::Whatsapp#provider_config`, never copies provider secrets, never touches Chatwoot conversation/message/contact data.
- **Uniqueness rationale:** `phone_number_id` is only ever set for WhatsApp (NULL for other kinds, and NULLs are distinct in a UNIQUE index), so scoping the unique index by `managed_by_bloomwire` guarantees deterministic routing for managed WhatsApp numbers while leaving non-WhatsApp managed rows unconstrained. It is also more robust than an `app_kind = 'whatsapp'` predicate for the router (no two managed integrations may claim the same number regardless of kind).

## Tests run (exact commands)

```
bundle exec rails db:migrate
bundle exec rspec spec/services/bloomwire/channel_integrations/whatsapp_resolver_spec.rb
bundle exec rspec spec/services/bloomwire spec/models/bloomwire_channel_integration_spec.rb spec/requests/super_admin/bloomwire_channel_integrations_spec.rb
bundle exec rubocop app/services/bloomwire/channel_integrations/whatsapp_resolver.rb spec/services/bloomwire/channel_integrations/whatsapp_resolver_spec.rb db/migrate/20260624000000_add_unique_managed_whatsapp_phone_number_id_index_to_bloomwire_channel_integrations.rb app/models/bloomwire_channel_integration.rb
```

Results: RSpec **269 examples, 0 failures** (including the 12 new resolver examples); RuboCop **0 offenses** on the 4 changed Ruby files.

## Out of scope

- The Phase 8 global webhook router / Meta payload processing (ADR 0004).
- Any webhook endpoint, signature verification, or message ingestion change.
- Any UI / tenant-facing change.
- DTO / serializer secret scrub (tracked separately).

author: thekaveh
body:
## Summary

User feedback: the Copy dialog's Cancel button is the only one that looks right. Every other ModalButton variant fills its background with `\$accent` (primary) or `\$danger` (danger), which reads as "spillover" against the modal container, and the focus state inherits `text-style: bold reverse` from `ModalButton.DEFAULT_CSS` that inverts fg/bg into the same solid-block effect. Other modals (FirstRun / Resume / inline ConnectionForm) were getting no theme styling at all because every rule was scoped to `ConfirmModal > Container > .modal-footer > ModalButton`.

## What changed

1. **Generalized the per-theme rules to `ModalButton`** (was `ConfirmModal > Container > .modal-footer > ModalButton`). Same outlined look applies to every modal that uses ModalButton.
2. **Dropped solid-fill backgrounds.** Every variant resting state uses `background: \$bg`, so the button sits visibly inside the `\$bg-elev` modal container with a clean outlined look. Variant identity is the border + text color, never the fill:
   - `-primary`: `border: round \$accent` + `color: \$accent`
   - `-danger`: `border: round \$danger` + `color: \$danger`
3. **Hover + focus lift to `\$bg-elev`** (the only bg change anywhere) and brighten the border/text:
   - Default hover/focus → border + text `\$accent`
   - Primary hover/focus → border + text `\$accent-hot`
   - Danger hover/focus → border stays `\$danger` (destructive signal preserved), text brightens to `\$accent-hot`
4. **Removed `text-style: bold reverse` from `modal_button.py`'s `DEFAULT_CSS`** — that was the source of the solid-block-of-accent focus effect that survived theme overrides.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest` — 954 default-tier + 184 snapshots, all green.
- [x] `uv run ruff check .` / `uv run mypy src` — clean.
- [x] All modal snapshots regenerated (Confirm/FirstRun/Resume/Crash/Quick-look across 10 themes) to lock the new outlined look.

author: raullenchai
body:
## Why this PR exists

When `tool_choice=\"required\"` is set on a reasoning model (Qwen3-0.6B reproduces ~50% of the time), the streaming SSE body looked like this:

```
data: {\"id\":\"chatcmpl-c9fa6a3a\",\"choices\":[{\"index\":0,\"delta\":{\"role\":\"assistant\"}}]}

data: {\"id\":\"chatcmpl-c9fa6a3a\",\"choices\":[{\"index\":0,\"delta\":{},\"finish_reason\":\"tool_calls\"}]}

data: [DONE]
```

ZERO `delta.tool_calls` chunks — the server promised a tool call via `finish_reason=\"tool_calls\"` that was never delivered. Clients depending on the tool call (LangChain, OpenAI Python SDK, AI SDK, claude-agents) cannot proceed and the agent loop deadlocks. Bug R11-V1.

R11-V2 (sibling): some streams reached `[DONE]` without any `finish_reason` chunk at all — a hard OpenAI streaming spec violation.

See `/tmp/dogfood-0812/vlad-r1.md` R11-V1/V2 section for the live captures.

## Root cause

`_apply_forced_tool_choice_filter` correctly drops scratch anchors whose `arguments` parses as a non-object root (e.g. bare-int `\"20230805\"` from `format_date(20230805)` — qwen3 frequently emits this shape inside `<think>`). But the cap-empty / filter-empty branches in `_process_channel_routed`, `_process_with_reasoning`, and `_process_standard` then set `tool_calls_detected=True` AND emitted `finish_reason=\"tool_calls\"` regardless of whether any `tool_call` StreamEvent had reached the wire. The two predicates disagreed: the filter ate the deltas, finalize still promised them.

## Systemic fix

Introduce `_tool_calls_emitted_to_wire`, a wire-truth counter incremented at every `StreamEvent(type=\"tool_call\", ...)` emit site (channel-routed, reasoning, standard) AND in `_build_tool_call_event` (finalize recovery). Route `_compute_finish_reason` and every `if self.tool_calls_detected: emit finish_reason=\"tool_calls\"` early-exit through the counter — when zero deltas were sent, downgrade to `output.finish_reason` (typically `\"stop\"`). `tool_calls_detected` keeps its parser-saw-call semantics so the tool-prose buffer drop and harmony cut-short rescue still fire — only the wire-promise gate changes.

R11-V2 safety net: add an `else:` branch in `routes/chat.py` so every closed stream emits a synthetic `finish_reason=\"stop\"` chunk when neither `buffered_finish` nor finalize recovery produced one. Logged at WARNING so an operator can diagnose engine-side anomalies that trigger the safety net.

## Probe results (20 fires against Qwen3-0.6B + `tool_choice=\"required\"`)

| Metric | Pre-fix | Post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| R11-V1 (finish=tool_calls + zero deltas) | **10/20** | **0/20** |
| R11-V2 (no finish_reason at all) | 0/20 | 0/20 |

Post-fix verified stable across two consecutive 20-shot runs.

## Test plan

- [x] 9 new pins in `tests/test_stream_forced_tool_reasoning.py`:
  - `TestR11AInvariantFilterEmptyDoesNotPromiseToolCalls` (5 tests) — single-chunk + multi-chunk + valid-call + finalize-recovery + reset-clears-counter
  - `TestR11AInvariantHoldsAcrossSuite::test_invariant_holds_for_every_scratch_shape` — parametrized across bare_int / quoted_string / unquoted_prose / array_root shapes from the dogfood-0812 evidence
  - `TestR11V2ExactlyOneFinishReason` (2 tests) — every closed stream has exactly one finish_reason chunk

author: mcross2298
body:
## Phase 2 — Dynamic Schedule Scaling Engine

Adapts a **custom multi-week program** to fewer training days in a given week **without ever mutating the stored template**. All state lives in an instance-level override; the frontend re-renders from it.

### Architectural constraints (spec §2.1) — honored
- **Immutable templates:** `mc_custom_programs_v1` is never written.
- **Instance-level state:** a new `mc_weekly_overrides_v1` object holds the weekly overrides; `cat-custom.html` / `run-program.html` re-render from it.

### The hook
`adjustFrequency(prog, week, targetDays, strategy)` — exactly the spec signature — with two strategies:

- **Option A — Consolidation:** keep `targetDays` days this week; redistribute the dropped days' exercises into the survivors by muscle match, **Primary compounds first** (tier derived from the Phase 1 `mc-biomech.js` movement patterns), under an absolute per-session **volume cap** (~1.7× the heaviest authored day). Accessory overflow is trimmed — the *"cap + drop overflow"* behavior chosen during planning. The merge is a **pure function** of `(program, targetDays)`, so the listing and the runner rebuild byte-identical days with nothing persisted.
- **Option B — Postponement / Linear Shift:** train `targetDays` this week; the rest slide into a new **catch-up week** inserted right after, **extending the program by a week** so no session is lost. Later weeks renumber forward.

### UX (spec §2.2)
- `cat-custom.html`: an **"Adjust this week"** control opens a bottom-sheet (day-count picker · Consolidate/Postpone toggle · live preview · Reset). The day list, week tabs, and ✓-done state all resolve through `MCSchedule`; merged days show a `+ Legs, Arms` provenance chip and adjusted weeks show a banner; a postponement adds a dashed **Catch-up** week tab.
- `run-program.html`: a consolidated day is rebuilt deterministically from `?cons=<targetDays>&cd=<index>` and gets its own logging namespace; postponed weeks need no change (their links carry the original day index).

### Scope
`4-Weeks-to-Open-` only — the data-driven custom-program model is the one place an override layer is clean. The static built-in HTML programs can't be re-frequencied without editing master files (which the spec forbids).

### Verification
- `node --check` passes on every tracked `*.js`; both HTML files' inline `<script>` blocks parse clean.
- `tools/build-sw.py --check` reports current (v115, `mc-schedule.js` precached).
- Headless tests confirmed: tier classification, consolidation across 4→3/2/1 (cap trims accessories at deeper cuts, Primaries always carried), postponement extending 4→5 weeks with a catch-up week, and **listing↔runner reproducibility** of merged days.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Bug and impact **Critical:** `CompoundLiquidator.executeOperation` always reverts successful flash-loan liquidations. After approving the Instadapp aggregator for `amount + premium`, the callback transferred the contract's **entire** base-token balance to `owner`. Instadapp collects repayment via `transferFrom` **after** `executeOperation` returns, so the aggregator could not pull owed tokens and the whole transaction reverted. **Trigger:** Any call to `liquidateWithFlashLoan` where the swap returns enough base token to cover repayment (including break-even cases where `balance == owed`). ## Root cause Profit skimming used `balanceOf` as profit and transferred it all to `owner`, without reserving `owed` for flash-loan repayment. ## Fix - Read balance once, `require(balance >= owed)` - Approve aggregator for `owed` - Transfer only `balance - owed` to owner - Add regression tests (`contracts/compoundLiquidator.repay.test.mjs`) covering repayment accounting and compile guard ## Validation - `npm run ci` — all tests pass (including new CompoundLiquidator tests) Targets fix at PR #69 (`cursor/avocado-flash-loan-contracts-4a5f`).

author: rosstaco
body:
## Problem

`idc doctor` reported a valid git worktree as an unsupported **external worktree** on a WSL remote:

> ⚠ worktree: `/home/user/repos/repo/.worktrees/wt-1` looks like a worktree or submodule but cannot be resolved (external worktree or submodule)

### Root cause

A worktree created **inside a devcontainer** records a container-absolute path in its `.git` file:

```
gitdir: /workspaces/repo/.worktrees/wt-1
```

`resolve_worktree()` derived the main repo from that recorded path and only walked the local filesystem **when the derived path didn't exist**. On WSL, `/workspaces/agent-spendster` happened to **exist** as an unrelated directory, so:

- `main_repo.is_dir()` returned `True` → the local-filesystem fallback was skipped
- `target.relative_to(main_repo)` then raised `ValueError`
- → the worktree was rejected as "external"

## Fix

Locate the owning repository on the **local filesystem first** (walk up from the worktree), and trust the recorded `gitdir` path only as a fallback when no local ancestor repository is found. The recorded path can't be trusted — it may be foreign (a container path) or even coincidentally present as an unrelated directory.

## Tests

- New regression test `test_resolves_worktree_when_foreign_gitdir_path_exists_on_host` reproduces the exact WSL failure — **fails on old code, passes on new**.
- Full suite: **348 passed**; `ruff` clean.

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505R1399-R1431) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505L222-R246) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505L639-R693) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505L1084-R1125) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505L1156-R1204) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505L94)
* Both calibrate buttons are now checkable, and their checked state is used to indicate when a calibration is in progress. The table views are automatically disabled ("greyed out") during calibration, improving clarity and preventing accidental edits.

**Calibration operation and UI feedback improvements:**

* The calibrate buttons are now programmatically unchecked when calibration is cancelled, completed, or cannot start due to missing prerequisites (e.g., no device connected, no selection). This prevents the UI from getting out of sync with the actual calibration state. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505R552-R560) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505R607) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505R1275) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505R1307) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505R1318-R1322) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505R1339-R1343) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505L1316-R1361) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505L1365-R1443) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505L1173-R1214)
* Added guard logic to prevent starting a new calibration if one is already running, and to reset button state if the user attempts invalid actions (e.g., clicking without a selection or device connection). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505L639-R693) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505R717) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505R727)

**User experience enhancements:**

* Introduced `scrollToCurrentAutoCell()` to automatically select and scroll the table to the cell being calibrated during auto sweeps, making progress visible to the user. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505R1471-R1475) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe8fa8884a0b2c018fab9488704131aa702e78a8dd3c6090503497a120dd505R1543) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-204d07489af7f076f9535fcb723728853c40f4503a1d2d079bd93aa7ee5655d1R123-R128)
* Updated translation source line numbers to match code changes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ecd4aa7f75459af2133e41ac76b62a4ff954ae58bb6490d0a6ea5a144f292f45L204-R204) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ecd4aa7f75459af2133e41ac76b62a4ff954ae58bb6490d0a6ea5a144f292f45L321-R327)

**Integration with device connection events:**

* Ensured that calibration button states are updated in response to device connection and disconnection events by calling `onDeviceConnectionStateChanged()` from the main window. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c72b037f3ac7abbd3d0ee519b6f456013a9bbf5a59df16308939320c04970447R1148) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c72b037f3ac7abbd3d0ee519b6f456013a9bbf5a59df16308939320c04970447R1166)

author: gunn4r
body:
Fixes the broken mobile header (the wordmark wrapped to two lines and the links + theme toggle overflowed the bar). Below `sm` (640px) the nav now collapses into a hamburger that opens a **full-screen overlay** menu. Desktop is unchanged.

## Approach
Built on a native `<details>`/`<summary>` disclosure so the menu **works without JS** (native toggle + correct button/`aria-expanded` semantics), consistent with the site's "functional with JS off" ethos. A small inline script layers on the niceties.

## Changes
- **`Nav.astro`** — desktop keeps the inline links + toggle (`hidden sm:flex`). Mobile (`sm:hidden`) shows the hamburger; opening reveals a full-screen overlay (logo + ✕ in the bar, **Products / About / Contact** centered, **theme toggle** below). Wordmark gets `whitespace-nowrap`. Inline script adds **ESC-to-close**, **close-on-link-tap** (incl. same-page `#anchors`), **body scroll-lock**, and auto-close when the viewport grows past `sm`.
- **`backdrop-blur` → `sm:` only** — a `backdrop-filter` ancestor becomes the containing block for `position:fixed` descendants, which trapped the overlay inside the 64px header (found it via computed styles: overlay height was 64px, not full-screen). Moving the blur to `sm:` leaves the desktop frosted bar intact and frees the mobile overlay to fill the viewport.
- **`ThemeToggle.astro`** (new) — extracted the toggle button so the desktop header and mobile menu share one definition instead of duplicating three SVGs.
- **`Layout.astro`** — the theme controller now wires + syncs **every** `[data-theme-toggle]` (`querySelectorAll`), so the header and menu toggles stay in step.

## Verification (in-browser, mobile + desktop, day + night)
- ✅ Closed bar: wordmark on one line, no overflow.
- ✅ Open: full-screen opaque overlay; logo + ✕; centered links + Theme.
- ✅ Open/close via hamburger, ✕, **ESC**, **link-tap**, and viewport-grow; scroll locks while open.
- ✅ In-menu toggle cycles the theme; both toggles report the same `data-mode` (synced).
- ✅ Desktop nav visually unchanged.
- ✅ `astro check`: 0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 hints. `npm test`: 24/24.

## Note
The overlay's open/close is native `<details>`, so it still works with JS disabled (links navigate; only the JS niceties + theme toggle — which always needed JS — go quiet).

author: bennyfactor
body:
Adds **Census block** as a third option on the resolution toggle — the most granular geography LODES is built from.

**Live after deploy:** https://bennyfactor.github.io/indy-commute-flows/

## What
- Block-level LODES OD, thresholded to commuter **count ≥ 3** — which drops ~873,000 of the region's 947k OD pairs (almost all `count == 1` fuzzing noise) and keeps the **~19,800 strongest block-to-block corridors** across **~8,000 blocks**. (Block-level is the noisiest LODES geography; the threshold is deliberate, not just for size.)
- Full interaction parity: hover/click-pin, boundary outline, two-color inbound/outbound flows, top-3/top-3 partner labels, color legend — all work on the block layer.

## How
- **`R/blocks.R` + `scripts/01e-fetch-block-data.R`** (new): thresholded block flows + block centroids + simplified block polygons (2020 `GEOID20`), every flow block covered.
- **`scripts/02-build-flowmap.R`**: third `add_flowmap(indy-block)` + hit/outline layers + a `block` payload entry; refactored the per-resolution wiring into helpers; prints the HTML size.
- **`R/interaction_js.R`**: generalized the interaction from a hardcoded two resolutions to iterate `Object.keys(RES)`, plus a "Census block" radio option. bg/zcta behavior unchanged.

## Notes
- Page weight **28.2 MB** (under the 40 MB bail threshold we agreed on; block polygons dominate). A future option is a coarser block-polygon simplification to trim it.

## Verification
Headless Playwright: on the block resolution, hover populates inbound/outbound lines (0 labels), click-pin keeps lines + adds ≤6 labels, Esc clears; block group spot-checked for no regression from the 2→N refactor. Data integrity (count≥3, both-endpoints-in-region, full centroid+polygon coverage) asserted at build and re-checked at review. Final opus whole-branch review: ready to merge.

author: blokzdev
body:
Second tier of **Phase P-Rich**. Research answers are full of equations, and the model already emits LaTeX — now Arxiver renders it. This also builds the **sandboxed offline WebView foundation** that R2 (Mermaid diagrams) will reuse.

## What renders now
A math answer (inline `$…$`, display `$$…$$`, or ` ```math `) renders as real equations instead of raw LaTeX. **Emulator-verified:** a display equation `Ŝ = Σ_{k∈Q} wₖxₖ` (hat / summation / subscripts) plus inline math in a themed table and section headings, and it **still renders in airplane mode** (offline). Plain answers keep the fast native R0 renderer.

## How (the design fork)
Inline `$…$` is the hard case (a WebView is block-level; native bitmap libs like jlatexmath aren't reliably on Maven Central). So a **math-containing answer is rendered whole** through one `RichBlockWebView` (commonmark `HtmlRenderer` → HTML → **KaTeX**), which handles inline + display perfectly and is the foundation R2 layers Mermaid onto.

- **`RichBlockWebView`** — sandboxed: JS on (KaTeX only), **all network blocked** (`blockNetworkLoads`), no content/cross-file access, **no `@JavascriptInterface`**. Loads only bundled `file:///android_asset/katex/`. Talks back solely via `arxiver://cite/{n}` (→ citation) and `arxiver://height/{px}` (→ self-size) link interception — no app data crosses into the page. Themed via CSS vars (light/dark).
- **`RichHtml`** (pure, unit-tested) — `HtmlRenderer` escapes the model's markup; `[n]` → `arxiver://cite` links **skipping math spans** (so `\sqrt[3]{x}` isn't linkified); themed KaTeX template.
- **`AskBubble`** routes by `RichContent.has(answer)` once streaming settles; plain answers untouched.
- **Provider-aware system prompt** — cloud also invites LaTeX; on-device Gemma stays on plain markdown.
- **KaTeX 0.16.11** bundled as offline assets (woff2 only, ~608 KB). **No new Gradle dependency** (reuses the platform WebView + R0's commonmark).

## Verification
`./gradlew build` green (JDK 17). New tests: `RichHtmlTest` (math + citation-link-skips-math + rich-content gate). Redaction goldens green (system-prompt base unchanged; cloud addendum appended). `VERIFICATION.md` + spec updated. Next: **R2 — Mermaid diagrams + charts on this WebView**.

## 概要
PR #29 マージ後に積んだカレンダー改善をまとめた PR です（#30 の年月ジャンプも取り込み済み）。

## 変更点

## What (Slice 2 — ownership-deletion proof)
Migrate github-devloop's **G14** ratchet from repo-global Python INTO the github-devloop package as a **declarative conformance pack**. It now runs **by ownership** (whenever github-devloop is an active package), not by repo identity — removing one hardcoded `packages/github-devloop/` path from the "generic" repo-global harness (the inverted-dependency smell).

- `packages/github-devloop/fkst.toml`: `[conformance] pack = "conformance/pack.toml"`.
- `packages/github-devloop/conformance/pack.toml`: a `text_forbid_regex` rule (engine: fkst-substrate#180) forbidding `\blocal\s+function\s+parse_name_only_paths\s*\(` in the package's own `*.lua` except `core.lua` + tests — the exact G14 invariant, as DATA.
- **DELETE the Python G14** entirely (module + test + `check_repo.py` fn/import/add + runner call + config doc label). `is_own_repo` + other B-specific ratchets stay (inventory-ratchet). grep = 0 dangling. No dual enforcement.
- `.fkst/substrate-ref` → current substrate dev (has `text_forbid_regex`).

## Verified (official substrate dev engine)
- The declarative G14 rule is **ACTIVE + 0 violations** on github-devloop (faithful to Python G14).
- A temp `local function parse_name_only_paths(` file **FAILS** the rule at its line.
- `scripts/run.sh test` → exit 0 (**OK: 15 packages**; github-devloop 630 passed, 0 failed); `scripts/run.sh check` → exit 0.

(An earlier draft noted a liveness-test "blocker" — that was a **false alarm from a stale local verification binary** built from a pre-#179-revert substrate commit; official substrate dev has the codex-status contract intact, confirmed by a read-only root-cause diagnosis + green official-engine run.)

Proves the ownership-deletion half of "conformance rules travel with the package": a package-specific rule moved from repo-global hardcoded Python into the owning package's data pack.

author: jcoludar
body:
## Summary

Adds a `protspace.stats` subsystem that computes **per-projection quality statistics** at
preparation time and bakes them into the `.parquetbundle` as an optional fifth part. This is the
**engine half** of the projection-statistics MVP (tracking issue: tsenoner/protspace_web#219;
related: tsenoner/protspace#324). The `protspace_web` PR that consumes it follows separately — **this PR lands first.**

Today the pipeline (`embed → project → annotate → bundle`) ships coordinates with zero quality
metrics, so judging a projection is purely visual. This change answers two questions per projection:

- **Cluster structure** — `cluster_validity`: KMeans with a distance-to-chord **elbow** estimate of
  K, scored by **silhouette**, **Davies–Bouldin**, **Calinski–Harabasz** on the projection coords.
- **Projection faithfulness** — `faithfulness`: **kNN-overlap** and **trustworthiness / continuity**
  between the source embedding and the projection — i.e. how much the reduction distorted the
  neighbourhood structure.

## What's in this PR

- **`src/protspace/stats/`** — a generalized `Statistic` contract (each statistic declares whether it
  needs the embedding and returns one or more `StatRow`s) + a lazy `STATISTICS` registry mirroring
  the existing `REDUCERS` pattern. sklearn imports stay **function-local** to preserve CLI startup.
  - `stats/cluster/kmeans_elbow.py` — KMeans sweep `K ∈ [2, min(round(√n), 50)]`, elbow via
    perpendicular deviation from the first→last inertia chord (argmax index → K).
  - `stats/metrics/validity.py` — silhouette (seeded sample above threshold) / DB / CH at that K.
  - `stats/metrics/faithfulness.py` — kNN-overlap@k and trustworthiness/continuity vs the embedding.
  - `stats/driver.py` — `compute_statistics(...)` iterating registered statistics per projection,
    isolating per-statistic **and** per-projection failures (a bad reduction is logged and skipped,
    never sinks the report).
- **Tidy long-format output** — an 8-column table (`space_kind, space_name, stat_family, label_kind,
  metric, metric_kind, value, extra_json`). New statistics add **rows, not columns**.
- **Bundle I/O (`data/io/bundle.py`)** — an optional **fifth part** `statistics.parquet`. Layout
  `core(3) + settings? + statistics?`; when statistics is present without settings, a **zero-byte
  settings slot** keeps the fifth position unambiguous. `write_bundle` / `read_bundle` /
  `extract_bundle_to_dir` **and `replace_settings_in_bundle`** are all updated — the last so
  `protspace style` no longer silently drops a trailing stats part.
- **Wiring** — `ReductionPipeline.run` (the one stage holding embeddings **and** projections)
  computes stats behind `prepare --stats/--no-stats`; new `protspace stats -i emb.h5 -p project_dir
  -o statistics.parquet` for the discrete path; `bundle -s/--statistics` folds a stats parquet in.
- **No new dependency** — scikit-learn (KMeans, silhouette/DB/CH, `manifold.trustworthiness`) is
  already a core dep.

## Robustness hardening (post adversarial review)

This branch was put through a multi-agent review; the confirmed findings are fixed here:

- **Faithfulness no longer silently drops trustworthiness/continuity for small n.** `trustworthiness`
  requires `n_neighbors < n/2` (strict); k is now clamped to `(n-1)//2` instead of `n-2`.
- **`cluster_validity` scores the full projection; `faithfulness` scores the embedding-aligned
  subset.** Previously clustering could be scored on the id-intersection subset only.
- **High-dim metric is threaded through** (`default_metric`) so faithfulness uses the run's metric
  rather than defaulting to euclidean for PCA/MDS/PaCMAP.
- **Multi-embedding attribution** — exact id-set cover wins immediately (no ambiguous tie-break); a
  source column maps each projection to its own embedding.
- **Precomputed (n×n) similarity/distance matrices are skipped for faithfulness** (not embeddings).
- **kNN self-exclusion is tie-safe** on coincident points (filter self, not column-0 slice).
- **`n_clusters` reports the achieved distinct-cluster count** (KMeans can collapse on coincident
  points), keeping the requested K in `extra`.

## Tests

- `tests/test_stats.py`, `tests/test_stats_bundle.py`, `tests/test_stats_cli.py` — known-answer
  numeric fixtures (blob separation; faithfulness on identity vs random projections; label-permutation
  alignment), the 8-column schema, the 5-part bundle round-trip, and the `protspace style` round-trip.
- Full suite: **534 passed** locally.

## Scope (MVP) & non-goals

In: per-projection `cluster_validity` (unsupervised/elbow) + `faithfulness`, baked at prep time,
carried in the bundle. Explicitly **out** (non-breaking future expansions): embedding-space
cluster-validity, annotation-feature label sources, on-demand recompute, the broader
`ProtSpaceExtractor` pair/edge/set analyses (future typed bundle parts), and frontend rendering. The
registry + long-format table leave seams for the scalar expansions.

**Data-format change:** additive, backward compatible — existing 3- and 4-part bundles read and
write unchanged.

Refs tsenoner/protspace_web#219, tsenoner/protspace#324

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Makes replays autonomous: the server now **detects every kill from CS2 GSI**, timestamps each one against the running OBS recording, and **auto-assembles them into a montage** that operators can fine-tune (omit kills, nudge in/out) before rendering with ffmpeg. New **Highlights** page in the nav.

**Why capture is recording-based, not replay-buffer-based:** the OBS replay buffer is a single fixed window and can't save overlapping clips (rapid multi-kills would be dropped, and the existing save path even *blocks* concurrent saves). So instead the full OBS recording is the source footage and the kill feed is the edit list — this guarantees *every* kill is clippable. (An optional `autoSaveReplayOnKill` toggle still fires a buffer save per kill for instant in-broadcast replays, independent of the montage flow.)

### How it works

1. **Kill detection** (`highlightService`): diffs the observer `allplayers` block on each GSI payload. A player whose `match_stats.kills` rose ⇒ killer; players whose `deaths` rose ⇒ victim pool (paired in order — GSI has no explicit killer→victim mapping, so victim is best-effort); active weapon + `round_killhs` delta give weapon/headshot. The first payload (and any kill-count reset = new match) only seeds the baseline, so no burst of stale kills. Warmup is skipped.

2. **Recording offsets** (`obsService`): tracks `recordStartedAt` and emits `recordingStarted` / `recordingStopped` (the stop event carries the file path needed for clipping). Each kill stores `{ recordingId, recordOffsetMs }`.

3. **Auto clip plan** (pure `buildHighlightPlan` in shared, used by the UI):
```
window(kill) = [offset - preRoll, offset + postRoll]
merge windows within mergeGapMs   // a 3K becomes one clip
=> HighlightClip { killIds[], label: "niko 2K · ak47", inMs, outMs, included }
```

4. **Montage render** (`montage.ts`): one ffmpeg `filter_complex` pass — `trim`/`atrim` each selected cut from the single recording and `concat` them, re-encoding so the join is always valid (ffprobe-gated audio so silent recordings still render). Result is registered into the existing replay library via `replayService.addLocalFile(...)`, so montages are loadable into the replay-player source like any clip.

### Host requirements (surfaced in the UI, like cloudflared)
- **ffmpeg** on the host (montage render). `ffmpegAvailable` is reported in state and the Generate button is gated on it.
- **OBS recording on** during the match (so there's footage). A montage can only render once its recording is **stopped** (OBS reports the file path on stop).

### API / protocol
- `GET /api/highlights`, `PUT /api/highlights/settings`, `DELETE /api/highlights/kills/:id`, `POST /api/highlights/kills/clear`, `POST /api/highlights/montage`
- New `{ type: 'highlights'; state: HighlightState }` broadcast (kills, recordings, settings, rendering, ffmpegAvailable).

### Verification
Drove GSI payloads through the real services on the VM: a seeded baseline then a 2K (1 HS) + a later solo kill ⇒ 3 kills detected, grouped into 2 clips with correct labels/offsets; rendered a montage from a synthetic 70s recording ⇒ valid concatenated mp4 registered in the replay library. `npm run build` + `npm run lint` pass.

Couldn't test against a live OBS + real CS2 observer feed here (no OBS/CS2 on the VM) — best confirmed on your production host.

## Summary
- Extend the existing `nudge` notification subsystem with a formal kernel runtime/update check:
  - fast local refresh nudge when the running kernel version differs from the installed distribution on disk;
  - at-most-once-per-UTC-day packaged-runtime update nudge that checks the latest published LingTai kernel version;
  - editable/source/dev installs are skipped for package-update checks.
- Add a new `system-manual` nested reference, `reference/runtime-update-checks/SKILL.md`, and surface it in the top-level router/YAML so agents know how to interpret `kind: kernel_version` nudges and ask humans before updating.
- Refresh nudge/notification docs and anatomy, including the `.notification/nudge.json` channel and hidden `.notification/.nudge_state.json` throttle state.

## Safety / behavior
- The update checker is read-only: it emits a `nudge` entry and never downloads, installs, refreshes, or mutates config by itself.
- Package-index checks are throttled to once per UTC day per agent and use a short timeout.
- Editable/dev/source runtimes do not run the package-update check.
- The skill explicitly says to ask the human before any download/update and to refresh only when safe.

author: orestisfl
body:
## Proposed commit message

`TestTcpServer` in `metricbeat/helper/server/tcp` bound the test server to a hardcoded port (`2003`). When the test runs in multiple parallel processes (for example under `stresstest.sh` with `-p`), the processes race to bind `127.0.0.1:2003` and all but one fail with `bind: address already in use`, so the test is flaky regardless of whether the race detector is enabled.

This change binds the test server to port `0` so the OS assigns a free ephemeral port, then reads the actual port back from the listener after `Start()` to connect the client. While here, the test helper is simplified: the now-unused `port` parameter is dropped, the helper returns the concrete `*TcpServer` (removing a type assertion at the call site), and a misleading log line that claimed the server was listening before `Start()` was called is removed.

## What?

Stacked on #79470

Adds a package-root Sass shim for `@wordpress/theme/design-token-fallbacks` and points the package export at that stable entry point.

## Why?

The Sass fallback helper needs to work in both package-export-aware build tools and older Sass setups that resolve packages from `node_modules` with a load path. Exporting or documenting a generated `src/prebuilt` path would make package internals part of the public API.

This should unblock us to reinstall the changes that we reverted in #79429.

## How?

Adds `packages/theme/design-token-fallbacks.scss` as a public shim that forwards to the generated helper. The package export now points to that shim with Sass/style/default conditions, and the docs use the same public `@wordpress/theme/design-token-fallbacks` import for both package importer and load-path Sass setups.


## Testing Instructions

1. Run `npm run storybook:build`.
2. Confirm the build completes successfully.

author: htian-qwq
body:
…raction

Root cause: 130 of 257,434 Endfield VFS bundles (0.05%) have a matched outer VFS encryption but unmatched inner encryption. After VFS descramble
+ LZ4 decompression, the block data is garbage. This garbage flows into SerializedFile parsing where object metadata is partially valid (classID, PathID) but object body data is corrupt. When AssetsManager.ReadAssets() constructs AnimatorController from this garbage, unchecked loop counts (numElements, numNodes, trianglesCount etc.) cause massive allocations (12-15 GB per bundle). With 16 parallel threads hitting these bundles simultaneously, peak memory reaches 200+ GB → system OOM kill.

Additionally, EndianBinaryReader.ReadBytes(count) used `new List<byte>(count)` which pre-allocates count bytes — a garbage count of ~1 billion directly triggers a 14 GB allocation before any data is read.

Fix applied in multiple layers:

1. SkipProcess=true in CLI consumer (PRIMARY FIX): Set AssetsManager.SkipProcess=true so ReadAssets() is never called automatically. The CLI then manually constructs only Texture2D objects from sf.m_Objects, skipping AnimatorController and all other types entirely. This eliminates the 14 GB allocation at its source.

2. EndianBinaryReader hardening:
   - ReadBytes(count): reject if count > stream remaining length
   - ReadArray<T>(del, length): reject if length > stream remaining length
   - ReadInt32Clamped(maxCount): new method for count fields

3. Structural sanity checks in container parsers:
   - BundleFile.cs: uncompressedBlocksInfoSize ≤ 64MB
   - VFSFile.cs: header fields, block sizes, node sizes, total stream ≤ 2GB
   - VFSUtils.cs: blocksCount/nodesCount ≤ 10000
   - SerializedFile.cs: typeCount/objectCount/scriptCount/externalsCount /refTypesCount/readTypeTree childrenCount/TypeTreeBlobRead numberOfNodes /stringBufferSize — all clamped
   - Texture2DExtensions.cs: width/height ≤ 32768, pixels ≤ 1B

4. CLI runtime guardrails:
   - --per-bundle-alloc-limit-mb (default 512): post-LoadFiles alloc check
   - --mem-watch-percent: RSS watchdog with 200ms sampling
   - --trap-bundle-alloc-mb: copy offending bundles for analysis
   - Memory watchdog diagnostic: RSS/GC heap curve, recent bundle timings
   - find-bad-bundles subcommand: scan all bundles, identify bad ones
   - classify-bundles subcommand: header-only analysis, zero alloc
   - inspect-bundle subcommand: magic/entropy/hex dump analysis

5. Logging cleanup:
   - All [ALLOC-TRACE] output moved from Console.Error to Logger.Verbose
   - Removed verbose "PerFileAllocBudget wired up" per-thread spam
   - Normal runs now produce only batch progress + final summary

6. FastAPI pipeline fix:
   - Added --png-compression fast to extract command (was defaulting to "none" = no compression, producing unnecessarily large PNG files)

Verified: full 257,434 bundle extraction completes in 157s at 16 threads, 0 failed, 0 blocked, memory peak ~31GB (normal LZ4+Texture working set), 20,329 images written. No OOM, no watchdog trips.

author: mguozhen
body:
## 问题 / 背景
广告获客的注册用户里，很多**激活了（发过 API 调用）但从没充值**。我们这两天是手动发现的：翻 `/user` + `/user/topup` 两张分页表再交叉比对——慢、临时、运营无法复用。结果是 33 个候选，其中 5 个最热（重度调用 + 余额见底，已撞墙）。

## 改动
新增 `GET /api/user/recall_candidates`（admin 鉴权、只读），直接返回同一队列：
- `plg` 组（真实自助用户，排除 enterprise/admin/内部）
- 已激活：`request_count >= min_calls`
- 没成功充值过：`id NOT IN (成功 topup 的 user_id)`
- 低余额：`quota <= max_balance(USD)`
- 按 `request_count desc` 排序，最投入的先出

**Query 参数**：`min_calls`（默认 1）、`max_balance` USD（默认 1）、`limit`（默认 100，上限 1000）。

## 范围
- `model.GetRecallCandidates` — GORM 查询，成功 topup 的 `NOT IN` 子查询；`group` 列用 `commonGroupCol` 做跨库保留字转义（Rule 2）
- `controller.GetRecallCandidates` — 参数解析 + USD→quota（`common.QuotaPerUnit`）
- `router/api-router.go` — adminRoute 注册一行

## 影响 / 风险
纯**新增**，不改任何现有 symbol 行为。**只读、无状态 → 多节点安全**（Rule 11）。复用现有 `AdminAuth` 鉴权。无用户可见文案 → 无 i18n 面。

## 验证
- `go build ./...` 成功；`go vet` 无问题；`gofmt` 无改动
- 逻辑对照本地临时查询（产出 33 候选 / 5 热）一致

## 后续（不在本 PR）
前端可在 admin 用户页加一个「召回候选」视图消费此接口；或接自动化做 1:1 召回（配套 1:1 配额诱饵）。

author: davidfowl
body:
## Description

Azure Key Vault names remain reserved by location-scoped soft-delete tombstones after the live vault is deleted. When an implicit Key Vault child is created for PostgreSQL password authentication, parent reprovision needs to include that child; otherwise users can hit an ARM deleted-state conflict that requires changing the AppHost model even though the conflict is recoverable or diagnosable.

This change expands per-resource Azure target discovery to include annotation-based parent relationships so reprovision/delete/get-resource include implicit Azure children, while keeping change-location scoped to the selected resource so a parent with an implicit Key Vault child is not blocked as a Key Vault target. It also distinguishes successful Key Vault tombstone purge-and-retry from the case where Azure reports a deleted-state conflict but the deleted vault cannot be found in any attempted location, surfacing a structured diagnostic and recommended actions instead of retrying into the same provider error.

Validation:

- `dotnet test --project tests/Aspire.Hosting.Azure.Tests/Aspire.Hosting.Azure.Tests.csproj --no-launch-profile -- --filter-class "*.AzureEnvironmentResourceExtensionsTests" --filter-not-trait "quarantined=true" --filter-not-trait "outerloop=true"`
- `dotnet build tests/Aspire.Playground.Tests/Aspire.Playground.Tests.csproj /p:SkipNativeBuild=true`
- Manual Bicep playground validation for `postgres2` implicit Key Vault reprovision and `storage` role-assignment child reprovision, including dashboard checks with `playwright-cli`.

Fixes: #18403

body:
## What this does

Makes the app deployable from a clean checkout with no hardcoded personal data or infra URLs. Configuration now comes entirely from environment variables.

## Changes
- **Remove hardcoded personal data and infra URLs** — backend/frontend URLs and personal values now read from env vars.
- **Restrict CORS to an allowlist** instead of wildcard `*`, driven by a new `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` env var (declared in the Render config; omit it to keep allow-all).
- **Make `server.ts` a frontend host only** — removed dead/duplicate webhook code.
- **Fix broken image fallbacks** — replaced retired URLs with working Unsplash CDN URLs.
- **Docs** — reconciled README with reality, removed stale plan, added a job/portfolio readiness assessment.
- **gitignore** Python bytecode caches.

## ⚠️ Required after merge (the new code expects these)
Deploys will break unless env vars are set, because hardcoded fallbacks were removed:

**Render (backend):** add `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` = your frontend URL (e.g. `https://your-app.vercel.app`). Existing secrets unchanged.

**Vercel (frontend):** ensure `VITE_BACKEND_URL` (your Render URL), `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`, `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `VITE_APP_URL` are set, then **Redeploy** (Vite bakes `VITE_*` at build time).

**Telegram:** confirm the webhook points at `https://<render-url>/api/webhook`.

author: kmonsoe
body:
## Why

The curator background agent was consuming **18k–58k tokens per job** in prod. The static prompt prefix (skill markdown + tool JSON schemas) is re-sent on *every* turn of the tool loop (`runtime.ts:63`), so both the **tool-set size** and the **iteration count** compound the cost. This PR attacks both.

## Changes

### 1. Tighter per-skill tool allowlists (`packages/types/src/job-catalog.ts`)

`TOOL_PREFIXES_BY_URI` gated each curator skill by broad module prefixes (`conv_`, `kb_`, `crm_`, `outreach_`), loading 10–30 tool schemas into context every turn. Each skill now allowlists **only the exact tools its procedure calls**, verified against the skill markdown:

| Skill | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `conv/set-topic-and-title` (per-conversation, highest volume) | all `conv_*` (~30) | 5 exact |
| `kb/review-content` | `conv_`,`kb_` (~47) | 5 exact |
| `crm/clean-contact-data` | `conv_`,`crm_` (~45) | 3 exact (drops unused `conv_`) |
| `crm/extract-contact-from-message` | `conv_`,`crm_` (~45) | 4 exact |
| `outreach/draft-initial-email` | 4 prefixes (~60) | 5 exact |
| `outreach/draft-reply-email` | 4 prefixes (~60) | 5 exact |
| `cms/review-stale-entries` | `cms_` (~28) | 6 read-only |

**Behavior is unchanged** — dropped tools were either operator-review-loop tools or ones the skill never calls. A disallowed call returns a recoverable `isError` result (not a throw), and dropped tools are filtered out of `listTools()` entirely, so the model never sees them.

Bonus: `review-stale-entries` drops every mutating `cms_*` tool, so its propose-only invariant is now enforced at the runtime layer instead of by prompt instruction alone.

### 2. Lower the curator iteration cap (`packages/agent-host/src/runner.service.ts`)

Curator skill passes now stop after `CURATOR_MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS` (**16**, was a hardcoded 24). Clips worst-case per-job token spend; unfinished batch sweeps resume on the next scheduled run (dedupe keys keep them idempotent). Kept well above the conversation-side default of 8 so batch sweeps retain headroom.

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` — all 29 tasks pass (incl. `backend-core`/`agent-host` which consume `toolPrefixesFor`).
- `@getmunin/types`, `@getmunin/agent-host`, and `set-topic-job` test suites pass; updated the two tests asserting the old allowlists.
- No docs-fixture/OpenAPI regen needed — curator tool allowlists aren't part of the public MCP catalog (pre-commit `openapi:generate` produced no diff).

## Changeset

`patch` on `@getmunin/types` + `@getmunin/agent-host`.

author: johnnyffm
body:
## What

Satchel shipped **English-only**. This brings the trading UI to the **exact set of languages phoenix-pocx offers** — a 1:1 match of its `web-wallet/src/assets/locales` + `core/i18n/languages.ts` (same 26 codes, names, native names, and order).

**26 locales:** en, bg, ca, cs, de-de, el, es-es, fi, fr, gl, hi, hr, id, it, ja, lt, nl, pl, pt-br, ro, ru, sk, sr, tr, uk, zh-cn.

(Verified: language codes diff **EXACT 1:1** against phoenix-pocx's `languages.ts`.)

## Two parts

**1. The 25 translation bundles**
- Each mirrors `en.ts` key-for-key and is typed `: Bundle`, so **`tsc` enforces completeness** — a missing/stray key fails the build (unknown keys still fall back to English at runtime).
- All `{placeholder}` tokens, `\n`, and brand/technical tokens (`Satchel`, `pactd`, `Nostr`, `Corkboard`, `HTLC`, `Taproot`, `sat/vB`, `pactoffer1:`, the literal `QUIT` confirm word, URLs, coin tickers, …) preserved **verbatim**.
- Trading-domain wording per language (swap / maker-taker / timelock / refund / funding / redeem / feerate / order-book bids-asks), using each language's established crypto-community terms; Serbian in Cyrillic.
- The Turkish bundle is imported aliased (`trBundle`) so it doesn't collide with the i18n module's own `tr()` translate-mirror export.

**2. First-run usability fix**
The header's language picker sat behind the onboarding dialogs' modal backdrop, so on a fresh install you **couldn't change language until setup was finished** — forcing new users through onboarding in a language they may not read.
- Extracted the picker into a shared `LanguageMenu` (globe + native-name list), reused by the toolbar and a new first-run instance.
- A `LanguageMenu` now floats above the dialog backdrop (zIndex modal+100) during every pre-ready gate (wizard / seed / unlock / coins), mirroring how phoenix lets you set language before onboarding.

## Validation
- `tsc --noEmit` ✅ (key-for-key completeness across all 26 bundles)
- `eslint .` (i18n no-literal-string guard) ✅
- `vite build` ✅
- Placeholder token sets match `en.ts` exactly in **every** non-English bundle; `QUIT` / `Satchel` / `pactoffer1:` literals intact in all.
- Language codes **EXACT 1:1** vs phoenix-pocx `languages.ts`.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #6501

The `nvdcve-2.0-modified.json.gz` feed has been unreliable:
- At times returning 0 bytes or HTTP 401
- Currently serving a full dump of all CVEs (~200MB compressed), causing RST_STREAM errors mid-download via Cloudflare

Once the initial year-feed sync is complete, `modified` is the wrong feed for incremental daily updates. The `recent` feed (`nvdcve-2.0-recent.json.gz`, ~0.6MB) is the correct choice.

## Changes

- `NvdDataFeed.java` — added `RecentDataFeed` record returning `"recent"`
- `NvdDataFeedMetadata.java` — parse `gzSize` field from metadata
- `NvdVulnDataSourceFactory.java` — added `resolveIncrementalFeed()`: probes `nvdcve-2.0-modified.meta` before each sync; falls back to `RecentDataFeed` if the probe returns non-200 or the `gzSize` exceeds 50MB

## Behaviour

- If `modified` is healthy and small (≤50MB): used as normal — no change from current behaviour
- If `modified` is oversized or unavailable: logs a warning and uses `recent` instead
- Self-healing: automatically switches back to `modified` if NVD fixes the feed

## Test plan

- [ ] Trigger manual NVD mirror and confirm `recent` feed is selected when `modified` gzSize exceeds threshold
- [ ] Confirm mirror completes successfully with `recent` feed
- [ ] Confirm `modified` is used when gzSize is within threshold

author: luciferyang
body:
## What changes are proposed in this pull request?

`ConsistentHash.Partition.getPartitionKey()` built its hash input from the node object directly:

```java
return String.format("%s:%d", node, index);
```

`%s` resolves to `node.toString()`, so `Node.key()` was never used. This PR places virtual nodes on the ring by `node.key()`, adds a fail-fast check for a null key, and documents the `key()` contract.

`Node.key()` exists so the ring is keyed on a stable, logical id. Using `toString()` instead left `key()` as dead code, and the ring only happened to be correct because the one implementation (`ExecutorNode`) returns the same value from both methods. A future `Node` that implements only `key()` would be placed by `Object.toString()` (the identity hash), producing a different layout on every run and across JVMs — i.e. not consistent hashing at all. No user-facing change.

Fixes #12350.

## How was this patch tested?

Added two unit tests in `ConsistentHashTest`: one asserts partitions are hashed by `key()` and never `toString()`, the other that a null key is rejected. The existing cases still pass.

author: pmurillo
body:
## What

Documents four runtime constraints in the `create-html-app` skill that a skill user currently cannot infer, and fixes one code-fence language tag.

While building an HTML App from this skill, each of these came up as a real "I had to guess" moment:

- **Alpine plugins** — the skill lists `Alpine` as a global but not which plugins ship. Relying on, say, `x-collapse` when it isn't bundled fails *silently* (no-op), so the note asks authors to confirm availability first.
- **No CDN, stated explicitly** — "no dependency `<script>` tags" is already there, but its consequence isn't: CDN libraries (Mermaid, Chart.js, D3, …) won't run, so visuals must be built natively or precomputed. (Concretely: I reached for Mermaid before realizing it couldn't load.)
- **Preview** — the globals are injected by Hubble, so opening the `.html` directly in a browser renders blank. Worth saying so nobody debugs a "broken" app that's actually just outside its runtime.
- **Persistence** — no same-origin access means `localStorage`/cookies are unavailable; state should persist through the Files API instead.

Also changes the *Structuring Logic* example fence from ` ```ts ` to ` ```html ` (the snippet is HTML/JS, not TypeScript).

## Why

These are all "things you can't discover from the markup" — exactly where the skill adds the most value. Each addition is a sentence or two; no structural changes.

## Scope

Docs only — single file (`skills/create-html-app/SKILL.md`), 7 insertions / 3 deletions. No behavior changes.

author: voces
body:
## What

A struct-union (`Cat | Dog`) `if`-expression whose **arms are concrete variant values** now lowers correctly:

```vl
type Animal = Cat | Dog
function pick(c: i32): Animal {
  const cat: Cat = { meow: 1 }
  const dog: Dog = { bark: 2 }
  return if c > 1 then cat else dog   // was: invalid wasm "expected (ref $uBox), found (ref $variant)"
}
```

Previously a soundness hole (check-clean, run-broken) in **return**, **binding** (`let`/`const`/`=`), and **argument** positions.

## Why

A value-typed union `if` produces the union box `(ref $uBox)` (its blocktype), but a kind-8 variant value is a raw `(ref $variant)`. The two arm-coerce sites —

- `emitUnionIfArm` (the value-typed union `if` — return / argument joins), and
- `emitNulArmToLocal` rep 0 (a union-annotated `let`/`const`/assignment if-init),

— both called `emitUnionCoerce`, which passes a struct-typed expression straight through `emitExpr` (the raw variant ref). So the boxed blocktype saw the wrong ref type.

## Fix

A variant **return** / **argument** already boxed via `emitUnionBoxArg` (`i32.const <tag>` + `struct.new $uBox`). The if-value arms now route through that same helper, which boxes a variant ref and **defers every other arm shape** (object literal, passthrough union, scalar) to `emitUnionCoerce` unchanged — so value-union joins (`i32 | string`) and object-literal arms stay byte-identical. Two one-line call-site swaps.

## Test

New case `tests/cases/unions/union-if-value-variant.vl` — return, binding, reassignment, and argument positions; also exercises `else if` chains and the value-union (`i32 | string`) regression path.

## Gates

- `native-fixpoint.sh`: HOLDS byte-for-byte
- `deno test -A tests/cases_wasm_test.ts`: 631 passed / 0 failed
- `native-corpus-sweep.sh`: PASS=495, standing xfails CHECKFAIL=3 RUNFAIL=1, LOGDIFF=0
- `lint-self.sh`: clean

## Follow-up

An **un-annotated** function returning a struct-union if-join (`function pick(c) if c then cat else dog`, no `: Animal`) still defaults the join to an i32 blocktype — that's a separate return-*inference* gap (the inference needs to classify a tail struct-union if-value), distinct from this coerce-site fix. Left as a follow-up.

## Details

Documents the proxy provider's signed-JWT identity headers, which were previously undocumented, and explains the recommended verification pattern for upstream applications.

### Changes

- **`index.md`**
    - Add the `X-authentik-jwt` row to the user headers table and `X-authentik-meta-jwks` to the application headers table (both are sent by the outpost but were not listed).

author: jonwalstedt
body:
## Summary

## Approach and Hypothesis

The test `alert_details_right_panel_table_tab.cy.ts` was failing with a 150-second timeout on `cy.get('[data-test-subj="globalLoadingIndicator"]').should('not.exist')` in `waitForAlerts` (`tasks/alerts.ts`), called from `waitForAlertsToPopulate`. The global loading indicator (`globalLoadingIndicator`) tracks ALL in-flight HTTP requests made through Kibana's `http` service — not just the specific search strategy endpoint. The root cause was an ordering issue in `waitForAlerts`: `cy.waitForNetworkIdle('/internal/search/privateRuleRegistryAlertsSearchStrategy', 500)` was called BEFORE the `LOADING_INDICATOR` check. During the 500ms idle window for that specific endpoint, other background requests (entity analytics, data view init, histogram fetches, etc.) would fire. After `waitForNetworkIdle` resolved, those non-search requests were still in flight and kept the spinner visible for the entire 150s Cypress retry window. The fix moves `waitForNetworkIdle` to AFTER the `LOADING_INDICATOR` check, so the spinner naturally waits for ALL in-flight requests (not just the search endpoint) to complete before the assertion passes. Then `waitForNetworkIdle` confirms the search endpoint is also idle. This is the same root cause and fix as identified for the related `bulk_add_to_timeline` flaky test on a parallel fix branch.

**Changes**

- 53f83407fc29 fix(test): fix flaky alert_details_right_panel_table_tab by checking loading indicator before network idle

Fixes #270433
Fixes #270434

body:
create deep link for new team credit stops like cloud.comfy.org/cloud/subscribe?tier=standard&cycle=monthly&_gl=1*1ilhegx*_gcl_au*MjY0MTE1NzA0LjE3ODE4NTc5MTQ.*_ga*MTcxNjgzOTExOC4xNzgxODU4NTUy*_ga_C8GM67L51P*czE3ODIyODY3NTckbzEyJGcxJHQxNzgyMjg5MzgyJGo2MCRsMCRoMA.. 
## Summary

Adds a **Stripe-direct deep link for the Team plan** so the marketing pricing page (`comfy.org/cloud/pricing`) can send users straight to Stripe checkout, exactly like the personal tiers do today.

```
cloud.comfy.org/cloud/subscribe?tier=team&stop=<stopId>&cycle=<monthly|yearly>
```

This is the Stripe-direct counterpart to the pricing-table deep link (`?pricing=team`, #13001) — same initiative, separate entry point.

## What changed (cloud app only)

- **`CloudSubscriptionRedirectView`**: branches on `tier=team`, reads the slider `stop` + `cycle`, and routes to the workspace billing checkout. `tier=team` without a `stop` falls back to `/`. Personal tiers are unchanged.
- **`performTeamSubscriptionCheckout`** (new util): mirrors `performSubscriptionCheckout` (personal) but calls `POST /api/billing/subscribe` with the per-credit plan slug + `team_credit_stop_id`. A `needs_payment_method` response is a full-page redirect to the Stripe `payment_method_url`; `subscribed` / `pending_payment` land back in the app, which polls the billing op.
- **`workspaceApi.subscribe`**: additive optional `team_credit_stop_id` param.
- **`getTeamPlanSlug(cycle)`**: maps the cycle to the catalog slug (`team_per_credit_monthly` / `team_per_credit_annual`).

Routes through the **workspace billing** endpoint (not the personal `/customers` one) because the per-credit Team plan lives there, and the backend explicitly lets **any** workspace — personal included — subscribe to it, so a marketing visitor does not need a pre-existing team workspace.

## No new BE work

The contract is already on `Comfy-Org/cloud` main: `handleSubscribe` accepts `{ plan_slug: team_per_credit_*, team_credit_stop_id }`, a fresh subscribe (no active sub) returns `needs_payment_method` + `payment_method_url`, and `GET /api/billing/plans` returns `team_credit_stops`. Only a team *change* (existing sub → new stop) is unsupported, which is irrelevant for the marketing button (new subscribers).

## Out of scope

- **Website button** — emitting the slider `stop` id + the monthly/yearly toggle into the URL belongs in the website pricing page (PR #13065, Michael). This PR is the cloud-app capability the button targets.

## Merge gating

Soft-gated on the cloud team contract being **deployed to prod** (it is on cloud main). Until then the link 422s against prod; no impact on existing flows.

## Stack

Stacked on `jaewon/fe-1104-pricing-table-deep-link` (#13001). Not for `main` until that lands. **Draft** until the prod-deploy confirm.

## Tests

- `teamSubscriptionCheckoutUtil.test.ts`: slug-by-cycle, redirect to `payment_method_url`, lands in-app when no Stripe step, off-cloud no-op.
- `CloudSubscriptionRedirectView.test.ts`: team link checks out via the workspace path with the chosen stop/cycle and never the personal path; missing `stop` → home.

`pnpm typecheck`, oxlint, oxfmt green; affected unit suites green.

body:
## Summary | 概述

Fixes three Context Compiler issues:

| Issue | Description | Status |
|-------|-------------|--------|
| #247 | Context understanding drift — confirmed facts re-interpreted in long conversations | 🟢 Fixed |
| #155 | Context leakage — old turn keywords appear in new thinking | 🟢 Fixed |
| #229 | Historical re-processing — every new message re-processes ALL history (O(n²)) | 🟢 Fixed |

## Changes | 变更

### New modules in `kun/src/loop/context-compiler/`

1. **fact-anchor.ts** (517 lines): Bilingual (Chinese + English) heuristic fact anchor extraction with three-tier confidence (confirmed/tentative/overridden). Five anchor categories (decision/assumption/constraint/conclusion/preference). Statement quality scoring. Merge logic with topic similarity detection and override propagation. XML-format output for system prompt injection.

2. **turn-isolator.ts** (274 lines): Strict turn-level isolation by turnId partitioning. Turn boundary marker injection. Optional carry-forward of last tool result. `verifyTurnIsolation()` test utility. `detectContextLeakage()` defense-in-depth check.

3. **stable-prefix.ts** (336 lines): Byte-deterministic prefix compilation built on top of existing ImmutablePrefix (does NOT replace it). `factAnchorsStable()` allows anchor appending without cache invalidation. `stablePrefixFromImmutable()` bridge function. SHA-256 fingerprinting with component-level change detection.

4. **context-compiler.ts** (226 lines): Orchestrator class. `compileTurn()` produces CompiledContext with separated prefix/active/historical sets. `extractAnchorsFromTurn()` called after each completed turn.

### Modified modules

- **agent-loop.ts**: (a) Created ContextCompiler instance; (b) after each completed turn, extracts fact anchors; (c) before building ModelRequest, injects formatted anchors into system prompt when they exist

## Architecture | 架构

The ContextCompiler extends ImmutablePrefix rather than replacing it. System prompt, tools, pinned constraints, and few-shots remain managed by ImmutablePrefix. The ContextCompiler adds fact anchors and turn-level compilation as a higher layer.

## Testing | 测试

- Full kun suite: 789/791 passing (2 pre-existing failures)
- 21 tests covering: fact extraction (English/Chinese/override/tool results), merging (dedup/promotion), formatting, turn isolation, stable prefix stability, integration with agent-loop
- Typecheck: zero new errors

## Review Notes | 审核要点

This is the most impactful PR — it modifies agent-loop.ts (the core orchestrator). The changes are minimal: 15 lines added, 1 removed. The fact anchor injection only activates when anchors exist (after 2+ turns), preserving prefix cache stability for single-turn conversations.

author: teknium1
body:
## Summary
Telegram streamed replies that grow past 4096 chars no longer spawn an infinite nested-reply duplication loop.

Root cause: `edit_message`'s overflow split ran on **every** streamed edit (`finalize=False` included). Splitting moves the active message ID to a continuation, so the next accumulated-token edit re-splits the full text — looping once per token after the limit is hit.

## Changes
- `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`: gate `_edit_overflow_split` on `finalize`. Mid-stream, truncate to a single preview message via new `_truncate_stream_overflow_preview` helper (keeps editing the same ID). Fixes both the pre-flight path and the reactive `message_too_long` catch. Full content is still split-and-delivered on `finalize=True`.
- `tests/gateway/test_telegram_format.py`: flip the existing continuation-split test to `finalize=True` (splitting is now finalize-only), add two mid-stream truncation tests.

## Validation
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 7 growing oversized mid-stream edits | N continuation messages (loop) | 0 continuations, message_id stable |
| finalize=True | splits | splits, full content delivered (2 continuations) |

Targeted tests: 4 passed. E2E (real `edit_message`, mocked bot): mid-stream continuation sends = 0, ID stays put, finalize delivers full content.

## Credit
Salvaged from #50408 by @Tranquil-Flow (authorship preserved via rebase-merge). Closes #48648. Supersedes duplicate fixes #48663 (@liuhao1024, earliest submitter), #48718 (@kyssta-exe), #51266 (@RichardAtCT) — those targeted the pre-refactor path `gateway/platforms/telegram.py`, which no longer exists.

## Infographic

body:
`rankHomeWidgets` (home-priority.ts) already ranks the home surface by base priority + decayed attention signals, but its docstring — and the `WidgetHost` home-ranking comment (`WidgetHost.tsx:137`) — explicitly defer **how those signals are sourced** to the consumer ("Live attention/decay signals aren't yet attributable to a specific widget from the activity stream, so ranking runs with no signals"). This adds that missing seam.

`activity-signals.ts` maps the live `ActivityEvent` stream (from `useActivityEvents`) onto the home widget each event should boost:
- attention/blocking events (`blocked`, `blocked_auto_resolved`, `escalation`, `error`, `reminder`, `nudge`, `check-in`) → the **notifications** widget
- conversational events (`proactive-message`, `message`) → the **messages** widget
- everything else → the **agent-orchestrator activity** widget

It is pure and React-free (the `ActivityEvent` import is type-only), delegates the importance WEIGHT to `homeSignalWeight` (one notion of urgency across the surface), and stamps each signal with the event's own timestamp so `rankHomeWidgets` decays it by recency. No render-path change yet — this is the off-render mapping the WidgetHost comment says will "thread `now` in" once wiring lands. Exported from the `@elizaos/ui/widgets` barrel.

author: yuezengwu
body:
## 背景

排查一次线上事故:一张 `@l42y PLACEHOLDER` 的 ask 卡片弹给人类,skip 之后紧接着才弹出真正有内容的那张。根因是 agent 把一条 `chat ask` 当成了「可空跑、内容随后补」的普通 shell 命令并提前执行:

```
first-tree chat ask l42y "$(cat /tmp/internal-build-plan.md 2>/dev/null || echo PLACEHOLDER)"
```

文件还没写,`cat` 失败被 `2>/dev/null` 吞掉,兜底 `|| echo PLACEHOLDER` 生效,于是字面量 `PLACEHOLDER` 成了一张**真实、不可撤销、且会阻塞目标人类**的 ask 卡片正文。

服务端 `sendMessageSchema.content` 是 `z.unknown()`,对正文**零校验**,任何半成品/空正文都会落库并 fan-out。

## 改动

在服务端唯一的内容校验 choke point `validateMessageContent`(同时被 `sendMessage` 与 `preflightMessageSendIntent` 调用)加守卫:当 `content` 是字符串且为

- 空 / 纯空白,或
- 仅由占位符 sentinel 构成(`PLACEHOLDER` / `TODO` / `FIXME` / `TBD` / `XXX`,trim 后整体匹配、大小写不敏感)

时,在事务开启前抛 `BadRequestError`,永不落库、永不 fan-out。

设计取舍:
- **放服务层而非 schema**——沿用既有架构,`content: z.unknown()` 故意保持 format-agnostic,format 相关校验归服务层(对标 `validateFileContent`)。所有客户端(CLI / web / SDK)统一受约束。
- **校验原始正文(mention 注入前)**——事故里发出的原始 content 是 `PLACEHOLDER`,经 mention 注入才成 `@l42y PLACEHOLDER`;只有在注入前校验才能命中 sentinel。
- **占位符按整体匹配**——正文里只是「提到」这些词不受影响(有测试覆盖)。

## 行为变更(需 reviewer 注意)

空正文不再被 mention normalization 救成一句光秃秃的 `@name`,而是 fail-closed 直接拒收。这正是事故那一类:`chat ask`/`send` 总带目标 mention,所以 `$(cat 缺失文件)` 的空 body 原本会 fan-out 一张无正文的 `@name` 卡。更新了唯一一个编码旧宽松行为的 normalization 测试。

## 测试

- 新增 `message-empty-body-validation.test.ts`:覆盖 text / request 两种 format 下的空、纯空白、纯换行、占位符正文;并断言「正文只是提到 PLACEHOLDER」仍放行。
- 全套 server 测试 **1567 passed**;`pnpm typecheck`、`biome check` 均过。

## 关联

源于对该事故的排查(本地 session 事件日志)。这是事故修复方案中的 **B1(服务端拒收空白/占位正文)**。可选后续:CLI `send.ts` 的空检查改为 trim 对齐 `create.ts`;以及为 ask/send 增加 `--dry-run` 预览。

author: chocobar
body:
## Problem

Adding Anthropic as a provider via the UI fails with:

```
upstream models endpoint unreachable: failed to get models from
'https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models' provider: 401 Unauthorized -
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"Invalid bearer token"}}
```

Zed agents using that provider also fail to authenticate. "Invalid bearer token" is the tell: Anthropic only emits that when an `Authorization: Bearer` header reaches it. API keys must go in `x-api-key`.

## Root cause

`RetryableClient.ListModels` dispatches to `listAnthropicModels` (which sends `x-api-key`) only when `c.isAnthropic` is true; otherwise it falls through to `listOpenAIModels` (which sends `Authorization: Bearer`).

The env/config provider path sets the flag (`SetIsAnthropic(true)`), but `initializeClient` — the DB/UI-configured provider path — never did. This regressed in commit `c6f57128f` which removed the `isAnthropicProvider(c.baseURL)` base-URL fallback from the dispatch, leaving the DB path with no way to be detected as Anthropic.

## Fix

Set `isAnthropic` in `initializeClient` for endpoints that target Anthropic (name `anthropic`, matching the UI's canonical name, or an `api.anthropic.com` base URL). Vertex endpoints are excluded since they authenticate via OAuth, not `x-api-key`.

## Test

`anthropic_models_regression_test.go` captures the auth header via httptest: without the flag the client sends `Authorization: Bearer` (the bug); with it, `x-api-key` (the fix).

NOT yet tested end-to-end against a live stack — needs `./stack rebuild api` then re-adding the provider in the UI.

Yentl flagged a wave of /de traffic from a t3n newsletter and asked if we can track it. We **were** capturing the UTMs but dropping two Mailchimp-specific URL params:

| Param | Meaning | Status before |
|---|---|---|
| \`mc_cid\` | Mailchimp campaign ID (canonical newsletter identifier) | ❌ dropped |
| \`mc_eid\` | Per-recipient email ID — **identifies WHICH subscriber** from a newsletter | ❌ dropped — biggest miss |

Per Yentl's call (pixel-only, no server-side storage), three minimal client-side changes per file:

1. **ATTRIBUTION URL_KEYS** extended to include \`mc_cid\`, \`mc_eid\`. Captured at page load, persisted to localStorage so multi-session journeys attribute correctly.
2. **\`audit_completed\` track() call** passes mc_cid + mc_eid as params. Flows to gtag (GA4 custom event params), fbq custom_data, and lintrk once LinkedIn IDs are configured.
3. **\`lead_captured\` track() call** same — newsletter-converting leads retain recipient ID in Meta CAPI Lead events for audience filtering.

## Verified in preview against the exact production URL

\`/de?utm_source=t3n+Newsletter&utm_campaign=73a0778204-RSS_EMAIL_MARKETING&utm_medium=email&utm_term=...&mc_cid=73a0778204&mc_eid=cc15c85360\`

\`\`\`
ATTRIBUTION.mc_cid = "73a0778204"
ATTRIBUTION.mc_eid = "cc15c85360"

gtag('event', 'audit_completed', { ..., mc_cid: "73a0778204", mc_eid: "cc15c85360" })
fbq('track', 'CompleteRegistration', { ..., mc_cid: "73a0778204", mc_eid: "cc15c85360" })
\`\`\`

## How to filter in GA4 (once events accumulate)

Reports → Engagement → Events → \`audit_completed\` → secondary dimension → "Event parameter: mc_eid" → unique recipient count

- Client-only changes, no API/server touched
- EN ↔ DE mirrored byte-for-byte
- i18n-check green

author: makszhukov
body:
### What does it do?

In the Content Manager layout, when a user has no authorised models for the
active locale, the redirect target is changed from `/403` to
`/content-manager/403`.

```diff
- return <Navigate to="/403" />;
+ return <Navigate to="/content-manager/403" />;
```

A regression test is added that mocks `useContentManagerInitData` to simulate
a user with no authorised models and asserts that the layout renders the
Content Manager `NoPermissions` route (`/content-manager/403`) rather than the
admin catch-all.

### Why is it needed?

When an admin user's role is restricted to specific i18n locales, switching to
a locale the role can't access left the user on a generic **"Page not found"**
screen instead of a permissions message.

The cause is purely front-end routing: the `NoPermissions` page is registered
at `/content-manager/403` (see `packages/core/content-manager/admin/src/router.tsx`),
but the layout redirected to `/403`, which resolves to `/admin/403` — a path
with no registered route — so the admin catch-all (`path: '*'`) rendered the
global `NotFoundPage`.

The condition guarding the redirect already references `'/content-manager/403'`
(`pathname !== '/content-manager/403'`), so redirecting to that same path is the
consistent, minimal fix. Server-side RBAC (returning `403` for the unauthorized
locale) is correct and untouched.

### How to test it?

1. Enable i18n and create two locales, e.g. **en** (default) and **fr**.
2. Create a localized collection type (e.g. `Article`) with `draftAndPublish`
   and an entry that has both `en` and `fr` localizations.
3. In **Settings → Roles**, create a role whose Content Manager permissions on
   `Article` are scoped to **English** only (the "Locales" property).
4. Create a user with that role and log in as them.
5. Open the entry and switch to the **French** locale, e.g.
   `/admin/content-manager/collection-types/api::article.article/<documentId>?plugins[i18n][locale]=fr`

**Before:** the app navigates to `/admin/403` and shows "Page not found".
**After:** the user is shown the **NoPermissions** ("You don't have the
permissions to access that content") page.

Automated: `yarn test:front packages/core/content-manager/admin/src/tests/layout.test.tsx`

### Related issue(s)/PR(s)

Closes #26707

author: arajkumar
body:
Chunks live in `_timescaledb_internal`, so `FOR TABLES IN SCHEMA` publications miss them and replication silently skips chunk data.

Backfill chunk membership by reading the schema set straight from the CREATE/ALTER PUBLICATION parse tree: CREATE is reconciled in the `ddl_command_end` event trigger (new WHEN TAG entry), ALTER in `process_ddl_command_start` after prev_ProcessUtility. SET rebuilds the full new schema set since PG drops every tracked chunk row on SET; DROP removes them; options-only ALTER is a no-op.

ALTER TABLE ... SET SCHEMA on a hypertable reconciles its chunks (remove from old schema's publications, add to new) before `ts_hypertable_set_schema` flips the catalog.

Chunks already covered natively via their own schema (`associated_schema_name`) get no redundant explicit `pg_publication_rel` row, which would survive a later DROP and orphan. The mirror case is handled too: dropping the chunk-home schema while the hypertable's schema stays published adds explicit rows so chunks stay published. OSM (foreign-table) chunks are skipped throughout.

author: johnrtipton
body:
## ADR-022 Iter 3 Phase 3.1 — mount state-restore + signed-snapshot restore/emit + on_mount hooks (#1913)

Second PR of the WS mount convergence (after Phase 3.0's cheap grows, #1911). Ports the transport-agnostic mount STATE-RESTORE + on-mount hooks the WS `handle_mount` has into `ViewRuntime.dispatch_mount` — the SSE mount path since Iter 1 (#1887) — so the runtime restores + emits signed snapshots identically. **LIVE for SSE mount** (parity, gated `enable_state_snapshot` opt-in); **WS still uses `handle_mount` (untouched until Phase 3.3b).**

### What landed (each WS file:line → runtime)

| Port | WS source | Runtime |
|------|-----------|---------|
| `run_on_mount_hooks` (redirect → `navigate` + abort) | `websocket.py:2383-2401` | after `_check_auth`, before `mount()` |
| Session-saved-state restore (#1466) | `websocket.py:2424-2474` | gated, before `mount()`; sets `_mounted_from_restore` |
| Signed `state_snapshot` HMAC restore (SECURITY-BOUNDARY) | `websocket.py:2491-2587` | VERBATIM caps; sets `_mounted_from_restore` |
| `state_snapshot_signed` EMIT | `websocket.py:2754-2792` | onto the mount frame, opt-in only |

- `_django_session_key` is now stamped on the view from `request.session` on the runtime path so the HMAC `sid` binding validates/emits the SAME session binding WS does.
- `_mounted_from_restore` is a new framework attr initialized in `LiveView.__init__` BEFORE the `_framework_attrs` snapshot (#1393) — reset on reconnect, never persisted. It activates the Phase-3.0 `has_prerendered → skip_html_for_resume` resume optimization.

### Security boundary — byte-identical caps

The signed-snapshot restore is the security boundary (CWE-345 → CWE-915). The HMAC binding (`unsign_snapshot` slug/sid/TTL) + size (64 KB) / keyset (256) / dict-type caps + `DJUST_STATE_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED` master-switch + `_should_restore_snapshot` veto are ported VERBATIM. A snapshot signed for view A / session S1 / older than `DJUST_STATE_SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE` does NOT restore.

### Doc-claim-verbatim HMAC-caps TDD (#1046) + gate-off (#1468)

`python/djust/tests/test_runtime_mount_state_restore_1913.py` (18 cases) drives `dispatch_mount` against a real Django request + DB session. Each cap (forged-unsigned, cross-view slug, cross-session sid, expired TTL, tampered, oversized, over-keyset, `_should_restore_snapshot` veto, opt-in #1552) asserts the snapshot does NOT restore + has a gate-off sibling. Gate-off verified: skipping the slug check in `unsign_snapshot` → cross-view restore wrongly succeeds (RED); gating the runtime restore/emit/hook-redirect off → corresponding tests RED.

### Hard constraints honored

- `websocket.py` has **no diff** — `RUNTIME_OWNED_VERBS` / WS routing / `handle_mount` / `handle_mount_batch` UNTOUCHED.
- Anti-drift pins updated: `state_snapshot_signed` removed from `_WS_ONLY_MARKERS` (now on runtime); `live_view.py` setattr-whitelist line numbers shifted +11.
- Existing nets green: `test_state_snapshot_signing.py`, `test_ws_reconnect_state_1465.py`, `test_sse_runtime_convergence_1887.py`.

### Verification

Full CI-way suite: `tests/ python/tests/ python/djust/tests/ -n auto` → **8530 passed, 21 skipped, 0 failed**.
