Issue 13 — draggable divider between the two file panels + collapse/restore the right panel. Spec: `.scratch/diptychon-mvp/issues/13-panel-resize-and-toggle.md`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Draggable divider resizes the panels; ratio retained for the session (HSplitView).
- [x] Toolbar button (split-view icon) hides/restores the right panel; left fills when hidden.
- [x] Keyboard shortcut also toggles it (⌥⌘S).
- [x] With the right panel hidden, active-panel + keyboard stay coherent (active forced left; ⌥⌘→ no-op; Tab re-opens + focuses the right panel).
- [x] Restoring preserves the right panel's directory + selection (PanelModel kept alive).

## How it works
- `HSplitView` for the two panels (min 240 each). Collapsing **swaps the whole container** (HSplitView ↔ left-only) — HSplitView can't drop a conditional child.
- `WorkspaceModel.rightPanelVisible` — registered default true, UserDefaults-persisted; toolbar `rectangle.split.2x1` + ⌥⌘S.
- Coherence: hide forces `active = .left`; mouse half-detection forces left; ⌥⌘→ no-ops; Tab re-opens.

## Gotchas (documented for next time)
- HSplitView won't remove a conditional child → swap the container.
- `object(forKey:) as? Bool` doesn't read launch args / give a true default → `UserDefaults.register` + `bool(forKey:)`.

27 green (22 unit + 5 UI). New `testToggleRightPanel` (hide → 1 table, restore → 2, keeps directory). Verified on-screen (collapsed = left fills window).

## Summary

- New `shopify-mcp/` directory: a standalone TypeScript MCP server built on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`
- Connects to any Shopify store via `SHOPIFY_STORE_DOMAIN` + `SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN` env vars — designed for a brand new unused store
- Full theme editing: list/get/create/duplicate/publish/delete themes; read/write/delete/copy individual theme files (Liquid, CSS, JS, JSON)
- Standard store management: products, collections, orders CRUD
- Raw `graphql_query` / `graphql_mutation` escape hatches for anything not covered by dedicated tools

## Theme tools

| Tool | What it does |
|------|-------------|
| `list_themes` | List all themes and their roles (MAIN / UNPUBLISHED / DEVELOPMENT) |
| `get_theme` | Inspect a single theme |
| `list_theme_files` | List every file; filter by prefix (`sections/`, `assets/`, etc.) |
| `read_theme_file` | Read a Liquid / CSS / JS / JSON file |
| `write_theme_file` | Create or overwrite a theme file |
| `delete_theme_file` | Delete one or more theme files |
| `copy_theme_files` | Copy files between themes |
| `create_theme` | Create from a public ZIP URL |
| `duplicate_theme` | Clone an existing theme |
| `publish_theme` | Set as live MAIN theme |
| `update_theme` | Rename a theme |
| `delete_theme` | Permanently delete |

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm install && npm run build` compiles cleanly (verified ✅)
- [ ] Add a new Shopify Custom App with `read_themes`/`write_themes` scopes, copy the access token
- [ ] Add MCP config to Claude Desktop or `.mcp.json` as documented in README
- [ ] Run `list_themes` → verify themes return
- [ ] Run `read_theme_file` on `layout/theme.liquid` → verify source
- [ ] Run `write_theme_file` on a DEVELOPMENT theme → verify change appears in Shopify admin
- [ ] Run `publish_theme` on a test theme → verify MAIN role changes

author: qwasg
body:
## 概述

G2.2 DXIL 第二后端 A 路"打通"可行性诊断 **round-5**（纯取证，不裁 A/B，不裁是否 bump D-205，不落实现）。
补 round-4 跳过的**诊断 3**：测「换更新 LLVM 能否让 A 打通」。栈式 PR，base 指向 #87（round-4）。

## 做了什么

隔离目录 `H:\llvm-upstream-test` 自编更新 `llvm-project` 最新 main：
- commit `82c5bce5233f964da4f8086b2341067314d841d7`，LLVM **23.0.0git**，2026-06-24
- 距 D-205 pin `a255c1ed` / 22.1.7 约 6 个月跨度（含期间全部 DirectX 后端修复）
- 经 `RURIX_LLC` 临时用；**未动** D-205 pin / **未覆盖** `H:\llvm-dxil` round-3 基线 / **未改** toolchain.rs / src/

对更新 llc 重跑 round-4 两诊断（同口径，每配置 ×12）。

## 同口径对照（round-4 pin vs round-5 更新）

| 轴 | round-4（22.1.7/a255c1ed） | round-5（23.0.0git/82c5bce5） | 判定 |
|---|---|---|---|
| asm 文本 DXIL emit | 96/96 稳定 | 96/96 稳定 | 稳定（不变） |
| obj DXContainer 写出器 | 全配置非确定崩溃 0xC0000005 | 全配置非确定崩溃 0xC0000005 | **still-broken** |
| IDxcValidator 接受 llc | reject 0x80aa0009（metadata） | reject 0x80aa0009（metadata） | **still-broken** |
| 容器（STAT/顺序/签名） | 缺 STAT + 顺序异 + 未签名 | 同 | **still-broken** |
| DXIL 版本子轴 | （未测） | llc DXIL 1.0 == dxc 1.8 DXIL 1.0 | 无版本 gap（排除 partial） |

## 结论（产证据，不下裁决）

- **两轴皆 still-broken**：bump 到最新上游 main 仍打不通 A → **fundamental（上游 DirectX 后端未成熟），非陈旧 pin 问题**。
- **DXIL 版本子轴排除 partial**：llc 与 dxc 1.8 均 DXIL 1.0/SM 6.0，拒绝是元数据编码不合规、非 validator 版本太旧。
- owner 选项收敛为：等上游成熟 / 贡献上游 / B 桥接（**AI 不裁 A/B，亦不裁是否 bump D-205**，硬规则 1）。

## 声明

- **A 打通结论**：最新上游仍 still-broken（fundamental）→ 是否 bump D-205 pin **仍 owner 裁**（真 bump=owner 决策+独立 errata，不在本 spike）。
- **D-131 仍 C**（不回填 RFC-0003 §9 / 13 §D-131）。
- **G-G2-2 未签、G2.2 验收门仍 open**（A 打通=工具链可行性 ≠ Rurix MIR→DXIL 实现 ≠ device 真跑 golden）。

## 自验全门（真跑）

- `check_schemas` PASS
- `trace_matrix` PASS（156/156，零新 RXS）
- `budget_eval` PASS（69 pass，0 skip）
- `check_guardrails` PASS（vs origin/main 9 路径；vs #87 base 5 路径）
- `check_contribution` PASS
- LF 逐文件 CR=0 + 尾 0a；round-1~4 既有 evidence 全部 byte-unchanged（blob SAME）
- 已知环境红：pr-smoke engine_integration_smoke 缺 MSVC/CUDA（自 #78 非回归），如实标注。

纯取证：探针扩展隔离于 `spike/`，自编 LLVM 产物不入库（commit 写进证据 JSON）。

author: a-ghorbani
body:
## Summary

Adds MTP / speculative-decoding draft-model support, consuming the published **llama.rn@0.12.5** — the release that synced llama.cpp to b9769 and shipped the MTP / speculative draft-model work from llama.rn PR #355 — as a normal **prebuilt** registry dependency (standard `0.12.4 → 0.12.5` upgrade). No from-source build, no vendored tarball.

Two modes, both supported:
- **Embedded / hybrid MTP** — a self-contained model carries draft layers; `model_draft` left unset, speculative just enabled (MTP defaults: `flash_attn_type 'auto'`, draft cache `q8_0`).
- **Separate-draft pairing** — a target + a distinct small draft model loaded together; `model_draft` = the draft file path (paired defaults: `flash_attn_type 'off'`, draft cache `f16`, draft GPU layers 99).

Mode is **derived** from whether a paired draft resolves to a downloaded file — no persisted mode enum. All mode defaults are applied as `?? user-value` fallbacks, so an explicit user setting is never overwritten.

## What changed

- **llama.rn upgrade (prebuilt)**: bumped `0.12.4 → 0.12.5` in `package.json` / `yarn.lock` / `ios/Podfile.lock`. The published release ships the prebuilt assets (iOS `rnllama.xcframework`, Android jniLibs for arm64-v8a + x86_64), so the net native diff vs `main` is exactly those three dependency-lock files — a plain upgrade. No committed source tarball, no `rnllamaBuildFromSource`/`RNLLAMA_BUILD_FROM_SOURCE` flag, no Podfile header-path injection, no `post_install` `project.pbxproj` mutation, and no OpenCL ICD stub. The four native config files (`ios/Podfile`, `ios/PocketPal.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`, `android/gradle.properties`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`) are byte-identical to `main`; `pod install` leaves the tree clean.
- **Persistence**: `ContextInitParams` gains `speculativeEnabled`, `selectedDraftModelId`, and `spec_draft_*`; `CURRENT_CONTEXT_INIT_PARAMS_VERSION` is `2.3` with the feature defaulting OFF for upgraded records (no behaviour change for existing users). `selectedDraftModelId` is optional, so it needs no migration step or version bump.
- **Draft parse path**: a cross-repo `draft.{hf_repo,hf_filename}` block in the device rules, parsed with the **same** path-segment security guard as model/mmproj (rejects path separators and `.`/`..` traversal; GGUF-only; huggingface.co host). A malformed draft block drops only the draft, keeping the target.
- **ModelStore**: read-only `resolveDraftConfig` (pre-mutex) with a two-channel precedence — a per-target device-rules-authored draft wins, the global user-picked draft is the fallback; two-mode `initLlama` params; `activeDraftModelId` single-writer with all release resets mirroring the projection-model pairing; best-effort draft auto-download honouring the same precedence (a draft download failure never fails the target download). The pre-load memory check now sums the target, projection, **and the paired draft's own weights and KV cache** (sized by the target `n_ctx` and the draft cache type).
- **Settings**: a speculative master toggle, a **global draft-model picker** (downloaded non-projection models + a "None" entry), a **draft GPU-layers control**, and draft cache-type menus. The draft cache-type label shows the **effective** resolved default (f16 paired / q8_0 embedded); the cache menus are enabled when a separate draft is paired and disabled with an explanation for embedded MTP, matching the runtime contract.

## Verification

- Lint (0 errors), typecheck, and the full Jest suite (247 suites, 3780 passed / 2 skipped) all green.
- `pod install` leaves the working tree clean (no generated `project.pbxproj` mutation); the committed checkout builds as-is.
- iOS Release build: PASS (prebuilt `rnllama.xcframework`; AppIntents wrapper compiles).
- Android `assembleProdRelease`: PASS — the APK packages **both** arm64-v8a and x86_64 from the prebuilt jniLibs (no from-source ABI risk).

## Open items / follow-ups

- **Device verification owed** (physical iOS + Android, may run after this draft):
  - speculative no-op gate: a non-MTP model with speculative enabled and no draft loads with **no native error** and produces output (the only proof of the speculative no-op assumption), on iOS and Android.
  - visual captures: no-op load, paired-draft-active, paired-draft-missing, and the Settings advanced speculative section.

author: yvdriel
body:
Session 4 of the video runbook. Closes the meeting loop: a coach curates a reel of an athlete's clips onto a parent-meeting feedback form, plays it in order during the meeting, and the reel surfaces on the read-only portal once the form is completed.

## What's here

**Coach side.** An attach/reorder panel on the feedback detail page. Pick a ready clip, give it a caption, move it up or down, detach it. Reorder writes `sortOrder` atomically through `db.batch`. The panel is editable only *before* the meeting; once you start the in-person edit, and after the form is completed, the reel is play-only. That rule lives in a small tested predicate, `isReelEditable(status, editing)`.

**Playback.** No permanent or public Stream URL anywhere. Tokens are signed server-side per request (1h) and passed to a pure player component that the coach page and the portal both reuse. Non-ready clips render a placeholder instead of a broken frame.

**Portal exposure.** A completed form's reel shows in the portal's feedback tab. Rather than add a second consent check, it rides the existing `isPortalBlocked` gate, so an under-16 without recorded parental consent sees no reel (their whole portal is already blocked). Decision taken with the user on 2026-06-24; 16+ reels show without a separate gate.

No migration. `feedback_clips` and the `clips.visibility` enum landed back in Session 1.

## Out of scope

Athlete-side single-clip upload during prep is deferred. It needs a public, prepare-token-gated upload path (the coach upload is session-gated), which doesn't exist yet — that's a follow-up session.

## Verification

`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build` all clean. Test suite: 108 pass, including the new reel-order/gate cases. Full playback end-to-end (real phone clip → reel → portal) needs live Cloudflare Stream and a ready clip, so that part is a manual prod check.

author: 0bu
body:
## What

Adds six read-only charge-telemetry sensors to the Home Assistant MQTT bridge, pulled from the `charge_state` poll that already runs:

| Entity | Unit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Charging current (actual) | A | delivered right now |
| Charging current (requested) | A | what the car asked for — `actual < requested` ⇒ externally throttled |
| Charger phases | — | 1 / 2 / 3 |
| Energy added | kWh | this charge session (`total_increasing`) |
| Time to full | min | `duration` |
| Charge limit reason | — | None / EVSE / BattTempLow / HighSoc / Cabin (diagnostic) |

## Why

These fields are already decoded for free in the same `CarServer_ChargeState` the bridge parses for SOC / power / amps, so surfacing them adds **no extra BLE round-trip** and negligible heap. They give Home Assistant a fuller picture of a charge session — e.g. detecting externally-limited charging via actual-vs-requested current, or session energy and time-to-full for dashboards.

## Scope / safety

- **HA/MQTT bridge only.** The `/api …/vehicle_data` evcc path and the `/status` web UI are untouched — `http_server.cpp` is not modified, so evcc behaviour is bit-identical.
- Each field is **presence-gated** (proto3 optional): emitted only when the car reported it, so an unseen value reads "unknown" in HA rather than a phantom 0.
- Currents/energy/time are published in native units (A / kWh / min) — no imperial conversion needed.

## Verification

- `idf.py build` (esp32s3) green — binary `0x17cdd0` (~1.56 MB), 50% of the app partition free.

## What Is Being Fixed

The import-processes list endpoints identified their scope group by internal numeric ID (`siteId` / `assetLibraryId`). Internal IDs are neither stable nor portable identifiers, and this is inconsistent with the external reference code (ERC) pattern used across the headless APIs.

body:
- Bugfix for phase-2 of GPU offloading of image pre-processing
 - Resolved execution failure in resample_pil_ref

### Description
Optimization of GPU offloading of image pre-processing caused execution failure. It is caused by assertion in resample kernel selection.

### Detail
Pillow's CPU resample copies the input straight to the output when neither axis needs
 resampling (input size == output size on both axes). The staged GPU pipeline derives the 
 number of passes from NeedHorizontalPass/NeedVerticalPass, so a true identity would emit
 zero passes: the output is left unwritten and the primitive is built with zero kernels,
 which crashes at execution. Force a single horizontal pass for the identity case; it runs
 with scale==1 (identity) coefficients and copies the input to the output.


### Tickets:
 - CVS-188909

author: sradco
body:
## Summary
- Fix e2e-management-api CI test failures by addressing four issues discovered during CI debugging:
  1. **Wrong cluster**: Server used `rest.InClusterConfig()` which connected to the build cluster instead of the provisioned test cluster. Introduce `loadKubeConfig()` that prefers KUBECONFIG when set.
  2. **Dead informers**: The k8s client was created with a 30-second timeout context. When `createHTTPServer` returned, `defer initCancel()` cancelled the context and stopped all informers — freezing the relabeled-rules cache permanently. Pass the server-lifetime context to `NewClient` instead.
  3. **Missing auth token**: The e2e framework only read `config.BearerToken`, which is empty when the CI kubeconfig uses client-certificate auth. Add `resolveToken()` that falls back to creating a ServiceAccount token via the TokenRequest API.
  4. **Spec-equivalence conflicts**: All test rules used `vector(1)`, triggering 409 conflicts across tests. Give each rule a unique PromQL expression.

## Root Cause
The CI step `monitoring-plugin-tests-management-api` runs on the build cluster (build01) with KUBECONFIG pointing to the provisioned test cluster. Multiple issues prevented the e2e tests from working:
- The server used `rest.InClusterConfig()` connecting to the wrong cluster
- Informers were killed after init due to a cancelled timeout context
- No bearer token was available for HTTP requests (client-cert kubeconfig)
- Shared PromQL expressions caused duplicate-spec rejections

## Test plan
- [x] `go build ./...` passes
- [x] `go test ./pkg/... ./internal/...` passes
- [x] `go vet ./...` passes
- [ ] CI e2e-management-api test passes

author: op-bot-common
body:
Permission-sensitive cache types (`user`, `orgUser`, `profileUser`) gate admin / role / membership decisions. The L1 memCache is per-process, so an `invalidate()` only drops the entry on the instance that ran it — every other instance keeps serving the stale value for up to the L1 TTL (~2 min). That window is a privilege-escalation hole: a user who loses admin on instance A still looks like an admin to instance B until B's local TTL expires.

This change moves the decision into the cache module itself. A `PERMISSION_SENSITIVE_TYPES` set forces `cache()` and `invalidate()` to skip the L1 for those three types, so every read goes to Redis where `invalidate()` writes a 1-second tombstone that all instances see immediately. Callers that already pass `skipMemCache: true` (e.g. `getOrgAccessUser`) are unchanged; this is the safety net for callers that forget.

Out of scope for this PR — the second half of the audit's recommendation, wiring `invalidate()` for `profile` / `organization` into Supabase realtime so each process can drop its local L1 entry on broadcast, requires server-side channel subscription that doesn't exist yet. Tracked separately.

Source: ONE-40 audit, finding #20.

author: jamie8johnson
body:
## MCP Phase 2b — `cqs_index` fire-and-forget (+ view.rs NUL fix)

Completes the user-blessed Phase 2 scope (notes-writes from 2a + index here), on top of the 2a mutation channel and gating.

**Fire-and-forget, never a Store write.** `dispatch_index` calls `request_reconcile()` (the same `SharedReconcileSignal` primitive as `dispatch_reconcile`) and returns immediately with `{status:"queued", queued:true, reindex_deferred:true}`; the watch loop performs the actual rebuild. The daemon's `Store<ReadOnly>` typestate invariant (from 2a) is preserved — no writable Store in the handler (asserted by `index_keeps_store_read_only`).

**`--force` withheld by absence.** New scoped `IndexArgs` JsonSchema core exposes only optional `slot` — there is no `force` field, so `index --force` / model-swap / improve-docs are unreachable over the wire regardless of the flag (pinned by `index_force_is_unreachable_as_a_tool`: exactly one index tool, schema has no `force` property). `slot` is honestly documented as advisory on the single-slot daemon path.

**Same gate as 2a** — `CQS_MCP_ENABLE_MUTATIONS` at both layers (`require_mutations_enabled` runs first in the `"index"` arm; fail-closed, tested). Annotation `idempotentHint:true`, `destructiveHint:false`. Flag-on `tools/list` = 23 (19 read + 3 notes + index); client polls completion via the existing `cqs_wait_fresh`/`cqs_status` read tools.

**Folded fix:** `src/cli/batch/view.rs:194` had a raw NUL byte in a comment (made `file` report "data" + plain grep treat it as binary) — replaced with `\0`. Verified the file is now NUL-free.

**Tests:** full `--tests` sweep 4815/0; index queues promptly (<500ms, signal flip) / rejected flag-off / Store-read-only invariant / force-key-ignored. clippy/fmt/provenance clean.

(Pre-existing flake noted separately: a CWD-race in `dispatch_review_unrelated_delta_no_marker` — not from this diff.)

author: jurei733
body:
## Überblick

Dieser PR adressiert Issue #688, ohne das Issue automatisch zu schließen. Ziel ist ein robusterer Korrektheitsfix für den Kodierstand nach Änderungen an `.vocs`-Dateien plus ein belegter Performance-Umbau für die Freshness-Ermittlung über Unit-Dateien.

## Änderungen

- Nach erfolgreichem `.vocs`-Speichern wird direkt die Aktion „Kodierstand prüfen“ angeboten und mit `refreshCodingFreshness=1` geöffnet.
- Erfolgreiche `.vocs`-Uploads im Testdateien-Dialog bieten dieselbe Prüfung auch ohne Warnung an.
- Die Job-Definition-Liste berechnet Planned-Usage-Daten nur noch bei explizitem Opt-in.
- Unit-Dateien speichern `codingSchemeRef`-Metadaten in `structured_data`; bestehende Produktivdaten werden per Liquibase-Backfill ergänzt.
- `file_upload` erhält zusätzlich indexierbare Lookup-Spalten `file_id_normalized` und `coding_scheme_ref_normalized`. Uploads und Testcenter-Importe füllen diese Werte direkt.
- Unit-Dateien ohne `CodingSchemeRef` werden explizit mit `__NO_CODING_SCHEME_REF__` markiert. Dadurch bedeutet `NULL` in `coding_scheme_ref_normalized` nur noch echter Legacy-/unverarbeiteter Zustand und triggert nicht dauerhaft den Regex-Fallback.
- `getUnitIdsByCodingSchemeRefs` filtert zuerst über `coding_scheme_ref_normalized`, bildet daraus konkrete Unit-Refs und nutzt dann kandidatengesteuerte `CROSS JOIN LATERAL`-Index-Probes auf normalisierte Unit-Namen/Aliase. Die alte materialisierte All-Units-CTE ist entfernt.
- XML-Regex läuft nur noch als getrennter Legacy-Fallback, wenn es überhaupt unnormalisierte Unit-Dateien gibt; auch dieser Fallback nutzt danach kandidatengesteuerte Unit-Probes.
- Der Lookup-Backfill setzt zuerst Werte aus `structured_data`, führt Regex nur noch für danach weiterhin unbekannte Unit-Dateien aus und markiert anschließend bekannte Unit-Dateien ohne Ref mit dem No-Ref-Sentinel.

## Validierung

- Regressionstest: `.vocs`-Overwrite mit Coding-Scheme-Änderung markiert Auto-Coding und manuelle Kodierung als stale/review-required.
- Regressionstest: Erfolgreiche `.vocs`-Uploads bieten in der UI direkt „Kodierstand prüfen“ mit `refreshCodingFreshness=1` an.
- Regressionstest: Unit-Dateien ohne `CodingSchemeRef` erhalten den No-Ref-Sentinel und aktivieren nicht den Legacy-Regex-Fallback.
- Regressionstest: `getUnitIdsByCodingSchemeRefs` erzwingt den kandidatengesteuerten Index-Probe-Pfad und verhindert die alte `unit_candidates`-CTE auch im Legacy-Fallback.
- Manuelle Gegenprüfung: Nach temporärem `.vocs`-Upload zeigte die API direkt `v1 STALE` und `v2 MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED`; die Kodierübersicht zeigte anschließend „Kodierstand prüfen“.
- `npx nx test backend --runInBand`
- `npx nx lint backend --skip-nx-cache`
- `make dev-db-validate-changelog`
- `git diff --check`

## Performance-Beleg

Synthetische DB-Simulation des Kernpfads `getUnitIdsByCodingSchemeRefs` am 26.06.2026 in der lokalen Docker-Postgres-DB mit rollbacked Benchmark-Schema:

- Setup: 1.000.000 Units, 10.000 Booklets, 1.000 Persons, 100.000 normalisierte Unit-Dateien, 1.000 passende Unit-Dateien, 1.000 Legacy-Unit-Dateien.
- Messmethode: `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, SUMMARY ON, TIMING OFF, BUFFERS OFF)`.
- Alter all-unit CTE-Pfad, 1.000 Treffer: `Execution Time: 2074.576 ms`.
- Neuer kandidatengesteuerter Pfad, 1.000 Treffer: `Execution Time: 6.258 ms`.
- Alter all-unit CTE-Pfad, keine Treffer: `Execution Time: 1609.311 ms`.
- Neuer kandidatengesteuerter Pfad, keine Treffer: `Execution Time: 1.068 ms`.
- Legacy-Existenzprobe: `Execution Time: 0.022 ms`.
- Alter Legacy-Fallback, 1.000 Treffer: `Execution Time: 1547.964 ms`.
- Neuer Legacy-Fallback, 1.000 Treffer: `Execution Time: 13.326 ms`.

Damit ist die Denormalisierung nicht nur Robustheits-Metadatum, sondern wird im Freshness-Pfad tatsächlich als indexierter Vorfilter plus indexierbarer Unit-Datei-Zuordnung genutzt. Unit-Dateien ohne Ref sind als bekannt ref-los markiert und halten den Legacy-Fallback nicht offen.

Refs #688

body:
Online research resolves the macOS on-device gate definitively (#19). Third-party FSKit is broken on macOS 26 — a confirmed **Apple bug** affecting all implementations including Apple's own `FSKitSample`: `fskitd` rejects the client connection (`Hello FSClient! entitlement no`), documented in [andrewgazelka/loaf#1](https://github.com/andrewgazelka/loaf/issues/1), with Apple DTS confirming a fix is pending.

Corrects the earlier 'reboot is the remedy' note (a reboot / `sudo killall fskit` does **not** fix it — already tried by others) and clarifies **SIP is not involved**: FSKit is a user-space app-extension model designed to run with SIP enabled; the `kickstart` SIP error was only about restarting a system daemon. Re-validate when Apple ships an FSKit fix.

**Description**

Fix `op-proofs init`'s post-init backfill so retries don't overshoot the operator-requested target. Init was computing `target_earliest_block` as `proof_window.earliest.number - window`.  This works on the first run because earliest == latest (init just placed the snapshot at the chain tip). author: gmpassos
body:
## Summary

Second step of the maps work — adds **container-entry assignment** to the Dart frontend + interpreter. This also unlocks **list index assignment** (`a[i] = v`), which was missing for the same reason. The grammar's assignment left-hand side was only a bare `variable()`, so `m[k] = v` and `a[i] = v` failed with a `SyntaxError`.

- **Grammar** — parse `variable[key] op expr` as an assignment target, with all compound operators (`=`, `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `~/=`). Enables idioms like `m["x"] += 1` (frequency maps).
- **AST** — new `ASTExpressionVariableEntryAssignment`; new `ASTValue.writeKey` / `writeIndex` that mutate the underlying `Map`/`List` **in place**. A `Map` is always written by key (even a numeric one); a `List` by index. For compound ops the current entry is read, combined, and written back.
- **Code generators** — dispatch + emit `variable[key] op expr`, so programs round-trip (parse → regenerate → re-parse). The abstract base's default throws `UnsupportedError`; the Wasm implementation lands with the Wasm-maps slice.
- **Empty-collection inference fix** — an empty `{}` literal (typed `Map<dynamic,dynamic>`) is now assignable to a typed map like `Map<String,int>`. `ASTTypeMap.acceptsType` now treats a `dynamic` key/value component as a wildcard — matching how lists already ignore their element type for assignment, so `Map<String,int> m = {};` works just like `List<int> a = [];` (the asymmetry was that `ASTTypeArray` doesn't register `generics` while `ASTTypeMap` does, so maps were strictly checked).

## Tests

`test/apollovm_dart_maps_test.dart` extended (now 27 tests): map set/update/grow, String keys, variable keys, String values, compound `+=`, empty-map frequency counter, and list index assignment (set, compound, in-place reorder). Pass on `-p vm` and `-p chrome`. Full suite green (504), round-trip regeneration verified, `dart analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings` clean, formatted.

## Next

**Wasm map codegen** — now that the frontend fully supports maps (literals, `m[k]` get/set, `.length`/`.keys`/`.values`/`.containsKey`, iteration, params), the Wasm backend can implement them as parity-tested slices.

## Summary
- Add `rejection_reason`, `reviewed_by`, and `reviewed_at` to `Listing::$fillable` so marketplace/listing moderation decisions actually persist their audit trail.
- Restore the real assertions in `ListingModerationServiceTest` that previously documented (and locked in) the buggy `null` behaviour.
- Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `[Unreleased] → Fixed`.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Documentation update

## Contributor Terms
- [x] I have read and agree to `CONTRIBUTOR_TERMS.md`, including the licence grant, patent grant, ownership/employer-permission confirmation, third-party-code restrictions, and AI-disclosure requirements.
- [x] I confirm I own this contribution or am authorised to submit it on behalf of the person or organisation that owns it.
- [x] I have disclosed meaningful AI-generated or AI-assisted contributions in this PR, or this PR contains no meaningful AI-generated or AI-assisted contribution.

**Third-Party Material Disclosure:** None

**AI Contribution Disclosure:** Authored with Claude Code (Anthropic) — diagnosis, the `$fillable` fix, the restored test assertions, and the changelog entry.

## Root Cause Analysis (required for bug fixes)
**What was the bug?**
Listing moderation decisions silently lost their audit trail. When an admin flagged, approved, or rejected a listing, the rejection reason (`rejection_reason`), the reviewing admin (`reviewed_by`), and the review timestamp (`reviewed_at`) were never written to the database, even though the code appeared to set them.

**Root Cause:**
`ListingModerationService::flag()`, `approve()`, and `reject()` write those columns via `$listing->update([...])` (mass assignment). The columns exist in the `listings` table, but they were missing from `Listing::$fillable`. Eloquent's mass-assignment protection silently strips any key not in `$fillable` — no error, no warning — so the three moderation fields were dropped on every write.

**Why wasn't it caught earlier?**
The existing unit tests actually asserted the *buggy* behaviour (`assertNull($row->rejection_reason)`, etc.) with `// NOTE:` comments flagging the suspected cause, so the test suite was green while the bug was live. There was no test asserting the values should persist.

**Prevention:**
- The three fields are now in `Listing::$fillable` (`reviewed_at` was already cast to `datetime`).
- `ListingModerationServiceTest` now asserts the values actually persist (reason text, `reviewed_by === admin id`, `reviewed_at` not null) — converting the tests from "documents the bug" into a real regression guard against future `$fillable` omissions.

## Pre-Deployment Checklist
- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes in `react-frontend/` — n/a (no frontend changes)
- [ ] `npm run build` succeeds in `react-frontend/` — n/a (no frontend changes)
- [x] PHP syntax check passes (`php -l` on all changed files)
- [x] New DELETE/UPDATE queries include `AND tenant_id = ?` for tenant-scoped tables — n/a (no new queries; service already scopes by `tenant_id`)
- [x] No `data.data ??` patterns introduced
- [x] No new `as any` type assertions without justification
- [x] No locale files changed

## Test Plan
Replicated the CI bootstrap locally (MariaDB 10.11 + `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` + seeded tenants 1/2) and ran the targeted suite:

```
MAIL_MAILER=array vendor/bin/phpunit \
  tests/Laravel/Unit/Services/ListingModerationServiceTest.php --no-coverage
→ OK (22 tests, 57 assertions)
```

Also verified there is no mass-assignment exposure: the user-facing update path (`ListingService::…->fill(collect($data)->only($allowed)->all())`) uses an explicit `$allowed` whitelist that does **not** include the moderation fields, so they remain settable only server-side by `ListingModerationService`.

author: zacxdev
body:
Two GUI activity collectors feeding the existing activity-collector spool in the **v1 emit format**, so the daemon (collector.py) ships them unchanged. **Local-spool only — nothing ships to ClickHouse** (gated on the authed store, PR #67).

Stacked on `feat/activity-collector-slice` (depends on its emit/collector foundation).

## Deliverable 1 — X11 full-content keylogger (`scripts/collector/keylog/`)
- Global capture via the **X11 RECORD extension** (python-xlib) as the logged-in user — no root, no `input` group.
- `keycode -> keysym -> char` honoring Shift / CapsLock / AltGr; Latin-1 + Unicode keysyms. A fresh keymap re-query catches keycodes remapped on the fly (how xdotool/IMEs inject unicode) that a cached lookup misses.
- Chunker buffers keystrokes into typing units — flush on **focus-change / Enter / idle (2s) / maxlen (4096)**; BackSpace edits the standing buffer. (Rationale: one row per keystroke is useless + wasteful.)
- Active-window context attached: WM_CLASS (app), `_NET_WM_NAME` (title), active window id (session), EWMH/i3 workspace.
- Emits `source=keys kind=typing text=<chunk> app=<wm_class> project="" session=<win id> payload={title,workspace,flush}`.

**Verified on the live X session with SYNTHETIC xdotool input only** (no real keystrokes): the exact probe `keylog-probe-AbC123 !@# 你好` + Enter round-tripped through the spool in correct v1 format. Test capture shredded after.

## Deliverable 2 — Chrome MV3 browser collector (`scripts/collector/browser-ext/`)
- MV3 extension: `chrome.tabs` / `webNavigation` / `windows` / `idle` + `storage.session` (active-duration survives SW suspension). Full URL capture. POSTs nav/focus events to a loopback receiver.
- `receiver.py`: stdlib `http.server` on `127.0.0.1:8787`, maps events to v1 spool records (shares `keylog/spool_emit`). Kept as a separate service so the privileged shipper has no inbound socket.

**Verified end-to-end in chromium on the live session**: loaded unpacked, navigated example.com -> example.org; `nav` + `focus` records landed in the spool, with `active_ms` correctly computed across navigations (11404ms). (Initial run surfaced a missing `storage` permission — fixed.)

## Tests (29, all green)
keymap/modifier->char, chunking boundaries, emit-format round-trip through the real `collector.parse_line`, receiver POST->spool incl. arbitrary content (quotes/newlines/unicode/a fake `password123!`).

## Nix wiring (staged, NOT switched)
`home.file` symlinks for both module dirs + two `systemd.user.services`: `keylog` (gated on `graphical-session.target`; needs X) and `browser-activity-receiver` (loopback). Validated via `nix eval` of the activation config; **not** enabled — enablement is a deliberate converge step.

## Safety
Nothing shipped to ClickHouse. All test captures/spools used `/tmp` dirs and were shredded; no keylogger left running.

author: copilot
body:
The `scan_ruby` GitHub Actions job was failing due to a tooling-version check, not an application security finding. The Brakeman wrapper forced `--ensure-latest`, which exits non-zero whenever a newer Brakeman release exists than the locked project version.

- **Root cause**
  - `bin/brakeman` injected `--ensure-latest`, causing CI failure with Brakeman `7.1.1` when `8.0.5` was available.

- **Change**
  - Updated the Brakeman wrapper to invoke the bundled executable directly and stop enforcing “latest available” at runtime.

- **Impact**
  - `scan_ruby` now reflects actual static-analysis results for the codebase, rather than failing on upstream tool release drift.

```ruby
#!/usr/bin/env ruby

require "rubygems"
require "bundler/setup"

load Gem.bin_path("brakeman", "brakeman")
```

author: praxeo
body:
Four requests from this session, all client-side (no build step), validated by the full jsdom flow suite.

## 1. Saved transcripts moved to the top
History (the "Show saved transcripts" toggle + list) now sits at the **top** of the settings card, above Access — instead of buried beneath Access/Options/Keyterms/Advanced/Audio. The primary dictation card stays first in the DOM (compactness contract intact) and the persisted `historyVisible` collapse toggle is unchanged.

## 2. Invisible caret in the "Last dictation" box
The slot kept a 96px display cap (`max-height`/`overflow:auto`) with no padding, which clipped the caret while typing or adding a new line ("not visible but working"). On `:focus` the cap is now lifted (`max-height:none; overflow:visible`), plus an explicit `caret-color` and a no-reflow accent ring.

## 3. "Last dictation" box always available
`renderLastDictation` no longer hides the slot mid-session — it stays visible & editable whenever there's a filed note (only hidden when nothing is filed, since an empty slot can't persist an edit). "Append to this" is disabled mid-session.

## 4. Append via the phone mic — **the real bug**
> *"appends on the desktop but the phone mic doesn't respect it"*

Root cause: the desktop's `deliverRemoteText` **always replaced** its note with whatever the phone sent — it never consulted the desktop's append mode. So phone dictations could never append.

**Fix — the desktop OWNS append in the phone-link flow:**
- A **joined phone is a dumb mic**: `startRecording` forces a fresh single dictation when joined (click-to-append suppressed in `toggleAppendArm` + the box-focus arm), so it always delivers **one** segment.
- The **desktop** then appends or replaces in `deliverRemoteText` per **this device's** append mode / one-shot arm — mirroring single-desktop append, which a clinician expects to apply no matter which mic dictated.
- **Single-owner by design**: if both sides appended you'd get **double-append = wrong text on a chart**. The `delivery_id` dedupe ring runs *before* the append, so a replayed/retried delivery can never double-append. A *solo* big-button device (not joined) still appends locally.

> ⚠️ **Design note for review:** I chose "desktop owns append" because the desktop is the note/clipboard owner and you said append already works there. The trade-off is that a *joined* phone's local click-to-append is now a no-op (append is the desktop's job). If you instead wanted the **phone** to own append (e.g. an append control on the big-button screen), say so and I'll flip it.

## Validation
`node --check worker.js` + served-inline-script check + full `tests/flow.test.mjs` suite → **all scenarios pass**. Scenario 20 gains desktop-appends-phone-delivery (+ replay-dedupe + append-off-replaces); s25b asserts a joined phone delivers a single segment & click-to-append is a no-op; s32 asserts the slot stays visible mid-session. `CLAUDE.md` updated to match.

author: hm21
body:
Closes #5490

## Description

Fixes two independent ways the camera record button could end up unable to
stop a recording. Both surface as the same user report: *"the recording just
kept running and I couldn't stop it."*

**1. Press-down button can't stop an externally-started recording (gesture layer).**
In hold-to-record (press-down) mode the shutter button was a dead stop control
whenever recording was started by something *other* than that press — a volume
key, BLE remote, or the toggle event. `onTapDown` bailed on `isRecording`,
`onTapUp` / `onTapCancel` bailed on `!_startedByPressDown`, and `onTap` /
`onLongPress*` are disabled in press-down mode, so nothing could issue a stop.
A fresh press-down on an already-active recording now stops it (and resets the
flag so the following release doesn't double-stop).

**2. Stop handler could latch `isStoppingRecording=true` forever (BLoC layer).**
`_onRecordingStopRequested` set `isStoppingRecording=true` and only cleared it
after several `await`s (audio-session teardown, native `stopRecording()`,
wakelock). If any of those threw, the flag stayed `true` and the guard at the
top of the handler swallowed *every* future stop — the recording kept running
with no way to stop it (matches the pure long-press report). The critical
window is now wrapped so the recorder always resets to `idle` (discarding the
partial clip) on failure, and the error is reported without flooding Crashlytics
(expected platform/IO failure → not wrapped in `Reportable`).

**Related Issue:**

None.

## Verification

- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — no issues
- `flutter test test/blocs/video_recorder/ test/widgets/video_recorder/` — 243/243 pass, including the two new regression tests:

author: imrans110
body:
## Problem

Submitting a `<TabbedForm>` with many required fields throws **"Maximum update depth exceeded"** (React's `NESTED_UPDATE_LIMIT`). The same fields in a `<SimpleForm>` work fine. Reported in #11290 with a verified reproduction.

Root cause: `useFormGroup` subscribes to react-hook-form's `validatingFields` to compute a group-level `isValidating` that is **not consumed anywhere** (`FormTabHeader` and `TranslatableInputsTab` read only `isValid`). Because react-admin wraps every validator as `async` in `useInput`, react-hook-form toggles `validatingFields` per field on submit; subscribing to it re-renders every form group on each toggle, so a `TabbedForm` with enough required fields across tabs exceeds React's maximum update depth. `SimpleForm` has no `FormGroup`, so it is unaffected.

## Solution

Stop subscribing to `validatingFields` in `useFormGroup`. The unused group-level `isValidating` becomes a constant `false`. Validation and the tab error badges — driven by `errors` / `isValid` — are unchanged. Per-input async validation spinners are unaffected, since those come from each input's own `fieldState.isValidating` (`useController`), not from `useFormGroup`.

## How To Test

- Open the new **`ManyRequiredInputs`** story (`ra-ui-materialui/forms/TabbedForm`) in Storybook and click **SAVE** with the fields empty: on `master` it throws "Maximum update depth exceeded"; with this fix it validates normally.
- Run the regression unit test:
  ```sh
  yarn test-unit packages/ra-core/src/form/groups/useFormGroup.spec.tsx -t "validating state"
  ```
  It fails on `master` (the group re-renders ~38× on repeated re-validation) and passes with this fix.

> The crash is timing-sensitive in a real browser; jsdom batches updates via `act()` and does not reproduce the depth overflow, so the unit test targets the underlying re-render behaviour while the Storybook story provides the in-browser check.

## Additional Checks

- [x] The PR targets `master` for a bugfix or a documentation fix, or `next` for a feature
- [x] The PR includes **unit tests** (if not possible, describe why)
- [x] The PR includes one or several **stories** (if not possible, describe why)
- [x] The **documentation** is up to date (no change needed — the only `isValidating` reference in the docs uses react-hook-form's global `useFormState().isValidating`, which this change does not affect)

Closes #11290

body:
## Problem

The service crashes at startup with `sqlalchemy.exc.ArgumentError: Expected string or URL object, got None` because `app/db/database.py` called `create_engine(DATABASE_URL)` at module import time, before `app/core/config.py` had a chance to run `load_dotenv()` and populate `DATABASE_URL`.

## Solution

Replaced the eager `create_engine` call with a `_get_engine()` helper that initialises the engine on first call and caches it in the module-level `engine` variable (initially `None`). `get_connection()` now delegates to `_get_engine()`, so the engine is only created when a connection is first requested — well after all environment variables have been loaded.

### Changes

author: elares
body:
## What

A tie-to-reality **validation** of a load-bearing design choice (no model change): the simulation feeds SDT and PDT exogenous ROS into **one** bistable death switch with a single `death_threshold` and `sdt_ros == pdt_ros` — i.e. the dose-to-kill is a property of the cell/tissue, not the ROS source.

**Zhu et al. 2015** (PMID 25927018, PMC4410434, "In-vivo singlet oxygen threshold doses for PDT") measured the reacted-singlet-oxygen necrosis threshold [1O2]rx in vivo as approximately **photosensitizer-independent**: Photofrin ~0.56, BPD ~0.72, mTHPC ~0.40 mM (~0.5 mM, within a factor of **1.8** across three chemically distinct sensitizers). That is real-world support for the model's single source-independent `death_threshold` structure.

## Changes (Python/docs only — no Rust)

- `scripts/validate_pdt_threshold.py` (pure stdlib, runs in CI; drift-guards `sdt_ros`/`pdt_ros`/`death_threshold` against `params.rs`).
- `analysis/calibration/pdt-threshold-validation.{md,json}` (committed result).
- `tests/test_pdt_threshold.py` (3 offline guards, incl. one pinning the O₂-dependence honesty caveat).
- CALIBRATION_STATUS row + CLAUDE.md real-data-anchored-legs line.

## Scope / honesty

- The model is dimensionless, so this validates the **form** (single source-independent threshold) + **order of magnitude**, NOT a unit-rigorous calibration of `death_threshold=10.0`. Status label is **"Partially anchored (form + order of magnitude)"**, not "Calibrated".
- The O₂-dependence form is only partly addressed: the model's `o2_dependent_exo_factor` (#336) is **linear** while Zhu's is **Michaelis/saturating**. The linear form is a first-order approximation; the precise oxygen-quenching constant is in the full text (**flagged, not fabricated**) — the Michaelis-form refinement is the remaining #464 follow-up.

## Validation

293 Python tests pass; no Rust change (fast CI). Adversarial honesty review: **0 issues** ("honest and appropriately scoped, does not overclaim"; citation accurate; validation logic sound, not circular).

author: zedoraps
body:
## 🔍 Problem

- BSD/RFC 3164 syslog timestamps do not include a year.
- `parse_time("%b %e %H:%M:%S")` currently falls back to 1970, forcing users to patch in a year manually.
- Timestamp arithmetic is brittle around leap years, year boundaries, and midnight boundaries for time-only inputs.

## 🛠️ Solution

- Add an explicit `reference` argument to `parse_time` for partial date formats.
- Resolve missing years by choosing the valid candidate closest to the reference time.
- Resolve time-only formats to the closest day around the reference time.
- Keep the old 1970 default when `reference` is absent, but emit a deprecation warning.
- Return null with warnings for unsupported partial date/reference combinations.

## 💬 Review

- Focus on the missing-date resolution logic, especially syslog-style timestamps, leap days, timezone offsets, and warning behavior for unsupported formats.

author: zachl111
body: ## Summary `ChatTool` stores its `parameters` as a JSON string in Firestore (to dodge Firestore nesting limits) and parses it back with a pre-validator. The validator calls `json.loads` with no guard, so a single app whose stored parameters string is not valid JSON raises `JSONDecodeError` while the `ChatTool` is being built. That turns into an HTTP 500 on the app read, and since the parse happens during model construction it takes down the whole read for that app, not just the one tool. This PR catches the parse error and drops the malformed value to `None`, matching the field's `Optional` default. This is a proactive hardening change; there is no filed GitHub issue for it. ## Root cause In `backend/models/app.py`, the `parameters` pre-validator `ChatTool.deserialize_parameters` does the conversion with no error handling: ```python @field_validator('parameters', mode='before') @classmethod def deserialize_parameters(cls, v): """Deserialize parameters from JSON string (stored that way in Firestore to avoid nesting limits).""" if isinstance(v, str): return json.loads(v) return v ``` The value comes straight from Firestore, so if a stored record holds a parameters string that is not valid JSON (a truncated or partial write, a legacy value), `json.loads` raises `json.JSONDecodeError`. That propagates out of validation as a 500 when the app is loaded, and because it fires during `ChatTool` construction the entire app read fails, not just the affected tool. ## Fix Wrap the parse in a try/except that catches the decode error, logs a warning, and returns `None`: ```python if isinstance(v, str): try: return json.loads(v) except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError): logger.warning('ChatTool.parameters is not valid JSON; dropping malformed parameters') return None return v ``` `None` is the declared default for `parameters`, so the bad tool loads with no parameters instead of crashing the read. Valid JSON strings parse exactly as before. ## Testing Added `backend/tests/unit/test_chat_tool_parameters_json.py` (registered in `backend/test.sh`). `models.app` is a light import, so the test sets `ENCRYPTION_SECRET` and imports `App` and `ChatTool` from source directly, then calls the validator through normal model construction. Cases covered: a non-JSON parameters string yields `parameters=None`, a valid JSON string still deserializes to the expected dict, and building a full `App` whose `chat_tools` entry has malformed parameters succeeds with that tool's parameters set to `None`. Verified red to green: the test fails on current main and passes with this change. ## PR status check No open PR changes the logic this PR fixes. The guard added here does not appear anywhere in this file's history, so it is not a previously reverted fix being resubmitted. No filed GitHub issue matches.

body: ## Контекст Follow-up к #457 (фиксы загрузки/glass в 2.0.47). Запустил **адверсариальную верификацию** этих двух фиксов 10-агентным sweep'ом — нашлось **5 реальных дефектов**, которые CI пропустил (chat integration-тест стабит `ChatRuntimeManager`, capture-тест хардкодит non-null `displayState`). Все исправлены с регресс-покрытием. | # | Severity | Дефект | Фикс | |---|---|---|---| | **A** | 🔴 CRASH | `agent-run-capture.ts` разыменовывал `displayState.isRunning` без null-guard → `TypeError` на cold `displayState===null` (capture-poll успевает к `getSnapshot` до резидентности рантайма) | null → not-yet-settled, продолжает polling. Тест `ARC-17C` | | **C+D** | 🔴 HIGH | cold-path перегружал `null` как «booting» И «ready-empty»; детерминированный boot-fail (нет creds) re-kick'ал свежий boot каждые ~250мс, а delete-before-throw гонял React Query retry и глотал ошибку | `coldBootState`-машина: `getSnapshot` возвращает стабильный `boot:{status,error}` и **никогда не throw**; failed sticky с экспоненциальным backoff (1s..30s); `disposeRuntime` чистит state. Тесты `chat.boot.test.ts` | | **B** | 🔴 HIGH | сессия **с историей** флешила ложное «Начните разговор» весь boot (`isConversationLoading` гас мгновенно) | клиент трактует `booting` как loading (loader, не empty-state), `failed` — как стабильную ошибку | | **E** | 🟡 MED | glass жил на **shared** `ModelSelectorContent` → тёк на legacy ModelPicker + text-heavy `McpOverviewPicker`; opaque Command маскировал эффект | opt-in `glass` prop (default opaque) + прозрачный Command; opt-in только workspace ModelPicker | ## Архитектура (loading state machine) ``` getSnapshot(cold): NONE/elapsed-backoff → kick boot, return boot:{status:'booting'} BOOTING (in-flight) → return boot:{status:'booting'} [runtimeCreations de-dups] FAILED (within backoff) → return boot:{status:'failed',error} [sticky, no re-kick] READY (warm) → real displayState + messages disposeRuntime → clears coldBootState (no phantom error) client: booting → loader · failed → stable error · ready+empty → empty-state (instant) ``` ## Проверки - `bun run typecheck` — 41/41 ✓ - `bun run lint` — clean, 6750 файлов ✓ - `bun test` host-service — 959 pass, вкл. **6 новых регресс-тестов** (`ARC-17C` + 4× `chat.boot.test.ts`) ✓ (1 pre-existing flaky terminal real-daemon тест, не связан с диффом) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Hardened the chat cold-boot path with a stable boot state and exponential backoff to stop crashes, swallowed errors, and empty-state flicker. Scoped the glass model picker to the workspace picker only. - Bug Fixes - Chat cold-boot: `getSnapshot` returns `boot:{status,error}` and never throws; failed boots are sticky with 1s–30s backoff and cleared on `disposeRuntime` (`packages/host-service`). - Capture loop: null-guarded `displayState` to avoid a crash on cold boot; keeps polling until settled (test `ARC-17C`). - Desktop client: treats `booting` as loading and `failed` as a stable error; prevents false “start a conversation” flash when history exists (`apps/desktop`). - Glass scope: added `glass` prop to `ModelSelectorContent` (default off) and made inner `Command` transparent when enabled; only the workspace `ModelPicker` opts in (`packages/ui`, workspace picker updated). Written for commit 023e04ea0be84ff92f6812d8739032478bf91f1f. Summary will update on new commits.

- `SessionKind` trimmed to `"worker" | "orchestrator"`; `isOrchestratorSession` tolerantly reads both `"orchestrator"` and `"meta-orchestrator"` role strings

author: noahgift
body:
## Summary

Fixes a real **wgpu portability bug** surfaced by the **intel AMD-Vulkan/RADV cross-silicon baseline**. Every GPU adapter-enumeration path in `aprender-compute` enumerated with `wgpu::Backends::all()`, which **includes `Backends::GL`**. On Linux hosts that expose GLES/EGL alongside Vulkan (the AMD-RADV box — and reproduced on this lambda RTX 4090 box), `all()` instantiates a GLES adapter whose `EglContext::make_current()` `.unwrap()`s and **fails inside `Drop`** → a panic in a destructor during cleanup → **SIGABRT** ("panic in a destructor during cleanup"), backtrace at `wgpu-hal-27.0.4 src/gles/egl.rs:305`, aborting the **whole process**. Standalone `list_adapters()`/`is_available()` could also spin/hang on the broken EGL path.

The compute kernels are correct — the fragility is purely adapter **enumeration** + the GLES `Drop` path.

## Fix

Add `gpu_backends()` → `wgpu::Backends::PRIMARY` (`= VULKAN | METAL | DX12 | BROWSER_WEBGPU` in wgpu 27; `GL` lives **only** in `SECONDARY`). Apply at:
- `device::shared_instance()` — construct the process-global `Instance` with this mask, so the **GLES backend is never even registered**.
- `GpuDevice::list_adapters_async` / `new_with_adapter_index_async` (`device/mod.rs`)
- `GpuDevicePool::all_async` (`pool.rs`)
- `monitor::backends` enumerate / query (`monitor/backends.rs`)

CUDA paths untouched (wgpu-only). Real GPU still found on every platform: Vulkan (Linux/AMD-RADV), Metal (Apple), DX12 (Windows).

## Falsifier (host-independent)

`test_gpu_backends_excludes_gles` inspects the bitmask: asserts it does **NOT** contain `Backends::GL` and **DOES** contain the platform's real backend.
- **RED** on `Backends::all()` (mask = `NOOP|VULKAN|GL|METAL|DX12|BROWSER_WEBGPU`) — mutation-verified.
- **GREEN** on `PRIMARY`.

## On-device evidence (this Linux box reproduces the GLES path)

- **BEFORE** (`Backends::all()`): 8 gpu/monitor tests FAIL, **all** panicking at `wgpu-hal gles/egl.rs:305` — the exact SIGABRT-in-Drop bug.
- **AFTER** (`PRIMARY`): `cargo test -p aprender-compute --features gpu --lib` = **3566 passed, 0 failed**, ZERO `egl.rs:305` panics; Vulkan adapter still enumerated.

## Cross-silicon verification (per cross-silicon directive)

- **intel (AMD-RADV / Vulkan)**: where it repros — confirm NO SIGABRT / NO hang, RADV/Vulkan adapter still found, parity passes. _(see PR comment)_
- **mini (Apple M4 / Metal)**: confirm Metal adapter still enumerated, parity tests still pass (mask didn't exclude Metal). _(see PR comment)_

## Contract

`contracts/apr-wgpu-adapter-enumeration-excludes-gles-v1.yaml` — `OBLIG-WGPU-ADAPTER-ENUMERATION-EXCLUDES-GLES`, `FALSIFY-WGPU-ENUM-GLES-001` (single-line ref). `pv validate` + `pv lint contracts/` PASS.

author: callum-rose
body:
Closes #15.

## Problem

The issue flagged a duplicated, drifted addon across two directories. Investigation showed it was broader: the repo carried **two complete, drifted copies of the entire Godot example project**, not just two addon folders.

- `EasyDI.Godot.Example/` was a **half-finished extraction that did not compile** — its `ApplicationLifetimeScope`/`SceneLifetimeScope` referenced `LifetimeScope`, `NodeInstaller`, and `NameHelper`, none of which existed in its own addon *or* in the `EasyDI.Godot.Core` package.
- `EasyDI.Godot/Godot/` was the complete, working copy.

A second, subtler divergence: the working addon **vendored its own copies of two types that belong to the published `EasyDI.Godot.Core` package** (`IReadyable`, `IEntryPointManagerExtensions`), and they had already drifted — the addon called `InvokeStartables()` while Core had renamed it to `InvokeReadyables()`.

## Changes

1. **Delete `EasyDI.Godot.Example/` entirely** — the broken, drifted duplicate. One example project remains.
2. **Depend on the authoritative `EasyDI.Godot.Core` package** — added a `ProjectReference` to the surviving project's `.csproj` and a matching entry in its `.sln`, mirroring how the deleted project was wired.
3. **Remove the addon's vendored Core types** (`Runtime/EntryPoints/IReadyable.cs`, `IEntryPointManagerExtensions.cs` and their `.uid`s) so Core is the single source for them.
4. **Fix the drifted call site** — `LifetimeScope` now calls `InvokeReadyables()` to match Core.

Keeping the canonical copy also preserves its genuine improvements (e.g. `GlobalRoot`'s `QueueFree()` de-duplication and the `ParentScopeType` enum) rather than regressing to the stale design.

## Verification

`dotnet build` of the surviving Godot project succeeds against Core.

## Note for reviewers (out of scope)

The surviving project pins `EasyDI`/`EasyDI.LifecycleHooks` at package version `1.0.0`, but those libraries are now at `1.1.0`/`1.0.4`, so a clean restore from nuget.org currently fails. This version drift is pre-existing and unrelated to issue #15 — left untouched here, but worth a separate fix.

author: janschm
body:
## Summary

This tightens composer/provider handling for platform-specific publish settings.

## Why

TikTok unaudited apps can only publish with `SELF_ONLY` visibility. The composer could show that state, but if the saved publish extras omitted `privacy_level`, the provider fell back to `PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE` and TikTok rejected the post. Pinterest also requires a board selection; the browser field was marked required, but server-side saves could still persist a selected Pinterest account without a board.

## Changes

- Auto-select TikTok `SELF_ONLY` in the composer only when creator-info says it is the sole allowed privacy option.
- Have the TikTok provider convert only an implicit missing privacy default to `SELF_ONLY` when creator-info permits only that value.
- Keep explicit public TikTok choices failing fast for unaudited apps.
- Enforce Pinterest board selection in the composer save endpoint.
- Preserve an existing Pinterest board if a later scoped save omits the board field.
- Add focused tests for TikTok unaudited privacy handling and Pinterest board validation.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest apps/composer/tests/test_account_scope.py tests/providers/test_tiktok.py apps/publisher/tests.py`
- `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check apps/composer/views.py apps/composer/tests/test_account_scope.py providers/tiktok.py tests/providers/test_tiktok.py`

body:
Fixes #172

`Brennan2019Hierarchical` targeted the v2 Deep Blue record but the reader still assumed the v1 layout and channel naming, so `study.run()` failed on a fresh download. #172 reports the `len(meta) != 2129` crash — it's the deepest of four migration breakages, three of which block loading before you reach it. Fixes:

1. **`_download`** now extracts `proc.zip` (the `timelock-preprocessing/*.mat` files) in addition to `audio.zip`, skipping `__MACOSX` entries. The extract-success marker is bumped to `success_extract_v2` so existing caches re-extract — they'd otherwise keep the old marker and never pick up the `.mat` files.
2. **`iter_timelines`** now excludes the 6 in-range subjects with no `.mat` (`S28, S29, S31, S33, S46, S47`) alongside the 9 incomplete-trial subjects (1973–1987 trials vs 2129 — the existing `# FIXME … bad trl?` set), yielding the 33 already declared by `_info`/docstring.
3. **`_load_raw`** types any channel absent from the `easycap-M10` montage (`EOG`→eog, else misc) before `set_montage`, handling v2's `AUD` (a few subjects keep `Aux5`). The channel assertion changes from "62 total" to "60 scalp EEG" (matches `data_shape`), since the aux name/count varies per subject.

This resolves #172's crash by excluding the incomplete subjects (the drop path — matching the paper's 33-subject cohort), rather than recovering them via a fixed alignment for the `meta.join(story)` index join. That recovery is a separate, larger decision — see the #172 discussion.

Adds a dataset-free regression test pinning `len(iter_timelines()) == 33`.

## Verification

`study.run()` loads all 33 subjects; `compute_study_info` matches `_info` exactly (33 timelines/subjects, 2226 events, `data_shape=(60, 366525)`, 500 Hz). `ruff check`/`ruff format` and `pytest neuralfetch/test_studies.py` are green locally.

## Notes for review

I worked through this independently from the tutorials — debugging down the stack to all four breakages — and only found #172 and @hubertjb's comment when raising this PR. @hubertjb, since you flagged taking it this week, it's entirely yours to take over, modify, or close; I'm opening it in case it saves the time.

author: markwuenschel-dev
body:
## Summary

Re-wires **login as a hard gate** in the web app. After the "Performance OS" redesign, the auth stack was left *parked*: the app opened straight into onboarding / the app shell, and login was only reachable on demand (Settings → account card, or a `LogWorkout` 401). This restores login as the front door — the app shell and onboarding are unreachable until the user is authenticated.

Backend auth (`/auth/register`, `/auth/token`, `/auth/me`) was already wired and is untouched; this is purely the frontend gate.

## What's included

- **New `web/src/perflab/screens/LoginScreen.tsx`** — a full-screen sign-in / register surface that mirrors the onboarding takeover's two-panel layout (brand panel + form) and reuses the existing `AuthProvider` actions (`login` / `register` / `isLoading`). Mode toggle, inline error surfacing, Enter-to-submit.
- **`web/src/App.tsx`** — renders `LoginScreen` whenever `!isAuthenticated`; the shell and onboarding render only once a token exists. Updated the stale top-of-file comment that described auth as "parked pending a follow-up" — this is that follow-up.

## How the flow works now

- **Unauthenticated** → full-screen `LoginScreen`, nothing else reachable.
- **Register** → `AuthContext.register` signs in and flips `onboardingPending` → `App` routes into the onboarding takeover → "Enter Perf Lab" → shell.
- **Sign in** → token set → shell.
- **Sign out** (Settings account card) → token cleared → back to the gate.
- **Token expiry** → a 401 on any `/v1` call hits `sessionBridge` → `AuthProvider` clears the token → user lands back on the gate automatically (no extra wiring).

The on-demand `AuthModal` (Settings / `LogWorkout` 401) is still mounted but now effectively dormant inside the app, since the gate blocks unauthenticated access. Left in place as a harmless fallback.

## Testing

Frontend-only change; no Python touched.

- `npx tsc -b` → exit 0 (clean)
- `npm run build` → green (only pre-existing warnings: browserslist data age, font `.woff2` runtime resolution)
- `npm run lint` → only the **3 known pre-existing** `react-refresh` errors in shadcn `badge`/`button`/`tabs`; **zero new** errors

## Notes

- Merging `main` auto-deploys production via Netlify.

## Objectif

Rapport automatique des **retours artisans**, généré **chaque lundi** et envoyé par email à l'administrateur, avec une **analyse** et un **plan d'amélioration priorisé** produits par l'IA. Une page admin permet de consulter l'historique et de générer un rapport à la demande.

## Ce que contient la PR

| Élément | Fichier |
|---|---|
| 🗄️ Table `feedback_reports` + RPC `get_feedback_reports()` (SECURITY DEFINER + allowlist admin, comme `get_all_feedback`) | `supabase/migrations/20260624140000_feedback_reports.sql` |
| ⚙️ Edge function : agrège les retours de la semaine → Gemini (synthèse, thèmes, plan priorisé impact/effort, quick wins) → stocke le rapport → email Resend. Auth : `x-cron-secret` (cron) **ou** JWT admin (bouton) | `supabase/functions/weekly-feedback-report/index.ts` |
| ⏰ Planificateur `pg_cron` + `pg_net` (lundi 08:00 UTC), secrets via **Vault** | `schedule_weekly_feedback_report.sql` |
| 🖥️ Page admin `/app/admin/reports` : historique + bouton « Générer maintenant » | `src/pages/AdminFeedbackReports.jsx` |
| 🧭 Route lazy + lien de navigation « Rapports hebdo » | `src/App.jsx`, `src/layouts/Layout.jsx` |
| `verify_jwt = false` (auth gérée dans la fonction) | `supabase/config.toml` |

## Étapes de mise en service (après merge / déploiement)

1. **Migration** : appliquée à la base (`feedback_reports` + `get_feedback_reports`).
2. **Edge function** déployée (`weekly-feedback-report`).
3. **Secrets de la fonction** (Dashboard → Edge Functions → Secrets) :
   - `GEMINI_API_KEY` *(déjà présent)*, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM` *(optionnel)*, `REPORT_RECIPIENTS` *(optionnel)*

4. **Planificateur** : exécuter `schedule_weekly_feedback_report.sql` (renseigner `<CRON_SECRET>`).

La page est utilisable immédiatement via **« Générer maintenant »** une fois la fonction déployée (l'email nécessite `RESEND_API_KEY`).

author: copilot
body:
Generated ComplexGitSync state files were persisting user-specific absolute paths, which can leak private local information. This update makes persisted path fields environment-variable based while preserving full runtime resolvability across Linux/macOS and Windows.

- **Path privacy for generated state artifacts**
  - `.gts` generation now writes home-anchored paths as env markers instead of raw absolute home paths:
    - `$HOME/...` on Linux/macOS
    - `%USERPROFILE%/...` or `%HOMEDRIVE%%HOMEPATH%/...` on Windows
  - Applied to:
    - `project.root_absolute_path`
    - `project.source_cgs_path`
    - `repo_state[*].absolute_path`
    - `repo_state[*].parent_absolute_path`
    - `repo_state[*].source_cgs_path`

- **`.lgr` register path sanitization**
  - `register.current_snapshot_path` and `snapshots[*].snapshot_path` now persist env-marker paths instead of raw resolved home paths.

- **Round-trip loading support**
  - Added explicit expansion/resolution logic so `.gts` and `.goc` inputs containing these markers are correctly resolved back to absolute filesystem paths at load time.

- **Documentation update**
  - `UPDATEFILES.md` now documents the path-privacy behavior for generated `.gts`/`.lgr` files.

- **Focused regression coverage**
  - Added unit tests covering:
    - `$HOME` serialization in generated `.gts`/`.lgr`
    - `.gts` rehydration from env-marker paths
    - `.goc` project source resolution from env-marker paths

```toml
# Before
root_absolute_path = "/home/alice/workspace/demo"

# After
root_absolute_path = "$HOME/workspace/demo"
```

author: jason-easyazz
body:
## What

When the touch panel's voice WS errors or drops, it shows a typing fallback (*"Type here while voice reconnects…"*). But that fallback was only ever cleared by `renderHome()` (idle/home button) — so when the socket **silently reconnects** (it does, with backoff in `skybridge-voice.js`), the panel stayed stuck telling the user voice was down even though it was already back.

## How I found it

Driving the live panel for screenshots, I saw it sitting in `sky-typing-fallback`. I verified the `/ws/voice/` backend is healthy — it connects and immediately streams `{"type":"state","state":"ambient"}` — so voice wasn't broken; the UI just never recovered. This is the "confused interface" class of bug.

## Fix

- Track the error-driven fallback distinctly (`voiceErrorFallback`), separate from a deliberately-opened command bar.
- On the `'ready'` event (fires when the socket re-opens, `skybridge-voice.js:85`), call `recoverFromVoiceError()` to return to voice mode.
- **Guards:** only recover when the mic is actually usable (`canUseMicrophone()`) and the user hasn't started typing a message. Cards/context on screen are left untouched.

## Tests

Extends `test_skybridge_resilience.js` (extract-and-shim of the real function body, no live kiosk):
- reconnect clears the stale typing fallback
- does not interrupt a half-typed message
- keeps typing fallback when the mic is unusable
- leaves a user-opened command bar open

**14 checks pass** (10 existing + 4 new).

## Verification
Unit-tested above; will confirm on the live panel (192.168.1.61) after deploy by inducing a WS drop→reconnect and screenshotting the recovery.

body: ## Summary Two major improvements — simplifies image imports and boosts Lighthouse performance from **80 → 98**. --- ## Part 1: Simplify image imports Eliminates the need to manually append `?w=400;800;1200&format=avif;webp;png&as=picture` to every image import. Images are auto-discovered via `import.meta.glob` and optimized automatically. ### Changes - **New `src/lib/image.ts`** — Exports `getImage()` helper and `ImageMap` type - **`vite.config.ts`** — `defaultDirectives` on imagetools plugin as safety net - **`QuestionCard.tsx`** — Generalized `SolutionImage` → `QuestionImage` (accepts `maxHeight` + `alt`), removed ~30 lines of duplicated ``/`` logic - **5 subjects migrated** (35 imports → 5 glob blocks): `cepe` (19), `esei` (6), `emeele` (6), `ece` (3), `equispe` (1) - **Docs**: `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `_template` updated ### Before / After ```ts // Before — 35 import lines with query strings import fig1 from "./assets/figure1.png?w=400;800;1200&format=avif;webp;png&as=picture"; image: fig1, // After — 1 glob block per subject, filename-based access const imageMap = import.meta.glob<{ default: Picture }>( "./assets/*.{png,jpeg,jpg}", { query: { w: "400;800;1200", format: "avif;webp;png", as: "picture" }, eager: true } ) as ImageMap; image: getImage(imageMap, "figure1.png"), ``` --- ## Part 2: Performance (Lighthouse 80 → 98) ### Code splitting — subject questions lazy-loaded `import.meta.glob` for questions was using `eager: true`, bundling all 26K lines of subject data into the initial JS. Changed to lazy (`eager: false`), which splits each subject's questions into its own chunk. | Chunk | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Main bundle (index.js) | 1,054 KB | **46 KB** | | Per-subject chunks | 0 (bundled) | 8 chunks (41–253 KB each) | Made all question query functions async (`getAllQuestions`, `getQuestionsByTopic`, `getQuestionsByExam`, `getTopicMegaTopicLabel`) and updated 4 page consumers to use `useState` + `useEffect`. ### CLS fix Added `min-height: 60svh` to the `` fallback spinner to prevent the footer from jumping as page content loads. ### Cache headers Added `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` in `vercel.json` for: - `/assets/*` (all hashed static assets — 1 year immutable) - `/exams/*.pdf` (exam PDFs) - Favicons, OG images, web manifest - `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` (1 day) ### Lighthouse results | Metric | Before | After | |---|---|---| | **Performance** | 80 | **98** | | FCP | 2.9s | **1.8s** | | LCP | 3.5s | **2.0s** | | CLS | 0.137 | **0 (fixed)** | | Render-blocking | 50 | **100** | | Accessibility | 100 | 100 | | Best Practices | 100 | 100 | | SEO | 92 | 92 | --- ## Verification - [x] `pnpm lint` — zero errors - [x] `pnpm build` — tsc + sitemap + vite build pass - [x] Lighthouse homepage — 98 Performance - [x] All 35 images optimized (AVIF, WebP, PNG at 400/800/1200px) - [x] Dev server (`pnpm dev`) loads without errors

body:
This pull request introduces several improvements to the process of handling user withdrawal ("desistência") in the system, focusing on better user experience, data integrity, and maintainability. The changes include enhanced UI feedback during the withdrawal process, improved backend logic for safely deleting related records, and a fix for anonymizing user data to avoid database constraint issues.

**Backend improvements to data deletion and anonymization:**

* Added the `_desvincular_referencias` function to automatically unlink all references to a record before deletion, ensuring that related records do not block the deletion process. This function dynamically handles any DocType that references the target, improving maintainability and robustness.
* Updated the `processar_desistencia` workflow: if deleting a `Responsavel` record fails due to existing links, the system now unlinks all references before retrying the deletion, ensuring data is properly cleaned up.
* Fixed the anonymization logic in `_anonimizar_user` to set `username` and `mobile_no` to `None` instead of an empty string, preventing unique constraint violations in the database.

**Frontend enhancements for withdrawal UI:**

* Improved the "Confirmar Desistência" modal by adding UI states for loading and error feedback, including a spinner animation and error message display. The modal now disables buttons during processing and resets UI state on open/close for a smoother user experience. author: meganechan
body:
## 🔴 Symptom (Tony)
`maw wake <alive-agent>` could route to "agent dead → re-launch" and `sendText` the launch command into the running agent's pane — operator sees `❯ claude` typed into a live agent (pollutes a working session).

## Root (same liveness family as #31/#32)
The "agent alive?" gate before the re-launch branch (`wake-cmd.ts` ~1637) trusted **only** `isAgentCommand(pane command)`. Any name it didn't recognize → "dead" → launch text injected into the live pane.

## Fix — `pane_current_command`, not pgrep alone
eq3 proved a pid-only guard has a **dangerous blind spot**: on some nodes a live `claude.exe` is **not** a child of the pane shell (`pgrep -P pane_pid` empty), so the pane reads "idle" → wake re-launches over the live agent. (Verified: on `25-lek` pgrep *did* find it; on `05-eq3` it did not — launch-method dependent.) tmux's `pane_current_command` reliably shows `claude.exe` in both.

A pane is re-launched into **only** when its foreground is a **bare shell** (`zsh/bash/sh/fish/empty`, dash-stripped) **AND** it has no live child process:
```ts
let agentAlive = info && isAgentCommand(info.command);
if (!agentAlive && info) {
  const cmd = (info.command || "").trim().toLowerCase().replace(/^-/, "");
  const isIdleShell = cmd === "" || cmd === "zsh" || cmd === "bash" || cmd === "sh" || cmd === "fish";
  if (!isIdleShell || !(await wakeSession.isPaneIdle(target))) agentAlive = true;
}
```
Any non-shell foreground (incl. `claude.exe` even when `isAgentCommand` misses it on a node without the `.exe` strip) is treated as alive. Mirrors the existing `ensureSessionRunning` idiom (`wake-session.ts:261`).

**`#31` (`.exe` via `pane_current_command`) remains the primary protector**; this is the safety net for nodes not yet on #31, and closes eq3's blind spot.

## Acceptance
- [x] live `claude.exe` (recognized OR not) → never re-launched → no `❯ claude` pollution
- [x] genuinely dead pane (bare idle shell) → still re-launched (no false-negative)
- [x] bare shell mid-startup (has children) → not re-launched (waitForEngine race)
- [x] CI green (build + 2964 default-safe + all isolated wake-cmd coverage); core-only, no hash

Note: the original "interactive attach-offer was dropped" premise was false — it's present at `wake-cmd.ts:1668`. Deploy: core → live pull alpha (no `pm2 restart`). Dev in worktree `~/maw-js-dev`.

author: philips77
body:
The `onServiceChanged()` method was added in Android S (API 31).
Before, the service changed event is inferred by checking connection parameters. 

Some Android phones, i.e. Samsung S8 with Android 9 Pie, perform service discovery also during bonding. This does not, however, invalidates services.
Moreover, invalidating services during bonding would cancel awaiting expected callback for the initial request that triggered bonding in the first place. Another request could then be started (with unlocked mutex) and would have been ignored by the system.

author: bobmatnyc
body:
## Summary

Claude Code 2.1.166 hardened cross-session messaging: relayed `SendMessage` calls no longer carry user authority. This broke MPM's Agent Teams workflow for scope expansion — the PM tried to reuse an in-context subagent via `SendMessage`, the subagent blocked, they argued 2–4 turns, then the PM spawned a fresh agent anyway (tokens wasted).

- **PM side** (`PM_INSTRUCTIONS.md`): explicitly prohibit `SendMessage` for scope expansion; mandate a fresh `Agent` call with full context + new scope embedded
- **Subagent side** (`BASE_AGENT.md`): add a one-turn graceful refusal protocol — subagents immediately signal "spawn a fresh agent" instead of arguing

## Changes

- `src/claude_mpm/agents/PM_INSTRUCTIONS.md` — new paragraph under Agent Teams Note banning SendMessage for scope expansion (CC ≥ 2.1.166)
- `src/claude_mpm/agents/BASE_AGENT.md` — new `## SendMessage Scope-Expansion Protocol` section teaching subagents to exit cleanly in one turn

## Test plan

- [ ] In Agent Teams mode, give PM a task, then ask to expand scope — confirm PM spawns a fresh agent rather than calling SendMessage
- [ ] If SendMessage is attempted (e.g. by an older PM prompt), confirm subagent responds with the one-line signal rather than entering an argument loop

Closes #901

**Description**

queryR2Absolute treats any flag at an executable address as a call target (registerFunctionFlag). In statically-linked binaries and firmware, .rodata shares the r-x segment with code, so `str.*` flags were registered as functions and pdg printed the flag name (e.g. `str.Hello`) instead of the string literal.

Skip string-space flags in that loop so they fall through to the existing string handling and decompile as literals again.

Restores the pdg string output asserted by the x86_16/x86_32/x86_64, comments, typedef and similar tests under test/db/extras.

author: himanshugoel2797
body:
Rethinks the base-Lisp interpreter (`libs/lisp/`) from a tree-walking CEK machine into a **compile-to-register-bytecode VM**, removes the unused shader tier, and **deletes the tree-walker**. The VM is now the sole evaluator and the OS boots and runs on it.

Design + plan: `notes/core/lisp-vm.md`.

Two decisions: (1) **replace the evaluator outright** — no fallback; (2) **don't freeze core ops** — they stay redefinable via VM inline caches guarded on the binding cell, which forces boxed cells (fixing `set!`-on-captured and mutual/forward local recursion).

### Status
- [x] **P0** — remove `libs/lisp_shader/` (~14.5k LOC) + design note.
- [x] **P1** — full expression-form compiler (inline caches, boxed cells, letrec/case/while/quasiquote); differential + 20000-case fuzzer, 0 failures.
- [x] **P2** — real freestanding kernel source `lbc.c`/`lbc.h`; resumable register VM (budget/suspend) + inline-cache prim fast paths.
- [x] **P3a** — compiled closures are GC objects (`LISP_OBJ_BCCLOSURE`).
- [x] **P3b** — wire the VM into `lisp_eval`/`lisp_apply`/`lisp_ctx_resume`; GC-root the register stack; compile the module system; grow register/frame stacks on demand.
- [x] **P3e** — **delete the CEK tree-walker** (`eval.c` ~1500 → ~370 lines: `step_eval`/`step_applyk`/`ctx_run`, `do_call`, all special-form starters, `K_*` frames, `qq_expand`, `lisp_make_closure`, the `form_id` field). The VM is the sole evaluator.
- [x] **P4** — boots clean single-core; **28/28 in-OS self-tests pass**, all `Core*` servers + drivers up; host suite green. Register VM ~25–27× the tree-walker on a tail loop (host bench).

### Known issue (pre-existing, not introduced here)
Under **SMP≥2**, ~30–50% of boots hit a flaky `#GP` memory-corruption race during multi-core scheduler bring-up (single-core is 100% clean). Root cause: `prim_send` (sched.c) `deep_copy`s a message into the **receiver's lock-free per-context heap from the sender's core** — concurrent unlocked heap access. Structural in `sched.c` (unchanged by this PR; the faster VM just exposes it more); the fix is a design change (per-heap lock / system-heap staging / receiver-side copy), tracked as a follow-up.
