author: davidbshan
body:
Addresses the open review comments on #202 (the `dev`→`main` release PR). Since #202 merges `dev`, these fixes land on `dev`.

## 1. `list_endpoints()` returned `[]` with no key configured (api.py)
With `RUNPOD_API_KEY` unset, the function iterated an empty key pool and returned `[]` **without a single authenticated call** — callers like slot-reconcile / teardown read `[]` as "fleet confirmed absent" and act on an unauthenticated view. Now it **raises** on a missing key (matching the old `request_with_retries()` behavior), and also **raises on a non-list 200 body** (previously skipped silently → a partial fleet view trusted as complete).

## 2. `advance_key()` wrap could make the deploy loop forever (keys.py, jobs.py)
`advance_key()` **wraps** and always returns `True` for a multi-key pool, so `deploy_train_endpoint`'s `if rp_keys.advance_key(): continue` could spin forever when *every* account is quota-exhausted. The deploy now **bounds failovers by `key_count()`** (one pass over the pool) and then raises; the lifecycle retry budget handles waiting for quota to recover. `advance_key()`'s docstring now states that `True` ≠ "more accounts remain".

## 3. No-capacity reported as "worker stuck" (jobs.py, base.py, lifecycle.py)
An `IN_QUEUE` / `THROTTLED` **never-scheduled** failure surfaced as `stalled: worker stuck`, pointing debugging at worker health instead of provider capacity. Added a distinct **`no_capacity`** failure category (never scheduled — no capacity for the pinned GPU class), so the terminal message now reads `no_capacity: never scheduled: job stuck IN_QUEUE for …`. It stays infra-shaped → retried on the next-best GPU. `UNHEALTHY` (failed image pull) and no-progress stalls remain `stalled`.

> Note: this is the **observability** half of the reported P2. The "burst capacity / broader fallback / submission throttling" half is a larger design change tracked with the known RunPod waterfall/throttle + MIG-exclusion work, out of scope here.

## 4. `_read_adapter_tensor_keys()` header-shape validation (lora.py)
The safetensors header is now validated to decode to a **JSON object with string keys**, raising a clear `ValueError` instead of a confusing downstream `TypeError` in `_is_lora_key` on a corrupt/hostile file.

## Tests
- `list_endpoints` raises with no key and on a non-list response.
- `deploy_train_endpoint` terminates (raises, no infinite loop) when all accounts are exhausted.
- The two capacity poll-paths assert `no_capacity`; UNHEALTHY/no-progress stay `stalled`.
- Non-object safetensors header raises `ValueError`.

`907 passed, 5 skipped`; `ruff check` clean.

author: yurii-vasyliev
body:
## Problem

`calculate-version.cjs` treated `point/*` branches as the old date-based beta snapshots, so `point/26.04.2` would build as `26.10.0.N-beta` instead of `26.04.2.N`. Versions were also a raw commit count off `origin/main..HEAD` (fragile to main drift), there were no per-version tags, and the `RELEASED_POINT_BRANCHES` repo variable was set but unused.

## Changes

**`scripts/calculate-version.cjs`**
- Cycle + point parsed from the branch name: `release/YY.MM` → `YY.MM.0.N` (cycle base), `point/YY.MM.P` → `YY.MM.P.N`.
- `N` is **tag-anchored** — release-worthy commits since the `.0` build tag, excluding `chore/ci/docs/test/style` so housekeeping commits don't burn a version (`fix(ci):` still counts).
- Uniform **`-rc`** suffix unless the branch is in `RELEASED_POINT_BRANCHES`.
- Unrecognized `release/`/`point/` branch names now throw instead of publishing a malformed version.

**`.github/workflows/release-and-build.yml`**
- Wires in `vars.RELEASED_POINT_BRANCHES` (previously dead config).
- Skips build/publish/tag when `v<version>` is already tagged → chore-only pushes are clean no-ops and every tag stays unique.
- Tags the source commit after a successful deploy (immutable version↔commit record **and** the next build's counter anchor).
- Isolated per-point PPA target (`ppa-build-point-<cycle>.<point>`) instead of a shared `ppa-build-point`.
- Adds `workflow_dispatch` to (re)build a branch after GA promotion via the variable.

## Dry-run (`RELEASED_POINT_BRANCHES=point/26.04.1`)

| Branch | Version |
|---|---|
| `main` | `26.10.0.N-beta` |
| `release/26.04` | `26.04.0.0-rc` |
| `point/26.04.1` | `26.04.1.0` (GA) |
| `point/26.04.2` | `26.04.2.0-rc` |

## Rollout notes
- The new logic only applies to a branch once that branch contains these files — `release/26.04`, `point/26.04.1`, `point/26.04.2` need this change merged/cherry-picked in to pick it up.
- First build on each branch starts at `.0` (no anchor tags exist yet); the anchor is created automatically by the tag step.
- Legacy `point/2026-04-14` and `release/1.x` branches will fail loudly if pushed (they don't match the calendar format).
- Per-point PPA target names change for `point/*`; downstream consumers of the old shared `ppa-build-point` need repointing.

author: baozhoutao
body:
## Problem

On the analytics dataset query path (`POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query`), a metric widget filtered on a boolean field (e.g. `{ is_critical: true }`) **always returned 0**, and pie/donut/bar charts grouped by a boolean dimension failed to bucket.

## Root cause

A lossy string roundtrip in the filter normalizer:

1. `stringifyForCube` serialized boolean `true` → `'1'` ([`filter-normalizer.ts`](../blob/main/packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/filter-normalizer.ts)) — indistinguishable from a numeric `1`.
2. `ObjectQLStrategy` then coerced `'1'` back to the **number** `1` via `coerceFilterValueForSql` and passed `{ is_critical: 1 }` into `engine.aggregate`.
3. The stored field holds a **real boolean** `true`, so `1 !== true` — the comparison never matched.

The SQL strategy needs `1`/`0` (better-sqlite3 cannot bind a JS boolean), but the ObjectQL engine compares against the *stored* runtime type — sharing one coercer was the defect.

## Fix

- `stringifyForCube` serializes booleans as the tokens `'true'`/`'false'`, preserving boolean identity through the `string[]` pipeline form (SQL output unchanged: `'true'` → `1`).
- New `coerceFilterValueForObjectQL` recovers a real `true`/`false` for the ObjectQL engine; SQL path keeps recovering `1`/`0`. Shared numeric recovery extracted into `recoverNumber`.
- `ObjectQLStrategy.convertFilter` uses the ObjectQL coercer.

## Test

New `objectql-strategy-boolean-filter.test.ts` — the mock engine filters/buckets in-memory rows by **strict `===`** (so a stringified `1` fails it):
- `{ is_critical: true }` → real boolean reaches the engine, count is non-zero (3);
- `{ is_critical: false }` → matches its rows (2);
- group-by on a boolean dimension → produces **both** `true` (3) and `false` (2) buckets.

Full service-analytics suite (154 tests) passes; package builds clean.

> Context: discovered while building an ObjectStack dashboard; the downstream project worked around it with a numeric-range filter + string mirror field. This is the real fix in framework.

- ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` dates parsed in addition to legacy M/D, **both stored at UTC noon** so ET day-bucketing in `/today` stays correct.
- The JSON-rows import path (`normalizeRowKeys`) reuses the same `canonHeader` recognition and now detects format from the row keys (no second table to drift).
- **How verified:** unit tests parse real-shaped Notion/Google/field-tracker CSVs; a smoke script round-trips a Notion CSV with interleaved `" 1".." 3"` junk columns.

### 2. Status / temperature vocabulary → stage (+ tag)
`mapStatus` maps the owner's exact Notion Status values and keeps the segment as a tag:
| Status | stage | tag |
|---|---|---|
| Hot (Clients) | customer | hot |
| Won Orders | won | won |
| Orders In Progress | customer | in-progress |
| Warm (Leads) | contacted | warm |
| Room Temp (Opportunities) | contacted | room-temp |
| Cold (Prospects) | lead | cold |
| Lost Orders | dormant | lost |
| Meta Ad Conversions | lead | meta-ad |

Loose sheet words (hot/warm/cold/opportunity, bare "lost") also map. The negation guard is preserved ("won't reorder"→lost), and a sale/order word beats a bare temperature word in free text ("won - was hot"→won). Engagement Level→tag (eng-high/…). Raw status is preserved in the single import log line.

### 3. Smart stage from ORDERS — "has an order so it's not a lead"
- On import, a row with an **Order Number** / a real **Order Status**, OR a company that already has **≥1 linked Order** (batched lookup), is a **customer**. `promoteStage` moves UP the funnel only and refuses to touch lost/dormant — won stays won, a deliberately-closed deal is never resurrected, no won→customer regression.
- `scripts/promoteCustomersWithOrders.js`: **one-time, manual, idempotent** backfill. Promotes lead/contacted→customer for order-bearing records; never touches won/lost/dormant/archived; `--dry-run` writes nothing. Not run on boot.
  - Run: `node scripts/promoteCustomersWithOrders.js` (or `--dry-run` to preview).
- `isCustomer (orders>0)` returned on `/:companyKey`, `/today`, `/pipeline`; `/dashboard` returns `customersWithOrders` (authoritative customer count from order reality).

### 4. Delete a single note / log entry
- `LogEntrySchema` entries now carry an `_id` (the `{ _id:false }` was removed). `DELETE /api/crm/:companyKey/log/:entryId` removes one entry by id, with a **delete-by-index fallback** for legacy id-less entries. Log dedup (by kind+dedupKey) and rendering are unchanged; no migration needed.

### 5. Archive-from-card
- `POST /api/crm/:companyKey/archive` and `/unarchive` — soft, reversible, single-card. Never hard-deletes; keeps the record + its order links + history. Archived cards drop out of today/dashboard/pipeline/calendar/list via the existing `NOT_ARCHIVED` filter.

### 6. Drop "Area", add exact address
- New `Client.address` (exact street address) surfaced on the company payloads + `PATCHABLE`. `area` kept in the schema for back-compat (stored regions preserved); the importer maps an Address column when present.

### 7. Search everyone at any stage, including contacts
- `searchOr` makes `?q=` a **global search** across companyName/clientName/companyKey/email/phone/tags AND contacts (name/email/phone) — at ANY stage (stage/tag filters are ignored when a query is present). Applied to `/list` and `/pipeline`. Regex input is escaped; a numeric query also matches a digits-only phone.

### 8. Audit the dashboard numbers
- `/dashboard` now selects `tags`, enabling the heads-up engine to **down-rank cold / never-worked leads** (a bare cold/meta-ad lead with nothing scheduled no longer floods the "needs attention" feed; overdue/hot items still always surface). Added `customersWithOrders` for reconciliation. Per-stage counts, follow-up buckets (overdue/dueToday/dueThisWeek on ET day boundaries), and touches7/30 verified to reconcile; archived excluded throughout.

### Replace-mode kept correct
`findReplaceable` sweeps any import provenance (field-tracker/notion/crm-sheet/import); `ownerTouched` ignores importer-generated temperature/engagement tags so a freshly imported, never-edited record stays replaceable.

## How verified
- `node --test` (full suite): **187/187 green**, including the pre-existing field-tracker, money/double-tax/order#-normalize, PO-engine, and clock tests (unchanged).
- New focused tests (`controllers/__tests__/crmImportV2.test.js`): format detection, exact-Notion + loose status→stage+tag, ISO date at UTC noon, order→customer promote-up-only, keep-cold/keep-lost vs field-tracker dead-skip, free-text sale-vs-temperature precedence, delete-log-entry (id + index fallback), global search $or, dashboard cold down-rank, import-tag-aware ownerTouched.
- End-to-end smoke script: multi-format CSV parse with junk columns, idempotent re-import (no duplicate log lines, owner reschedule survives), promote-up-only.
- Adversarial self-review by parallel reviewer agents; the three real findings (status precedence, dead-skip scope, JSON-path format detection) were fixed (commit `fed7fe9`).

## Risks / deferred
- Re-import idempotency, dedup, and soft-delete-only are all preserved; nothing is hard-deleted.
- A "thin" generic CSV (no fingerprint columns) carrying literal dead words like "no answer" is treated as a prospecting list and dead-skips — by design; the actual Notion/Google CRM sources are detected by their headers and keep cold/lost. The exact "Cold (Prospects)" / "Lost Orders" values aren't dead words, so they're kept regardless.
- The big CRM UX restyle is a separate later task; only small supporting frontend changes shipped (separate PR).
- `promoteCustomersWithOrders.js` is manual on purpose — run it once after the big import to reconcile stale stored stages.

body:
## Summary

Adds TY25 benchmark support for testing OpenAI GPT-5.5 on raw PDF tax inputs across all five TY25 jurisdictions: US, CA, IL, NY, and VA.

This PR also includes the first saved TY25 GPT-5.5 result set: 50 cases x 5 thinking levels, with model outputs and evaluation reports committed under `tax_calc_bench/ty25/results/`.

## What Changed

- Adds `--tax-year {ty25,ty24}`, defaulting the CLI to TY25 while keeping helper/API defaults backward-compatible with TY24.
- Adds a TY25-only model matrix: default TY25 runs use OpenAI `gpt-5.5` only, no tools.
- Supports TY25 thinking levels `lobotomized`/`none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, and `ultrathink`.
- Sends TY25 PDFs as raw OpenAI/LiteLLM `input_file` payloads, plus `remaining_data.json`; local PDF text extraction is not used.
- Adds jurisdiction-aware TY25 prompts that mirror the TY24 output style and list official form lines for:
  - Federal Form 1040
  - CA Form 540
  - IL Form IL-1040
  - NY Form IT-201
  - VA Form 760
- Adds TY25 scoring maps and XML extraction for all five jurisdictions, including attribute parsing, XPath sums, NY claimed-value handling, CA final total tax, Yonkers withholding, and US scoring parity with TY24 federal line count.
- Keeps TY24 behavior separate: the TY24 prompt module is renamed to `ty24_prompt.py`, TY24 discovery remains pinned for legacy helper calls, and TY24 result paths remain separate.
- Adds separate TY25 results/reporting paths under `tax_calc_bench/ty25/results`.
- Improves reporting with TY25 jurisdiction summaries split by model, thinking level, tools, and jurisdiction.
- Adds robustness around OpenAI response extraction, large-payload timeout/streaming behavior, invalid test names, and TY25 model/tool restrictions.
- Adds TY25 payload audit support and broad TY25 test coverage.

author: irieo
body:
Closes # (if applicable).

## Changes proposed in this Pull Request

I wanted to reply in #1735 and thus dived again into research papers on the fictitious objective topic (seminal work by [Slade 1994](https://www.jstor.org/stable/2950588) and [Hobbs 2001](https://hobbsgroup.johnshopkins.edu/docs/papers/IEEE_Hobbs_2001_LCP00918286.pdf)); and I realized that my reference to Hobbs paper in #1570 wasn't fully correct. This PR fixes wrong line in one markdown cell of the notebook example.

Summary: 
- *wrong take*: one of conditions for the existence of a fictitious objective is that there is no binding network constraints that create asymmetric shadow prices across strategic players. -> It is incorrect since the three-bus example in Section V of the paper actually solves the network case where the congestion is binding. That equilibrium is still the solution to the single QP.  So the binding network constraints with nonzero shadow prices do not destroy the fictitious objective.
- *correct take*: one of conditions for the existence of a fictitious objective is that players treat transmission prices as fixed (the player's perceived derivative of the transmission shadow price with respect to its own output is zero), so congestion enters every player's problem as a linear term. 

Why this matters: since congested networks don't break the fictitious objective (but endogenous congestion-price conjectures do), the fictitious objective formulation can scale to large transmission constrained systems. 

## Checklist

- [x] PR description is written by me. Any potentially verbose AI-generated content is marked (see [Contributing guidelines](https://docs.pypsa.org/latest/contributing/contributing/)).
- [x] I consent to the release of this PR's code under the MIT license.

author: cho1409
body:
swapCards() read the slot filenames with getStringValue(), which only looks at the current settings layer. In per-game settings, cards assigned only at the global level aren't present in that layer, so the swap bailed out with "Both slots must have a card selected to swap." even though the slots show cards.

Read the effective values (the same ones the slot widgets display) so the swap works against globally-assigned cards too.

Fixes #10723

### Description of Changes
swapCards() read the slot filenames with getStringValue(), which only looks at the current settings layer. In per-game settings, cards assigned only at the global level aren't present in that layer, so the swap bailed out with "Both slots must have a card selected to swap." even though the slot widgets clearly show cards. The swap now reads the effective values via getEffectiveStringValue() — the same source the slot widgets use to display — so it works against globally-assigned cards too.

### Rationale behind Changes
The display path (refresh()) already uses getEffectiveStringValue() (per-game override → global → default), which is why the cards appear in the per-game view. The swap path was the lone spot still reading only the per-game layer, producing a confusing error. Routing it through the same effective lookup makes the two consistent and lets users rearrange globally-assigned cards at the per-game level ([#10723](https://github.com/PCSX2/pcsx2/issues/10723)).

### Suggested Testing Steps

1. Create and format two memory cards.
2. Assign both in global settings (Slot 1 / Slot 2).
3. Open a game's per-game memory card settings (don't override anything).
4. Click Swap Memory Cards.
5. Before: error "Both slots must have a card selected to swap." After: the two cards swap (saved as per-game overrides).
6. Confirm swapping in global settings still works as before.

### Did you use AI to help find, test, or implement this issue or feature?
Yes — AI assistance was used to trace the root cause (getStringValue vs getEffectiveStringValue) and to build-validate the change locally (clang-17, Qt 6.11.1) replicating the Linux/Qt CI. The fix mirrors the existing display logic and I can explain the reasoning in full.

## Summary
Opt-in `[codegen] enum_metadata = true` feature that surfaces scalar custom options attached to enum values (`extend google.protobuf.EnumValueOptions`) as a type-stable `enum_metadata(value)::NamedTuple` accessor in the generated Julia.

This branch also fixes a scoping bug found in downstream use ([ToolpathPackages#7449](https://github.com/toolpath/ToolpathPackages/pull/7449)): the metadata schema is **universe-wide**, so it became non-empty as soon as *any* proto file declared such an extension — causing **every** enum in the run to emit a default-filled `enum_metadata` method, even enums whose own values set no options.

## Fix
`_emit_enum_metadata` now gates per-enum:
- enum sets one or more options → full default-filled `NamedTuple` (unchanged);
- enum sets none of the universe's options → type-stable empty accessor returning `(;)`;
- proto tree declares no such extension at all → no methods generated (`MethodError`), unchanged.

## Changes
- `src/codegen.jl`: per-enum gate in `_emit_enum_metadata`.
- `test/fixtures/proto/enum_meta.proto`: added an option-free `Shade` enum; regenerated `enum_meta.pb`.
- `test/test_enum_metadata.jl`: new testset for the empty-NamedTuple accessor.
- `src/ProtocGen.jl` + `examples/enum_metadata/README.md`: docstring/notes updated.
- Bump version to 0.2.6.

body:
## Sprint 4 · #42 + #43 — Session continuity + durability close-out

Final Sprint 4 PR, landing the last two issues on top of #40 (persistence) and #41 (restore/reconcile/re-arm), both already merged. **Sprint 4 closes the durable orchestrator.**

### #42 — Opt-in session resume (`Closes #42`)
- Persists `session_id` additively on `RunAttempt`/`RetryEntry` at the **existing** #41 chokepoints (no new write sites); captured at `SessionStarted`.
- New config `persistence.resume_sessions: boolean`, **default `false`**. When off, restore forces `rec.sessionId = null` → **byte-identical to #41** (verified by an OFF regression test + re-running all #41 scenarios + a clean-`b494e83` baseline).
- When on, a restored continuation carries its persisted `session_id` and dispatches with `--resume`. **Self-healing**: a stale/expired session fails the worker → existing failure→fresh-redispatch path resets to a fresh turn against the on-disk workspace. No bespoke resumption code; one continuation-dispatch flow with a conditional arg.

### #43 — Tests + docs + close-out (`Closes #43`)
- **Stabilized the pre-existing #40 debounce flake** (`persistence.test.ts`, `TestClock`). Root cause was two real races: a sleep-registration race (writer not yet parked when the virtual clock advanced) and the dominant real-FS settle race (`fs.exists` observing before `rename` landed). Fixed test-only with a parked-writer barrier (`TestClock.sleeps()`) + a bounded real-FS poll — assertion strength unchanged. **Deterministic: 20/20 (dev) and an independent 12/12 full-suite loop (Producer).**
- **Coverage audit** — added the genuinely-missing slices only: additive-field (`turn`/`failure_attempts`/`session_id`/`kind`) survival through the real `save→load` round-trip, and a debounce-coalescing assertion (N mutations/window → exactly one flush). No duplication of existing restore/resume/corruption tests.
- **Docs**: README **Durability** section + `persistence` config table; `docs/sprint-4/done.md` handoff (pins the boot-ordering exactly-once invariant); `docs/sprint-4/progress.md` close record; `PROJECT_BRIEF` §7 row + §8 rewrite (durability shipped, stale "deferred" note removed).

### Gates
`typecheck 0 · lint 0 · build 0 · **291 tests** green` (deterministic). Snapshot stayed strictly additive (no `/api/v2`).

### Carry-forward (documented in done.md)
- Live-Copilot `--resume` honoring across downtime is unproven (default-off + self-healing by design; only the fake self-heal path is tested).
- Checkpoint/restore state isn't surfaced in the dashboard yet.
- Schema migration is V1-only (the `migrateToCurrent` seam awaits its first real bump).

Closes #42, Closes #43.

body: ## Summary Adds an on-screen preview overlay mode for `pii-stream watch` so users without a second monitor can see PII detection output directly on top of the screen being captured. The existing preview only opened a separate AppKit window that mirrored the captured frame and drew detection boxes inside it. That made the preview awkward or unusable for single-monitor setups because the preview occupied separate screen real estate instead of aligning with the actual content being guarded. ## Changes - Adds a `PreviewPresentation` mode with the existing window preview as the default and a new `overlay` presentation. - Adds CLI support for `--preview overlay` plus a convenience `--overlay` alias. - Wires the selected presentation through `WatchOptions` into `AppCoordinator` and `PreviewWindowController`. - In overlay mode, creates a transparent, borderless, click-through full-screen AppKit window above the screen. - Reuses the existing overlay layer drawing logic while skipping captured-frame rendering, so the real screen becomes the backdrop. - Keeps the existing window preview behavior unchanged by default. ## Validation - `swift build -c release` - `swift run pii-stream-checks` - `git diff --check` --- ## Summary by cubic Adds an on‑screen overlay preview to `pii-stream watch`, showing detection boxes directly on your screen. Overlay renders with no delay and never blacks out the whole screen, improving single‑monitor workflows while keeping the window preview as the default. - **New Features** - Preview modes: `--preview window|overlay` (default: `window`) and `--overlay` alias. - Overlay uses a transparent, borderless, click‑through, full‑screen window above all spaces. - Boxes map 1:1 to screen bounds; no captured‑frame rendering, no preview delay, and no blackout fallback. - **Refactors** - Added `PreviewPresentation` enum and a window factory to build `window` or `overlay` variants. - Propagated the selected presentation from CLI `WatchOptions` into `AppCoordinator` and `PreviewWindowController`. Written for commit d424c63d69b71cedef350aeb4239dd362fee9a51. Summary will update on new commits.

author: itbrmste
body: ## Summary Adds **`npm install` support for the BRMSTE edge / Cloudflare Workers code**. Until now the only Worker code in the org (`deploy/worker/index.ts` on the GSI branch) was pure TypeScript with **no `package.json`** — CI just did a global `npm install -g wrangler`. There was no lockfile, no Worker types, no type-check, and no tests. This PR introduces a self-contained, reproducible **`edge/`** Cloudflare Workers project where the entire toolchain is a local dev dependency, so the edge builds, type-checks, tests (inside `workerd`), and deploys from a single `npm install`. ### What's included - **`edge/package.json` + `edge/package-lock.json`** — pinned, reproducible toolchain (no global installs): - `wrangler@^4.104.0` (build / dev / deploy) - `@cloudflare/workers-types@^4.20260624.1` (runtime types) - `typescript@^6.0.3` (`tsc --noEmit`) - `vitest@^4.1.9` + `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers@^0.16.19` (tests run **inside** `workerd`) - scripts: `dev`, `typecheck`, `test`, `deploy:dry`, `deploy`, `cf-typegen` - **`edge/src/index.ts`** — typed `Env`, HSTS + security headers on every response, additive routing, `404` default (never claims the domain root). - **`edge/wrangler.toml`** — Wrangler v4 config; `vars` + **additive** production routes (`brmste.com/edge/*`, `…/substrate/edge.json`, same for `brmste.ai`). - **`edge/tsconfig.json`** — strict TS against `@cloudflare/workers-types`. - **`edge/vitest.config.ts` + `edge/test/worker.test.ts`** — 6 runtime tests via `SELF.fetch` in the Workers pool. - **`.github/workflows/edge-ci.yml`** — `gate → npm ci → typecheck → test (workerd) → wrangler dry-run build` on Node 22, plus a credential-guarded `npm run deploy` job on push to `main`. - **`scripts/git-worker-brand-patent-gate.sh`** — logo-URL scan now skips `node_modules`/`.wrangler`/`dist` so the brand+patent gate still passes after `npm install` (additive excludes only — cannot mask a real violation). ## Testing **GitHub Actions `edge-ci.yml` is green** on the PR ([run 28103707036](https://github.com/BRMSTE-SB/.github/actions/runs/28103707036)): Brand & Patent Gate and `npm ci → typecheck → test (workerd) → wrangler dry-run build` both pass. The deploy job is intentionally skipped on PRs (runs only on push to `main`, when CF creds exist). Local pipeline (`node v22.14.0` · `npm 10.9.7`): - `npm ci` — 0 vulnerabilities, reproducible from the lockfile - `npm run typecheck` — `tsc --noEmit` clean - `npm test` — **6/6** passing inside the Workers runtime (`workerd`) - `npm run deploy:dry` — `wrangler deploy --env production --dry-run` builds a 5.86 KiB Worker bundle - `wrangler dev` (live `workerd`) — every surface verified with `curl`: `/healthz`, `/substrate/edge.json`, `/substrate/patent-enforcement.json`, `/` (HTML), `404` for unknown paths, and the HTTP→HTTPS `301` with HSTS - Brand + patent gate passes both lanes on a clean checkout **and** with `node_modules` present > Note: a first CI run surfaced that **Wrangler v4 requires Node ≥ 22** (the dry-run step failed on Node 20 while typecheck/tests passed); fixed by pinning CI + `engines` to Node 22. ## Notes - Self-contained: the Worker performs no required upstream calls, so it type-checks, tests offline, and deploys deterministically. - No secrets committed — `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` / `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` come from `CF_API_TOKEN` / `CF_ACCOUNT_ID` Actions secrets (see `SECURITY.md`). BRMSTE LTD · Companies House 15310393 · GB2607860 · PCT/GB2026/050406 CURSOR NEVER SIGNS · OPERATOR NEVER SIGNS · EDGE SIGNS · JUDGMENT SIGNS

author: elyxlz
body:
## What

Brings the agent back to the official **Claude Agent SDK** (`claude-agent-sdk`), which `core/` used before #623. cc_sdk was deliberately built as a drop-in for the SDK's public surface, so this is mostly an import flip (`core.cc_sdk` → `claude_agent_sdk`) plus a few fixups. **cc_sdk is kept in the tree, dormant**, as a ready alternative driver.

## How it works now

- **Imports flipped** in the 6 consumer files (`client.py`, `loops.py`, `models.py`, `tools.py`, `config.py`, `sdk_parsing.py`). cc_sdk's directory is untouched.
- **Options**: dropped the three cc_sdk-only fields (`max_context_tokens`, `context_window`, `expanded_context_window`). The official `ClaudeSDKClient.get_context_usage()` returns the same `{percentage, totalTokens, maxTokens}` shape, so context-usage logging is unchanged; the OpenRouter window + 1M beta still flow via `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS` env + `betas` (both native to the official options).
- **cc_sdk-only client members** (`is_alive()`, `session_id`, `compact()`) are guarded with `try/except AttributeError` at their three call sites so the watchdog, error-path session-id capture, and dreamer compaction degrade gracefully on the headless SDK (sanctioned over the banned `getattr`).
- **Removed tmux-coupled features** that can't work on the headless SDK: the diagnostics **pane-tail** and the **`vestad attach`** command (+ their tests).
- **Image**: no longer pins/symlinks a `claude` binary — the SDK resolves its own bundled Claude Code CLI. `tmux` stays installed so cc_sdk remains runnable if reactivated.

## cc_sdk stays — leave it alone

Nothing in `core/` imports it. It's retained as a drop-in CLI-driving alternative; `CLAUDE.md` and `agent/core/cc_sdk/README.md` both say not to delete/refactor/rewire it without an explicit ask. Its transport tests (`test_cc_sdk`, `test_e2e_transport`, `test_stop_race`) still run and keep it healthy.

## Verification

- `./check.sh agent` — green (321 passed; the 3 removed tests are the pane-tail ones).
- `./check.sh vestad` — green (133 passed; `attach` command + tests removed).
- Official-SDK surface parity confirmed by introspecting `claude-agent-sdk` 0.2.108: every top-level name and `types` symbol `core/` imports is present, `ClaudeAgentOptions` has `betas`/`env`/`skills`/`setting_sources`/`stderr`/`can_use_tool`, and `ClaudeSDKClient.get_context_usage()` exists.
- The real interactive contract (transcript/hooks/MCP over a live agent) is gated by the release-only `test-live` e2e, as before.

## Fleet impact

No on-disk state or config format change, so **no migration**. `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` are bind-mounted into agents and `uv sync --frozen` runs at boot (`docker.rs`), so existing fleet agents install `claude-agent-sdk` on their next restart.

## Risk note

The SDK relies on its bundled Claude Code CLI being present/arch-correct in the container; the release `test-live` job boots a real agent from the freshly built image and gates publishing, which is the backstop here.

author: handys11
body:
## Goal

Cut the SonarQube duplication that remained after PR #25. Live baseline at branch start: **4.4% duplication / 754 dup-lines across 20 files**, of which **~51% was localization**. SonarQube flagged each per-feature catalog because its `["en"] = {…}` block and `["fr"] = {…}` block share an identical key sequence (e.g. `CommandLocalizationCatalog` was 94% duplicated). A `.resx` model removes that twinning — each language is its own file with no repeated C# dictionary syntax — and makes **adding a language a one-file drop**.

## What changed

### Localization (the main event)
- **Deleted** 6 × `*LocalizationCatalog`, 6 × `*Localizer`, 6 × `I*Localizer` marker interfaces, and `DictionaryLocalizer`.
- **Added** one flat shared resource set — `Strings.resx` (English/neutral) + `Strings.fr.resx` — holding all **193 keys** (prefix-namespaced, globally unique across the old catalogs), in `RustPlusBot.Localization`.
- **`ResxLocalizer : ILocalizer`** resolves per-call culture via `ResourceManager.GetString(key, culture)` — preserving the exact prior contract: requested culture → English fallback → key itself if missing; the format overload uses the requested culture's format provider. Culture stays a **per-call parameter** (this bot serves many Discord servers, each with its own language), so no `Thread.CurrentCulture`.
- All ~44 injection sites now inject the single `RustPlusBot.Localization.ILocalizer`; one idempotent `AddRustPlusBotLocalization()` (`TryAddSingleton`) replaces 6 DI registrations.
- The resx values were **generated programmatically from the old catalogs by reflection**, so emoji (⚡ ⭘ ⚠️ 🚨), accented French, and `{0}` placeholders are byte-exact. An `en/fr` parity test + key-count guard prevent future drift.

### Quick-win
- `MarkerReply.For(…)` shared by the `cargo`/`heli`/`chinook` command handlers (they differed only in `MarkerKind` + key prefix), mirroring the existing `RigReply` pattern.

### Pre-task: editorconfig hardening fallout
The `.editorconfig` hardening (style rules `suggestion`→`warning`) surfaced 5 latent violations under `TreatWarningsAsErrors`. Fixed 3 cleanly (IDE0028, IDE0130, IDE0060); the other 2 are documented line-level suppressions because their "fixes" conflict with other enabled analyzers (IDE0045 ↔ RCS1238/S3358 nested-ternary; IDE0290 ↔ CA2000 on a `CancellationTokenSource`).

## Deliberately not done
- A shared base for `CommandsHostedService` + `PlayersHostedService` was **skipped**: their only common project is the dependency-free `RustPlusBot.Abstractions`, and a base there would force hosting/logging deps onto the foundational project — not worth the coupling for ~30 boilerplate lines, and the two services differ in real per-event behavior.
- Switch/Alarm device symmetry left untouched (separate features; abstracting only to satisfy a metric would add coupling).

## Verification
- Build: **0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- Tests: **514 passing** across 13 assemblies (down from 531 only because 23 now-redundant catalog/localizer test classes were removed; the shared `ResxLocalizerTests` + parity tests replace them).
- `dotnet jb cleanupcode --profile=ReformatAndReorder` leaves zero diff.
- Behavioral equivalence (old catalog values vs new resx) verified across all 6 features in both cultures — 0 mismatches.

author: jesrey0
body:
## Summary

Adds buffered SSE streaming support to `POST /v1/chat/completions`. Currently the endpoint rejects any request with `stream=true` (returns HTTP 400 `"Streaming is not supported. Set stream=false or omit it."`), which blocks every modern OpenAI-compatible client that defaults to streaming — including the official `openai` Python SDK, `openai-node`, LangChain, LiteLLM, OpenWebUI, and most agentic CLIs. Many of these clients silently swallow the 400 and just produce empty output, which is hard to debug.

## Approach

This is **fake / buffered** streaming, not real token-by-token streaming. The browser backend can't emit incremental tokens (turn completion is detected by polling the copy button, not by intercepting upstream tokens), so the existing blocking chat handler runs unchanged, and the buffered response is then fanned out as a sequence of `chat.completion.chunk` SSE events that conform to the OpenAI contract.

This mirrors the existing fake-streaming pattern in `_stream_response_events` for the Responses API (`src/api/openai_routes.py` lines 1081-1230) so the codebase stays consistent — same architectural choice, applied to the chat-completions endpoint.

## Chunk sequence

1. Opening chunk with `delta.role = "assistant"` (no content yet)
2. Body, one of:
   - For text responses: word-sized content chunks with a 10ms inter-chunk delay so SDK consumers see progressive output
   - For tool-call responses: a single chunk carrying `delta.tool_calls = [...]` (no point chunking JSON arguments)
3. Final chunk with empty delta and the appropriate `finish_reason`
4. Literal `data: [DONE]\n\n` terminator

`id`, `created`, and `model` are stable across all chunks for a given response.

## Changes

- `src/api/openai_schemas.py` — adds `ChoiceDelta`, `ChoiceChunk`, `ChatCompletionChunk` Pydantic models matching the OpenAI `chat.completion.chunk` contract.
- `src/api/openai_routes.py`:
  - Adds `_stream_chat_completion_chunks(response)` async generator that fans the buffered response into SSE.
  - Removes the early 400 rejection in `create_chat_completion` and adds a conditional `StreamingResponse` branch at the end of the handler.
  - Drops `response_model=ChatCompletionResponse` on the decorator since the return type is now a union with `StreamingResponse`.

Existing non-streaming behavior is unchanged.

## Testing

Verified locally against the ChatGPT provider with the bundled `.env` defaults:

**`curl` with `stream=true`** — returns 4 well-formed SSE chunks for a one-word reply:
```
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":...,"model":"catgpt-browser","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":null,"tool_calls":null},"finish_reason":null}]}

data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","...,"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":null,"content":"ok","tool_calls":null},"finish_reason":null}]}

data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","...,"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":null,"content":null,"tool_calls":null},"finish_reason":"stop"}]}

data: [DONE]
```

**`curl` with `stream=false`** — unchanged; returns the same `ChatCompletionResponse` as before.

**End-to-end client test** — a CLI that uses the openai-completions adapter with `stream=True` as default successfully round-trips against the gateway and renders the response correctly. Previously these requests hit the 400 and silently produced empty output.

## Notes for reviewer

- The 10ms inter-chunk delay is intentional — purely cosmetic, to give consumers a visibly progressive output rather than dumping everything at once. It's a defaults choice and easy to tune later.
- I considered putting the helper in a separate `streaming.py` module but kept it co-located with the existing `_stream_response_events` for the Responses API, so both fake-streamers live next to each other and follow the same pattern. Happy to refactor either way.
- This PR does not address real token streaming (which would require either intercepting the upstream SSE response in `chatgpt/client.py` or watching DOM mutations during generation — both are real changes that belong in separate PRs).

author: bluecarbons
body:
## Security & Correctness Audit — June 2026

Full line-by-line audit of all source files. 6 files changed, 16 issues resolved.

---

### 🔴 Critical / Security

#### `src/core/http.js` — OOM via unbounded response body
- **Before:** `response.text()` was called with no size check. A malicious feed server returning 500 MB would exhaust Node.js heap.
- **After:** 5 MB hard cap enforced via `Content-Length` header (fast path) **and** after `response.text()` (covers chunked/streaming). Throws `Error: Feed response too large` before buffering.

#### `src/adapters/provider.js` — Prompt injection from crafted feed content
- **Before:** `item.title` and `item.contentSnippet` were interpolated raw into LLM prompts. A feed with `\nAssistant: ignore all previous instructions` in the title could hijack the LLM context.
- **After:** New `sanitizeForPrompt(str, maxLen)` strips ASCII control characters (`\x00–\x1F`), collapses newlines to spaces, and hard-caps at 500/2000/3000/500 chars per field. Injection of role-boundary sequences is blocked.

#### `src/adapters/provider.js` — Empty API key sent silently
- **Before:** When `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` were unset, an empty string was sent as `Bearer ` — producing a cryptic 401 with no actionable message.
- **After:** Explicit guard throws `Error: OpenAI API key is required. Set OPENAI_API_KEY env var or pass config.apiKey.` before any network call.

#### `src/adapters/provider.js` — Provider allowlist enforcement
- **Before:** Unknown provider strings reached internal dispatch; `createAnalyzer` threw only at the very end after other logic ran.
- **After:** `SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS` Set checked immediately at entry; unknown values throw before any env-var access or network call.

#### `src/mcp/server.js` — Untrusted MCP caller can supply arbitrary provider string
- **Before:** `args.provider` from an untrusted MCP caller was passed directly to `createAnalyzer` with no validation in the server layer.
- **After:** `ALLOWED_PROVIDERS` Set validated in `handleToolCall` before the value reaches `createAnalyzer`. Returns JSON-RPC `-32602 Invalid params` for any unrecognised value.

---

### 🟠 Correctness

#### `src/parser.js` — Deduplication broken by `crypto.randomUUID()` fallback
- **Before:** Items with no link/guid/title/pubDate got a fresh UUID as their `idSource` on every run. The same item was re-processed every execution, defeating the SQLite dedup layer entirely.
- **After:** UUID fallback replaced with `''` (empty string). ID is now deterministic (`sha256(feedUrl + ':')`) for blank items, making dedup stable across runs.

#### `src/adapters/provider.js` — Uncaught TypeError on empty `choices`/`content` arrays
- **Before:** `resData.choices[0].message.content` and `resData.content[0].text` threw uncaught TypeErrors when an LLM returned an empty array (rate-limit or refusal response).
- **After:** Explicit array-length guards throw descriptive errors before indexing.

#### `src/cli.js` — `--feed`/`--db` flags with no value silently misbehaved
- **Before:** `argv[++i]` could capture the next flag name as the feed URL, or be `undefined`, causing `resolve(undefined)` and confusing downstream errors.
- **After:** Each flag validates that the next token exists and does not start with `--`; exits with a clear error message if violated.

#### `src/core/parser.js` — `isoDate` was raw `pubDate` string, not ISO 8601
- **Before:** `isoDate` was set to the raw RFC 2822 string (e.g. `"Mon, 23 Jun 2026 12:00:00 +0000"`). Consumers that rely on `isoDate` for date parsing received unparseable strings.
- **After:** New `safeIsoDate()` helper runs `new Date(raw).toISOString()`, falling back to the raw string only if parsing fails (non-standard feed formats).

---

### 🟡 Coherence

#### `src/core/parser.js` — `contentSnippet` double-assignment
- **Before:** `contentSnippet` was set in the initial `normalized` object literal, then silently clobbered by an unconditional reassignment 10 lines later. The first assignment was dead code.
- **After:** Single assignment in the object literal. Removed redundant overwrite.

#### `src/core/parser.js` — XSS surface in `stripHtml`
- **Before:** `<form>`, `<embed>` blocks were not in the strip list. These can carry `onsubmit=`, `src=javascript:` vectors if `contentSnippet` is ever rendered as HTML by a downstream consumer.
- **After:** `<form>…</form>` and `<embed>…</embed>` added to the block-removal pass before the generic tag strip.

---

### Files Changed
| File | Changes |
|---|---|
| `src/core/http.js` | +5 MB response body size cap |
| `src/core/parser.js` | +XSS tags, +`safeIsoDate`, -double `contentSnippet` |
| `src/adapters/provider.js` | +`sanitizeForPrompt`, +empty-key guards, +array guards, +provider allowlist |
| `src/mcp/server.js` | +`ALLOWED_PROVIDERS` validation, +`limit` upper bound |
| `src/parser.js` | -`crypto.randomUUID()` dedup regression |
| `src/cli.js` | +flag argument validation |

## Description of Change

This pull request adds comprehensive validation tests for Ethernet, networking, and TLS/HTTP client functionality on ESP32 platforms. It introduces new test suites (with Arduino and Unity test code), test drivers, configuration files, and documentation to ensure robust automated validation of networking features in CI. The tests cover link/IP acquisition, TCP/UDP/mDNS/DNS, and secure HTTP client scenarios, and are designed for hardware runners with appropriate requirements and serial protocols for test automation.

**Ethernet Validation Tests**
- Added `ethernet.ino` implementing tests for Ethernet link status, DHCP/static IP, MAC address, link speed, gateway/subnet/DNS, DNS resolution, TCP connectivity, and static IP configuration.
- Added pytest driver `test_ethernet.py` to automate Unity test execution.
- Added test configuration `ci.yml` (tags, runner requirements, disables Wokwi/QEMU).
- Added detailed documentation in `README.md`.

**WiFi Networking Validation Tests**
- Added `networking.ino` with tests for WiFi-based DNS, TCP/UDP client/server, mDNS, and captive DNS server, using a serial protocol for credentials.
- Added pytest driver `test_networking.py` to automate test execution and credential passing.
- Added test configuration `ci.yml` (runner tags, SoC requirements, disables QEMU/unsupported hardware).
- Added documentation in `README.md` describing test cases, requirements, and serial protocol.

**TLS/HTTP Client Validation Tests**
- Added documentation in `README.md` for TLS/HTTP test suite, describing test cases, requirements, and serial protocol for CA certificate transfer.
- Added test configuration `ci.yml` (runner tags, disables QEMU/unsupported hardware/SoCs).

author: yyyyyyyan
body:
## Summary

Migrates the `dipper` plugin from the registry's legacy-synthesis fallback to an explicit declarative `BaseApp` definition, as part of the App Framework epic (Wave 3). This is a pure registration-mechanism change with a **byte-identical no-op** on the `dipper` OpenAPI and plugin-schema snapshots.

- **New `app/sep/plugins/dipper/app.py`** — a plain `BaseApp` carrying the existing hand-written JSON `api_router` (`api_routes.router`) and the deprecated Jinja `jinja_router` (`routes.router`) **unchanged**. Metadata (`display_name`, `uri_path`, `css_class`, `nav_order`) mirrors the bespoke `report`/`backup_mongo` definitions.
- **`app/sep/plugins/dipper/__init__.py`** — now exports `app` alongside the preserved `router` re-export (`__all__ = ["app", "router"]`), so the registry binds the explicit definition instead of synthesizing one.
- **`tests/app/sep/plugins/framework/test_registry.py`** — adds `dipper` to the bespoke-`BaseApp` parametrized coverage (and the schemaless list), and repoints five generic legacy-synthesis tests off the now-migrated `dipper` onto the still-legacy `alters` plugin (see *Bundled change* below).
- **`tests/app/sep/api/test_router.py`** — repoints seven config-driven-mount-loop tests off `dipper` onto `alters` for the same reason (see *Bundled change* below).

No model, schema, route, settings, or static-mount change. The registry produces an identical `key`, `api_router` object, mount prefix/tag, per-route dependencies, and operationIds whether `dipper` is legacy-synthesized or bound from the explicit definition — hence the snapshot no-op.

### Design note — declarative `BaseApp`, not `TaskExecutionApp`

The original ticket described wiring `dipper` as a `TaskExecutionApp` backed by a filename-keyed `ScriptSource` adapter. That mechanism is incompatible with the byte-identical-no-op requirement: `dipper`'s HTTP surface is **service-keyed** — `(service_id, collector_type)` resolves the collector script and injects PMM args **server-side** — whereas the framework's `ScriptSource` seam derives a **fixed filename-keyed** route set (`POST /snippet/execute`, `GET /snippet/schema`, `GET /snippet/history`) with no suppression flag. Adopting it would add `/snippet/*` paths `dipper` doesn't have, remove the root `POST /` execute, and change `GET /`'s response schema. A plain `BaseApp` derives **zero** routes and mounts the hand-written `api_router` verbatim, so it reproduces the exact surface. This follows the `backup_mongo`/`inventory`/`report` bespoke-`BaseApp` precedent. The reporter approved this deviation during planning.

### Acceptance-criteria remap

The ticket's ACs were written for the `TaskExecutionApp` mechanism. Under the approved `BaseApp` approach:

- **Met:** OpenAPI snapshot no-op; plugin-schema snapshot no-op; host resolvers stay app-local; `models.py`/`schema.py`/`constants.py` untouched; auth posture preserved (`POST /` remains the only state-changing route). *(checked in Jira)*
- **Substance met via a different mechanism (left unchecked):** `form-schema`/`script-preview` are preserved **exactly** (they stay in the hand-written `api_router` — there is no `extra_routes` mechanism on a `BaseApp`, which is stronger than carrying them as `extra_routes`). The registry still discovers `dipper` under key `dipper`, but as a `BaseApp` (no `script_source.py`).
- **Deferred / not applicable (left unchecked):** the `StaticMount` seam + `main.py` mount removal is W4-B scope (no `StaticMount` field exists; the `/static/dipper` mount is left in place — see *Known limitations*); no `test_script_source.py` (no `ScriptSource` hooks exist).

Recommend updating ticket ACs #1, #4, #5, #7, #9 to the `BaseApp` framing.

### Bundled change

Twelve generic registry/router unit tests used `dipper` as a concrete legacy-synthesis fixture: five in `test_registry.py` (`TestLegacyWrapping`/`TestFailFast`) and seven in `test_router.py` (`TestApiRouterConfigDrivenLoop`). Because `dipper` is no longer legacy-synthesized, those tests are repointed onto `alters` (a still-legacy plugin with the same structural shape — five hand-written API routes). This is a necessary mechanical consequence of the migration — the same repoint a prior `BaseApp` migration made (`inventory` → `snippets`) — not an unrelated behavior change. Two of the `test_router.py` tests still passed against the migrated `dipper` (it mounts either way) but had silently stopped exercising the config-driven `api_router_path` path the class exists to test; repointing them restores that coverage. Real-app and convention tests that legitimately reference `dipper` are left unchanged.

author: mideastscout
body:
## Problem

`briefing.json` refreshed server-side at 16:42 IDT (after the self-heal retry caught the recovered Gemini API), but the live site kept showing the old **06:26** timestamp. Cause: the briefing panel re-fetches in the browser only **every 6 hours**, while headlines/pulse/trends poll every 30 min:

```js
setInterval(loadBriefing, 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000);  // 6 hours
```

So an open tab won't show a new briefing for up to 6h. And now that the briefing can land **off** the 6-hour grid (e.g. a noon slot that only succeeds at 16:42 after a Gemini outage), a 6-hour client poll is guaranteed to miss it.

## Fix

Poll `loadBriefing` every 30 min, matching the other panels. `briefing.json` is tiny and already fetched cache-busted (`?t=…`, `no-store`), so this is cheap and an unchanged briefing just re-renders identically.

author: ggozad
body:
When a skill agent reaches its own request limit, run_skill now makes one
  tool-less completion seeded with the gathered message history instead of
  letting the failure propagate as a null. Gated by Skill.force_final_answer
  (default True).

  The limit is enforced by a per-agent _RequestLimitGuard capability that
  raises a private _SkillRequestLimitReached (a UsageLimitExceeded subclass),
  so a UsageLimitExceeded raised by a nested skill tool stays a real failure
  rather than being converted into a forced answer. History is captured in the
  same capability hook, keeping agent.run() and its AG-UI event streaming
  intact; mixed ExceptionGroups re-raise real sibling failures.

author: dudarenok-maker
body:
## Summary

Implements **fs-53** — automatic, language-aware text normalisation at the TTS boundary, so numbers, dates, currency, symbols, and a curated abbreviation set are spoken correctly instead of read literally (`$1,200` → "one thousand two hundred dollars", `1999` → "nineteen ninety-nine", `50%` → "fifty percent", `Dr.` → "Doctor").

Built spec-first (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-24-fs53-text-normalisation-design.md`, 3 adversarial review rounds) and plan-first (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-24-fs53-text-normalisation.md`, 2 adversarial review rounds), then executed task-by-task with per-task review.

### User-visible
- **Numbers/dates/currency/symbols/abbreviations are now spoken correctly** in generated audio for **English, Spanish, and Russian** books (the `supported:true` languages). French and German engines ship **fully implemented and unit-tested but dormant** — they activate automatically the moment their fs-50 `supported` flag flips, with no further work.
- **Russian raised floor**: years read as ordinals with correct case for the closed set of year-governing prepositions (в…году prepositional, с/до/от/после…года genitive, к…году dative); dates as neuter-ordinal day + genitive month (`3 января` → "третье января"); currency 1/2–4/5+ agreement (рубль/рубля/рублей); a 1/2 gender heuristic (один/одна, два/две).
- **Always-on, invisible**: the original manuscript text is never mutated — captions, the manuscript view, and quote-audit still show the written form. No new setting/toggle.

### Operator-visible
- **ASR content-QA gate stays aligned** (the load-bearing fix): the per-sentence WER gate is now fed the same fs-53-normalised, spoken-form text the audio was synthesised from, so expanded numbers no longer trigger false-positive `drift` / wasted re-records / spurious `asrSuspect`. This also sidesteps the non-English number-WER gap (#1084) by pre-spelling the numbers.

### Dev-visible
- New `server/src/tts/normalize/` module: `expandForSpeech(text, langCode)` composed of a shared locale-aware classifier layer (`classifiers.ts` + `index.ts`) plus five per-language engines (`lang/{en,es,ru,fr,de}.ts`) behind a `LangNormalizer` interface. `expandForSpeech` self-gates on `isSupportedLanguage` + a registered engine.
- `normaliseForTts(text)` gains an optional `langCode` 2nd arg; the no-`langCode` path is byte-identical to today (zero regression). `synthesiseChapter` threads `bookLanguage` into every audio-producing call, the batch-length key, and the ASR-QA expected text.
- Per-language `__fixtures__/*.txt` regression sets; 156 normalize-module tests.

### Scope note
Landed as **server-only** — the issue's Full-stack label anticipated a per-book toggle, but the design locked **always-on / no toggle / invisible**, so there is no frontend surface.

Regression plan: `docs/features/230-fs53-text-normalisation.md`. Known limitations (year-frame false positives, RU paucal gender, numeric-only dates, ISO currency codes, signed numbers, etc.) are enumerated there and in the spec.

## Test plan
- `npm run verify` (typecheck + all tests + e2e + e2e:visual + build) — **green** locally.
- 156 normalize-module tests (`server/src/tts/normalize/**/*.test.ts`): per-engine unit tests + per-language fixture sets + the activation-gate / dormancy / NaN-guard tests.
- ASR-QA alignment regression test (`synthesise-chapter-asr.test.ts`): `$1,200` synthesised + matching spoken transcript yields `ok`, not `drift` (fails before the fix, passes after).
- No-`langCode` byte-identity guard in `text-normalize.test.ts`.
- Full server suite green (3522 passing) with the synth-pipeline threading.

Owed (not in this PR): on-box manual acceptance render of a Coalfall chapter with a seeded `$1,200 / 1999 / 50% / Dr.` line, per the regression plan's walkthrough.

Closes #976

author: edofic
body:
Adds Crossplane-managed resources for the SAP HANA Cloud JWT authentication stack, closing the gap that prevented operators from declaring IdP-backed human-login flows (e.g. SAP IAS) through this provider. Implements #136.

A typical IAS-to-HANA SSO setup is now five resources: `PublicKey`, `JWTProvider`, `PersonalSecurityEnvironment` (purpose `JWT`), `Role`, and a restricted `User` with a JWT identity. See `examples/jwtuser/jwt-sso.yaml`.

## Commits

The change is split into six reviewable units. Each builds and tests on its own.

1. **`feat(user): make client connect declarative for restricted users`**
   Adds `spec.forProvider.enableClientConnect` (default `true`) and surfaces `status.atProvider.isClientConnectEnabled`. Restricted users are created without `CLIENT CONNECT`; without it any external login fails with internal error `U04` and nothing in the HANA error message hints at the missing toggle. Also fixes a latent bug: `Create` used to call `ENABLE PASSWORD LIFETIME` on restricted users created without a password, which HANA rejects.

2. **`feat: add JWTProvider managed resource`**
   New `admin.hana.sap.crossplane.io/v1alpha1/JWTProvider` wrapping `CREATE/ALTER/DROP JWT PROVIDER`. Reconciles issuer URL, external-identity claim, case-insensitivity, priority (defaults to `100` to match HANA's implicit default), application-user claim mapping (`SET CLAIM '<c>' AS APPLICATION USER`), and `HAS MEMBER` claim filters. `Update` emits the exact `ALTER` clauses required for each drifted field so `isUpToDate` catches out-of-band drift in both directions.

3. **`feat: add PublicKey managed resource`**
   New `admin.hana.sap.crossplane.io/v1alpha1/PublicKey` wrapping `CREATE/DROP PUBLIC KEY`. `spec.forProvider.pem` is validated with `encoding/pem` (must be a PKIX `PUBLIC KEY` block, no trailing data) and marked immutable via `XValidation self==oldSelf`. HANA has no `ALTER` for key material and the PSE binds keys by name, so mutating the bytes in place would be silent trust-boundary drift; rotation must go through delete + recreate.

4. **`feat(pse): extend PersonalSecurityEnvironment to support JWT purpose`**
   Adds a `purpose` discriminator (`X509` or `JWT`, defaults to `X509` for backward compatibility), plus `jwtProviderRef` and `publicKeyRefs`. When `purpose: JWT`, the client emits `SET PSE ... PURPOSE JWT FOR PROVIDER` and `ALTER PSE ... ADD/DROP PUBLIC KEY`. Existing X509 manifests continue to work unchanged.

5. **`feat(user): add JWT identity mapping and IAS-to-HANA SSO example`**
   Adds `authentication.jwtProviders[]` (provider name or `providerRef` plus external identity). The reconciler drives `ALTER USER ... ENABLE/DISABLE JWT` and `ADD/DROP IDENTITY '<id>' FOR JWT PROVIDER`. Observation surfaces `IS_JWT_ENABLED` from `SYS.USERS` and `JWTProviders` from `SYS.JWT_USER_MAPPINGS`. Ships the SSO example and e2e test.

6. **`test(user): wait for observed privileges to match spec before diffing`**
   Fixes a test flake where the Observe assertion ran before the controller had finished propagating observed privileges into the status, causing spurious out-of-date diffs. - Mostly unrelated to the rest but e2e tests were failing.

## Key subtleties worth reviewer attention

- **providerRef resolution before drift comparison.** Spec-side `jwtProviders[]` entries using `providerRef` are resolved to the HANA-side `JWT_PROVIDER_NAME` in both `Observe` and `buildDesiredParameters` before any comparison against observed entries (which always carry the resolved name from `SYS.JWT_USER_MAPPINGS`). Without this, `isJWTMappingsUpToDate` would never match, and the controller would `DROP IDENTITY` + `ADD IDENTITY` on every reconcile, transiently breaking auth in the gap. Locked in by `TestResolveJWTProviderNames`.

- **`IS_JWT_ENABLED` resilience.** Older HANA builds don't expose the column. `queryJWTEnabled` treats scan-shape mismatches as `false` (not an error), so the controller still reconciles against those instances.

- **`CLIENT CONNECT` observation nullability.** `IS_CLIENT_CONNECT_ENABLED` is `sql.NullBool` for the same reason. When the column is absent, `isClientConnectUpToDate` treats state as up-to-date to avoid flapping.

- **DDL syntax verified empirically.** `CASE INSENSITIVE IDENTITY` and `SET CLAIM '<c>' AS EXTERNAL IDENTITY` were both verified against HANA Cloud 4.00.000.00.1782807759; the client emits them exactly as accepted.

- **PublicKey immutability + rotation.** Because HANA has no `ALTER` for key material and the PSE binding is by name, `spec.forProvider.pem` is immutable at the CRD level (`XValidation self==oldSelf`). Rotate by creating a new `PublicKey` with a new name, updating the PSE's `publicKeyRefs`, then deleting the old key.

author: chris-tsiaousis-hpc
body:
Loosen up the tolerance and add better logging in case of failure

TLDR: `profile_batched_gemm_b_scale_impl.hpp` (lines 390-392) uses `rtol = atol = 1e-1`, while the sibling non-batched B-scale profiler uses `2e-2` in `profile_gemm_b_scale_impl.hpp` (lines 361-364). `KBatch > 1` adds an F16 atomic accumulation step, so the batched path is stricter on the noisier arithmetic path. Loosening up the tolerances should fix the flaky test. I've also added better loging in case of failures.

## Motivation

`test_batched_gemm_b_scale_wmma` can fail on gfx1201 when `KBatch > 1` because that path uses split-K F16 atomic accumulation. The existing batched B-scale tolerance was stricter than the non-batched B-scale profiler, even though the batched split-K path has additional rounding noise from native F16 atomics.

This PR aligns the batched tolerance with the comparable non-batched path and improves failure diagnostics so future mismatches identify the exact shape, KBatch value, instance, strides, and operator.

## Technical Details

Updated [projects/composablekernel/profiler/include/profiler/profile_batched_gemm_b_scale_impl.hpp](projects/composablekernel/profiler/include/profiler/profile_batched_gemm_b_scale_impl.hpp) to:

- Change non-FP8 verification tolerance from `1e-2` to `2e-2`.
- Match the tolerance already used by the non-batched B-scale profiler.
- Build a detailed failure message with:
  - instance index
  - `kbatch`
  - `M`, `N`, `K`, and `BatchSize`
  - `StrideA`, `StrideB`, and `StrideC`
  - selected operator name
- Move operator name construction earlier so it is available for diagnostics.

## Test Plan

Configured the CK gfx1201 build with device instances enabled and XDL disabled to isolate WMMA coverage.

Built and ran the focused batched GEMM B-scale WMMA test target:

```bash
ninja -C projects/composablekernel/build-gfx950-gfx1201 test_batched_gemm_b_scale_wmma
```

Ran the focused `MidLargeM` case across WMMA instances and then ran the full WMMA-only gtest target.

## Test Result

The WMMA-only gfx1201 validation passed.

- `MidLargeM` passed across 21 WMMA instances.
- Full `test_batched_gemm_b_scale_wmma` passed all 3 gtests.
- No incorrect-result lines were reported.

author: schorsch888
body:
## Summary

Closes the two remaining findings on issue #889 after #907 (which landed F014/F008/F052). Both are "trust the JWT `role` claim instead of live DB privilege" gaps.

- **F005** — `GET /metrics` (cross-tenant Prometheus exposition) was gated on the JWT `role`, so a forged or stale `role=admin` token could scrape platform-wide operational intelligence.
- **F002** — `refresh_session` re-minted the access token from the refresh token's `role` claim, giving a demoted admin (or a removed member) an indefinitely extendable stale-privilege window.

## Changes

- `routes/metrics.rs`: `scrape` extracts `State<AppState>` and calls `AdminService::require_platform_admin(scope.user_id())`, keyed off the live `users.is_admin` column. `metrics_routes()` is bound to `AppState`; `router.rs` drops the turbofish.
- `testing.rs`: removes the obsolete bare-handle `test_router`/`rewrite_test_bearer` shim (the JWT-role-only path it modeled was the F005 vulnerability). `ensure_recorder` stays — the DB-backed test `AppState` reuses it.
- `services/user.rs`: `refresh_session` is now async and re-reads the live `organization_members.role` via `UserRepository::find_membership_role`. The new access token carries the live role; a revoked membership yields `Unauthorized`.
- `routes/auth.rs`: awaits the now-async call.

## Validation

- `metrics_endpoint_test.rs` (DB-backed `#[sqlx::test]`): forged `role=admin` with `is_admin=false` → 403; member → 403; real platform admin → 200 with the exposition.
- `services/user.rs` in-src `#[sqlx::test]`: a stale `role=admin` refresh token is re-minted as `member` when that is the live role; a revoked membership is rejected with `Unauthorized`. Verified RED first (echoing `claims.role` fails the assertion).
- `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p agentforge-api --lib --tests` clean.

## Beginner UX / First-Time User Path

- Shortest safe path: A platform operator with admin rights scrapes /metrics and refreshes their session exactly as before; no new steps for legitimate users.
- Prerequisites shown before action: Scraping /metrics now requires a platform-admin account (the users.is_admin flag), not merely an admin-looking token.
- Success looks like: Platform admins still receive the full Prometheus exposition, and a normal session refresh returns a working access token at the user's current role.
- Error or recovery path: A non-admin caller to /metrics is declined with 403; ask a platform admin to scrape, or have your admin role granted in the database.
- Destructive or permission impact: A demoted admin or a removed member loses elevated access immediately on next refresh instead of keeping it until the token expires.
- CLI platforms covered, if applicable: Not applicable; this is a server-side authorization change with no Container CLI or Platform CLI surface.

author: jbmowgli
body:
## Summary

Fixes two real bugs found while debugging "dice won't connect" on a fresh Chrome install loading the prebuilt extension.

### 1. Bluetooth connect failure (main fix)
The die's GATT service (`6e400001…`) was found but `getCharacteristic('6e400003…')` failed with *"No Characteristics matching UUID … found in Service …"*, so connecting never completed.

Replaced the hardcoded notify-characteristic lookups (in both the connect and reconnect paths) with a `findNotifyCharacteristic()` helper that:
- tries the known modern/legacy notify UUIDs first, then
- falls back to enumerating the service's characteristics and selecting the first one with the `notify` property (which also forces a full GATT discovery, recovering from the missing-characteristic case), and
- logs the actual service/characteristic UUIDs it uses, so any remaining firmware variant is easy to diagnose.

### 2. Modifier box template path
`modifierBox.js` requested `src/components/modifierBox/modifierBox.html`, but the build copies the template to `components/modifierBox/modifierBox.html`. The mismatch was rejected by `web_accessible_resources` (`Denying load of …`) and forced the inline-HTML fallback. Corrected the path so the real template loads.

### Packaging
Rebuilt the prebuilt store zip (`pixels-roll20-extension-store.zip`) from a production build with source maps stripped, packaged with the `zip` binary.

## Testing
- `npm run lint` clean, `npm test` → **216/216 passing**.
- Verified live: Pixel die now connects when loading `dist/` directly, and the `Denying load … modifierBox.html` errors are gone.

author: merlimat
body:
Follow-up to #12: backend fixes found while investigating why etcd / consul / tikv failed in the cross-driver comparison on kind.

## etcd — classpath conflict (fixed)
`tikv-client-java` (the TiKV driver dependency) is an uber-jar that bundles an older, **unrelocated** `io.etcd.jetcd`. The shaded jar then contains two `io.etcd.jetcd.ClientBuilder` classes, and the one without `connectTimeout(Duration)` can win at runtime → `NoSuchMethodError` (an `Error`, so the run's `catch (Exception)` doesn't catch it → hard crash). Adding the TiKV driver had silently broken etcd.

Fix: drop the `connectTimeout` call. jetcd's core builder API (`endpoints`/`build`/`getKVClient`/`put`/`get`) is stable across both copies, so the etcd driver works regardless of which `ClientBuilder` wins. `dialTimeout` is now ignored. (Reordering the dependency declaration does **not** reliably fix this — shadowJar's resolved-classpath order isn't controlled by declaration order.)

## tikv — pod-IP advertise (partial)
The server advertised a headless-service per-pod DNS name, but that headless service has **no endpoints**, so the name never resolves and the client `UnknownHostException`s. Advertise `status.podIP` instead (directly routable). TiKV still has a deeper single-node region-bootstrap issue on kind and isn't fully working yet.

## consul
No code change — its earlier failure was the 384 Mi OOM + oxia-cluster contention already fixed in #12.

## comparison workers
Raise the default worker memory to **896 Mi**; the etcd jetcd/gRPC client OOMs at 384–640 Mi.

Verified on kind (arm64): oxia, zookeeper, redis, consul, **etcd** all run the workloads with the 3-worker cross-worker merge; tikv connects to PD but its cluster doesn't serve regions yet.

author: shipyard-local[bot]
body: The routing buffer assignment gave every node port its own scratch slot (slot_count = total ports). This reuses scratch across non-overlapping node lifetimes so the pool footprint scales with the graph's live width, not its total size — a 12-stage stereo chain drops from 26 slots to a small constant. Algorithm (off-RT, in build_graph_runtime_buffer_assignment): a node's input region is live only during its own processing; its output region is live until its last feedforward consumer's topological position; a feedback source's output is pinned live to end-of-block (the feedback capture reads it); feedback previous-block slots are never recycled (cross-block state). Regions are freed at the END of the position that last needs them and recycled by strictly-later nodes only, so a reused slot never aliases a value still being read this block. Reuse is size-bucketed to keep each region contiguous, so the executor's `slots.input_base + p` addressing — and the whole process_routed consumption — is UNCHANGED; this PR touches only the allocator. The executor is untouched, so the existing SignalGraph bit-exact parity tests (chain, diamond, feedback) are the correctness guard for the reused layout, plus a new split-lifetime fan-out case (A feeds an early consumer B and a late fan-in into out, forcing A's scratch to stay live across B). Assignment unit tests now assert invariants (regions in range; a node's own input/output regions never overlap; reuse never grows past total ports; long-chain footprint stays a small constant) rather than the old unique-slot layout. Reviewed adversarially: a 70k-topology fuzz model of the executor's exact consumption vs the allocator's free/reuse timeline found zero liveness corruptions; a negative control (pin removed) flagged corruption in ~43% of feedback graphs, confirming the feedback pin is load-bearing. No MUST-FIX. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01CizrUDYkAs1T8zTkR5dicE --- ## Summary by cubic Reused routing scratch slots via liveness allocation so the buffer pool scales with live width, not total ports, while keeping the executor unchanged and outputs bit‑exact. A 12‑stage stereo chain drops from 26 slots to ≤8 in tests. - **Refactors** - Added a size-bucketed region allocator that reuses contiguous input/output regions across non-overlapping lifetimes; executor addressing stays base + port. - Lifetimes: inputs live only during their node; outputs live until last consumer; feedback outputs pinned to end-of-block; previous‑block feedback slots are persistent. - Tests: kept SignalGraph parity (chain, diamond, feedback), added split-lifetime fan‑out; assignment tests assert invariants and verify constant-size footprint on long chains. Written for commit 19d8af5ea3f51ec5d3b98f6bf8acb6688763ef53. Summary will update on new commits.

This makes the render side resilient. ### What this delivers - **Client-side normalise-on-render:** runs the same `normaliseMermaidSource` (a byte-identical mirror of the generation-side normaliser - literal `\n`->`
`, quote punctuation labels) before `mermaid.render()`. This fixes the display of the two already-broken stored diagrams (frontend-portfolio + the platform project) WITHOUT a DB backfill, and catches any future slip. - **Graceful fallback, never a lexer dump:** if rendering still throws, the component renders a clean node/edge component-map from the stored structured `nodes`/`edges` (or a tidy "Diagram preview unavailable" message) - the raw error string is never shown to the user again. - The SVG path (DOMPurify), the View-source toggle, and the SVG download are untouched; defensive readers handle the untyped JSON columns without throwing. ### Tests ArchitectureDiagram 5 green (normalises before render; falls back to node labels on throw and hides the lexer string); full projects suite 80 green. A pre-existing test that asserted the raw error string is shown was removed as it asserted the exact behaviour being eliminated, and replaced with stronger coverage. Whole-branch review (opus): READY TO MERGE, no blockers; cross-repo normaliser identity verified. ### Pairs with ai-applications#345 (the generation-side guarantee). author: clement-tourriere
body:
`requires-python` is already `>=3.9`, but `uv tool install` / pipx can still place ggshield on an old *system* interpreter (e.g. Python 3.6 on RHEL 8 / CentOS 8 / openSUSE Leap 15), where it dies with a cryptic `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'dataclasses'` deep in startup.

This adds an import-time guard in `ggshield/__init__.py` that exits with a clear, actionable message (pointing at both `uv` and `pipx`) before any 3.7+ import is reached (kept free of 3.7+ syntax so it runs on the old interpreter itself).

Tests: `tests/unit/test_python_version_guard.py` (rejects 3.6/3.7/3.8 with the message; accepts 3.9+). Python 2.x is intentionally not covered: its annotations are 3.x-only syntax, so the module fails at parse time and the guard is never reached. Reviewed via Codex.

Internal ref: END-618 (surfaced by the satori install matrix).

author: tftio
body:
Closes #481

## Problem

Adding a git repository whose config is corrupt can crash the app on launch, and because the repo root is persisted the crash recurs on every relaunch — there's no way back into the app.

## Root cause

When a repository's git config is corrupt — e.g. a stale `core.worktree` redirect that resolves the bare root onto a linked worktree's directory — `git` / `wt` report **two worktrees at the same path**. Both load paths feed the listing straight into `IdentifiedArray(uniqueElements:)`, whose precondition **traps on duplicate ids** (a worktree's id is its working-directory path). The trap fires during repository load, which runs on every launch → crash loop.

Reproduced with a real bare-checkout repo whose `core.worktree` pointed into one of its linked worktrees; `wt ls --json` then returned two entries with the same `path`.

## Approach

Rather than crash — or silently dedupe and present a *guessed, possibly-wrong* worktree — **detect the duplicate and refuse to open the repository**, routing it through the existing load-failure path so the sidebar shows an error row explaining the repo may be corrupt. This validates at the boundary (the untrusted git/`wt` listing) and leaves the trusted-internal `IdentifiedArray(uniqueElements:)` construction unchanged — the same way missing/unreadable roots are already handled (`loadFailuresByID` → failure row).

Both the local (`wt ls --json`) and remote (`git worktree list --porcelain`) load paths get the guard.

## Changes

- `firstDuplicateWorktreeID(in:)` and `duplicateWorktreePathMessage(path:)` — shared by both load paths.
- Local: `loadRepositoriesData` refuses a repo with duplicate paths (`WorktreesFetchResult` with no worktrees + message); per-root fetch extracted into `worktreesFetchResult(for:gitClient:)`.
- Remote: `resolveRemoteRepository` keeps the placeholder and returns a `LoadFailure` for the same condition.

## Testing

- `firstDuplicateWorktreeIDFindsRepeatedPath` (unit) and `loadPersistedRepositoriesRefusesRepoWithDuplicateWorktreePaths` (end-to-end: corrupt repo → `loadFailuresByID` failure row, no crash).
- `swiftlint` passes on the changed files.
- Note: I could not run the full `xcodebuild`/`make test` suite locally — project generation fails building the bundled ghostty Zig dependency under zig 0.15.2 / macOS SDK 26.5 (`undefined symbol: _sigaction`), unrelated to this change. Relying on CI for the full build/test run.

## Note

Supersedes #479, which took a dedupe-and-recover approach. Refusing to open is more honest: it surfaces the corruption (which the user must repair) instead of silently showing a best-effort partial — and a repo reporting two worktrees at one path is never a healthy state to operate on.
