author: jurgenploeger
body:
## What
Makes the composer's single-line centering check enforceable instead of advisory. No new guidance, the skill already prescribed this.

## Why
The skill said to center the composer's side buttons (camera, GIF, quote, mic) on the single-line field, but as a passive line it got skipped twice while rebuilding reference apps (Tinder, Bumble). The buttons sank to the bottom instead.

## The change
At single-line input, the build step now has to measure and report each button's offset from the field center, backed by a screenshot. No screenshot means the check wasn't done.

## Result
Buttons now land within ~0.6pt of center, previously ~15-20pt low.

Full benchmark, runs, and findings: https://www.notion.so/37d6a5d7f9f681f4ade4ec7990be482d

author: joel323
body:
<!--
⚠️ If you do not respect this template, your pull request will be closed.
⚠️ Your pull request title should be short detailed and understandable for all.
⚠️ If your pull request fixes an open issue, please link to the issue.

✅ I have added the tests to cover my changes.

-->

### Summary
This PR continues work initiated on PR #66, where a new design for the pipeline was introduced via the classes `ParamsProvider`, `ProblemParamsProvider`, and `PipelineComponent`. 

### Details and comments
This PR implements the necessary changes on the sub-classes that inherit from `ParamsProvider`, `ProblemParamsProvider`, and `PipelineComponent`, removing the dependency on `BaseTrainer`. Specifically, the PR includes the following changes on the pipeline management  (i.e, setup of the pipeline and execution):

1. `pipeline.py`: Adds a Pipeline class to manage the execution and setup of the pipeline. It mainly gets arguments inputed by the user from via configuration files and command line. 

2. `training/__init__.py`: Removes the TRAINERS registry by three new registries, PARAMS_PROVIDERS, PIPELINE_COMPONENTS, PROBLEM_PARAMS_PROVIDERS.

This PR also includes changes to all the sub-classes that previously inherited from BaseTrainer. The new inheritance structure is now:
| File | Class Name | Inherits From |
|------|-----------|---------------|
| `optimized_parameter_loader.py` | `OptimizedParametersLoader` | `ParamsProvider` |
| `parameter_scanner.py` | `DepthOneScanTrainer` | `ProblemParamsProvider`, `HistoryMixin` |
| `random_point.py` | `RandomPoint` | `ParamsProvider` |
| `recursion.py` | `RecursionTrainer` | `PipelineComponent` |
| `recursive_transition_states.py` | `RecursiveTransitionStates` | `PipelineComponent` |
| `reweighting.py` | `ReweightingTrainer` | `PipelineComponent` |
| `scipy_trainer.py` | `ScipyTrainer` | `PipelineComponent`, `HistoryMixin` |
| `transfer_trainer.py` | `TransferTrainer` | `ProblemParamsProvider` |
| `transition_states.py` | `TransitionStatesTrainer` | `PipelineComponent` |


Other additional changes:
- `FixedAngleConjecture` has been removed, and `LoadFromJson` has been adapted to accept the database format from `fixed_angle_conjecture.json` database provided by the authors of the original paper. This means that the fixed angle conjecture method can be run as a form of parameter transfer with `TransferTrainer`.
- `TQATrainer` has been removed, and `TQATrainerFunction` has been added to `functions.py`. This means that  the TQA method can be run directly with `ScipyTrainer` by considering linear ramps as a form of `qaoa_angles_function`. 
- Small changes in `ParamResult` and `BaseAnglesFunction`: adding `TQATrainerFunction` as a possible `qaoa_angles_function` has led to the need of adding possible additional arguments to `BaseAnglesFunction`, because the TQA function needs the QAOA circuit depth. There might be another way to do this. 
- The change in parent classes (i.e., ParamsProvider, PipelineComponent, etc.) will lead to a lot of renaming. I have started by renaming the configuration files arguments as it is the most relevant to this PR. Find an example below, which first runs a TQA schedule and then further re-optimizes the resulting angles:
```
{
    "params_provider": {
        "provider_name": "ScipyTrainer",
        "provider_init": {
            "evaluator": "EfficientDepthOneEvaluator",
            "evaluator_init": {},
            "qaoa_angles_function": "TQATrainerFunction",
            "qaoa_angles_function_init": {"schedule": "tqa_schedule"},
            "minimize_args": {"options": {"maxiter": 100, "rhobeg": 0.2}}
    }
    },
    "pipeline_components": [
        {
            "component_name": "ScipyTrainer",
            "component_init": {
                "evaluator": "EfficientDepthOneEvaluator",
                "evaluator_init": {},
                "minimize_args": {"options": {"maxiter": 100, "rhobeg": 0.2}}
            }
        }
    ]
}
```

This PR also modifies the argument format provided via command line. With this update, `provider_kwargs` and `component_kwargs{idx}` are accepted.

### Version updated

Please increment the `qaoa_training_pipeline_version` variable and extend the main README.md.

author: jung-thomas
body:
## Bug

PR #591 redesigned the daily drift workflow to compare source-markdown hashes instead of rendered-HTML hashes, and accordingly dropped the Hugo build step from `content-drift-check.yml`. But the CLI's `--verify-only` short-circuit stayed at its original location — **AFTER** `discoverTutorials(opts.hugoDir)` and the `'No tutorials found'` guard.

With no Hugo output present, `discoverTutorials` returns an empty map → guard exits 1 BEFORE the verify-only block ever runs. Run [28104752827](https://github.com/sap-tutorials/tutorials-ims/actions/runs/28104752827) caught this:

```
Verify source-markdown hashes against dev:
  Discovering tutorials in hugo/public...
  Error: No tutorials found. Did you run the Hugo build?
```

## Fix

Move the verify-only block to run **right after the API-key check** (line 500ish), BEFORE `discoverTutorials` is called. The verify path has its own slug discovery via `readdirSync('.tutorial-cache/*.md')`; it doesn't need the Hugo output map at all.

Also removed a stray 90-line duplicate verify-only block left at the original position by the move (visible in the diff stat as net -41 lines after counting the 47 inserted at the new position).

author: raidostar
body:
Closes #95.

Shell-native parity with the Claude-Code-only `/redteam:redteam-config`: a
zero-dep, `input()`-based interactive `orchestrator.py config` to set the
per-role `[models]` (planner/implementer/reviewer/rescue) in
`.redteam/config.toml` from **any shell** (no Claude Code needed).

## What it does
- Shows current `[models]`, prompts per role (blank keeps the current value), and
  writes only the `[models]` keys back — preserving the rest of the file and its
  comments.
- Enforces the cross-provider **self-review invariant before writing** and
  REFUSES (exit 2) rather than silently "fixing" a collapse.

## Design (security boundary — for review)
- **Single source of provider resolution.** Extracts `reviewer_family_provider()`
  — a pure refactor of `reviewer_provider` (pinned by
  `test_reviewer_family_provider_unchanged_behavior`) — and uses it identically
  for **both** `reviewer` and `rescue`, so the self-review check can't drift
  between roles. The CLI guard checks the invariant across **every effective
  config** it would drive: the top-level `[models]` when untiered, else each
  **review-enabled** tier's merged models (review=false tiers are skipped,
  matching the runtime guard). It reuses the engine resolvers (`worker_provider`
  + `reviewer_family_provider`) rather than re-implementing resolution; the
  comparison is a one-liner over those shared values. *(Note for the reviewer: it
  does not call `_adversarial_pairing_error` directly — that guard takes a
  per-task resolved state/order and checks reviewer only; the CLI is static and
  adds rescue parity. Flagging the trade-off explicitly.)*
- **Comment-preserving write.** `update_models_block()` edits only canonical
  `key = "value"` lines in place (preserving inline/block comments and LF/CRLF)
  and **fails closed** (returns None → exit 2, writes nothing) on any
  non-canonical / duplicate / missing form. No TOML serializer is added (none in
  stdlib).
- **Corruption-proof.** A two-layer gate — textual (only edited value spans may
  differ; everything else byte-identical) and semantic (the candidate re-parses
  through the **same loader** to exactly the chosen values) — plus an atomic
  temp-file `os.replace` that preserves mode and leaves the original intact on any
  failure.

## Invariants held
- Engine stays project-agnostic; stdlib-only (zero runtime deps).
- `/redteam:redteam-config` (the Claude-Code surface) is unchanged.

## Tests
+18 in `.redteam/tests/test_config_cli.py` (pure-editor cases incl. CRLF /
comment / unsafe-value / non-canonical fail-closed; interactive happy path,
self-review + rescue-collapse refusal, review=false vs review=true tier
override, legacy-value-kept-on-blank, unknown-reviewer warn, EOF/missing-config,
gate-refuses-noncanonical). `ruff` clean, full suite 284 passed.

### Goal

Today the Compose SDK always draws a presence dot on user avatars when the indicator is requested: green when the user is online and grey when offline. This does not match the design system ("Common / Avatar Behavior") or the other Stream SDKs, which show the indicator only when the user is online.

This change hides the indicator when the user is offline by default, and gives integrators per-call control over the presence state. It is aligned with the iOS SwiftUI `AvatarIndicator`.

Linear: https://linear.app/stream/issue/AND-1257

### Implementation

- Added a public `AvatarPresenceIndicator` enum with `Online`, `Offline`, and `None`, mirroring the iOS SwiftUI `AvatarIndicator`.
- `UserAvatar` and `ChannelAvatar` now take `indicator: AvatarPresenceIndicator = None`. The shared `OnlineIndicator` draws green for `Online`, grey for `Offline`, and nothing for `None`. This is the single place the dot is rendered, so every screen that shows a presence indicator is covered.
- The default for the SDK screens changes: an online user shows a green dot, an offline user shows nothing. The grey offline dot is now an opt-in: pass `AvatarPresenceIndicator.Offline`, or override the avatar in `ChatComponentFactory`. There is no theme flag, which matches how iOS does it.
- Non-breaking. The previous `showIndicator: Boolean` parameter is deprecated and kept on both composables and on `UserAvatarParams` / `ChannelAvatarParams`, alongside the new `indicator`. The deprecated path preserves today's behavior (green online, grey offline) so existing integrations do not change silently. The factory resolves `params.indicator`, falling back to the deprecated `showIndicator` when `indicator` is not set.
- Migrated every SDK call site that showed the indicator (channel info, member info, members list, channel actions, search results, thread items) to the online-only mapping.

### 🎨 UI Changes

Avatars that show a presence indicator no longer draw the grey dot when the user is offline; they show nothing. Online avatars are unchanged (green dot). This is visible on the channel and contact info screens, the members list, the channel actions sheet, search results, and thread items.

The updated Paparazzi snapshots in this PR capture the before/after (the grey offline dot is removed from `UserAvatarTest`, `ThreadListTest`, and `MentionListTest`).

### Testing

Manual steps in the Compose sample app:

1. Open a 1:1 channel where the other user is offline. The avatar in the channel header and on the channel info screen shows no presence dot. When that user is online, it shows a green dot.
2. Open Group Info for a group with both online and offline members. Online members show a green dot; offline members show no dot (previously grey).
3. Long-press a 1:1 channel to open the channel actions sheet. The dot is shown only when the other user is online.
4. Open search results and the thread list. Author avatars show the dot only when the author is online.
5. To verify the opt-in: in a `ChatTheme` `componentFactory` override of `UserAvatar`, pass `indicator = AvatarPresenceIndicator.Offline` (or `if (user.online) AvatarPresenceIndicator.Online else AvatarPresenceIndicator.Offline`) and confirm the grey dot returns for offline users.

`AvatarPresenceIndicatorTest` covers the resolver mapping (online, offline with and without the opt-in, the channel "any member online" rule, and the null current user case).

author: hallyn
body:
We've long known (see
https://www.halfdog.net/Security/2012/TtyPushbackPrivilegeEscalation/ and https://jdebp.uk/FGA/dont-abuse-su-for-dropping-privileges.html) that su should be used to gain but not drop privilege.  Much more recently, linux added the ability to prevent TIOCSTI through a configurable /proc/sys/dev/tty/legacy_tiocsti setting.

If /proc/sys/dev/tty/legacy_tiocsti is set to 0, then we are protected from the callee injecting commands on caller's tty through TIOCSTI. If it's 1, or doesn't exist, then we are not.  That can be dangerous if caller is root.  We currently give up the controlling terminal for non-interactive uses of su (-c).  Let's do that for interactive calls as well, only in the dangerous case.

author: bradleybond512
body:
Sixth item of the diagnostics-audit P0 batch — the one the audit critic flagged as the **risky** one, so it's isolated and conservatively scoped.

## Problem (green-when-broken, with safety weight)
A feed whose latest fetch **succeeds but returns zero items** (an empty `200 OK` — a silently-broken auth response, an upstream that started returning `[]`) reads `fresh` by age alone, indistinguishable from one actively delivering data. A weather or earthquake feed could go silently empty and still look healthy.

`itemCount` **accumulates**, so it can never tell "this refresh was empty".

## Fix — additive, zero risk-path change
- `lastBatchItemCount`: SET to the latest refresh's size (not accumulated).
- `isDeliveringEmpty(source)`: pure helper — `lastUpdate && !lastError && lastBatchItemCount === 0`.
- `getEmptyDeliverySources()`: read-only list for diagnostics.

**Why it can't regress prod safety:**
- `FreshnessStatus`, `calculateStatus`, and risk aggregation are **untouched**. `calculateStatus` never reads item counts, so the empty signal never changes the `status` downstream risk logic keys off. The test asserts a delivered-empty source still reports `status='fresh'`.
- **No loader call sites change**: `recordUpdate` already receives `itemCount`; the default (`1`) keeps count-less callers non-empty.

Surfacing in a diagnostic UI is a deliberate follow-up, kept out of this PR to honor the critic's "isolate the risky change" guidance.

## Verification
3/3 tests (latest-vs-cumulative; fresh-but-empty detected **and status unchanged**; never-updated/errored not flagged). `typecheck:all` + eslint clean.

`claude/*` branch — Codex cross-agent review required before merge.

author: luca-veronelli-stem
body:
Closes #60

## Status: CODE-COMPLETE, VALIDATION-PENDING

Green CI is **not** sufficient for this ticket -- that is exactly what shipped the reverted #68 deaf-transport regression. The HARD pre-merge gate is the bench live-boundary check below; do **not** merge on CI alone.

## What this does

`probe` (and the `smoke` probe phase) survive a transient BLE **session loss** -- the link dropping mid-probe after a successful connect -- by reconnecting and re-probing within a bounded budget, instead of reporting a false `unreachable` (exit 3). Bench-found: 5/80 spurious exit-3s, all post-connect session losses.

This is the **redesign** of the reverted #68 (see #69 for the revert root cause). The key difference from #68: the BLE receive channel is now **stable for the transport's lifetime** -- never swapped, never completed on a session loss -- so the long-lived `LoggingTransport` receive pump no longer goes permanently deaf.

## Slices (each bisect-safe, gate-green at every commit)

1. `fix(ble)` -- the receive channel is completed **only** by `DisposeAsync`; `HandleSessionLoss`/`TeardownSessionAsync` no longer complete it. Session loss is signalled by `IsConnected` (and a send `Error`). I1 doc rework across `Ports.fs`, `SparkProbe`/`SparkUpdateProcedure` comments, `Logging.fs`, and `contracts/update-procedure.md`. Adds `LoggingTransportReconnectTests` -- drives the **real** `LoggingTransport` over a fake inner transport to pin the decorator contract in CI (the live-boundary blind spot that let #68 ship).
2. `feat(core)` -- bounded reconnect-on-session-loss in `Probe.reach`/`run`, keyed off `IsConnected` (not the round-trip `Result`); forwarded through `Smoke.run`; thunks built in `Program.fs`. `reconnectBudget = 0` is byte-identical to pre-#60.
3. `feat(cli)` -- `--probe-reconnects <n>` on `probe` and `smoke` (default 2; `0` disables; negative -> exit 2). `cli.md` documents it (FLAGGED spec edit).
4. `chore(cli)` -- a debug-only, env-gated fault-injection transport (`STEM_DEVICEUPDATER_FORCE_DROP_AFTER_SENDS`) that severs the real link after the Nth send, to reproduce a deterministic mid-probe session loss for the bench gate. No CLI flag, no cli.md; production `BleTransport` untouched.

## Verification (local gate -- both legs)

`./gate.ps1` green at each slice and at HEAD: `dotnet build -c Release` 0W/0E on both `net10.0` and `net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0`; the cross-platform suite (incl. the new `LoggingTransportReconnectTests`, the reconnect `ProbeTests`, the `--probe-reconnects` `CliContractTests`, and `FaultInjectionTests`); the `Tests.Windows` leg; and `dotnet format whitespace`.

- Cross-platform suite: 294 passed / 4 skipped.
- Windows leg: 19 passed.

The decorator contract is proven in CI; the **driver's** live adherence (real `BleTransport` keeps the channel stable) and the end-to-end reconnect are live-only by design (constitution VI) -- the bench gate below.

## HARD pre-merge gate -- bench live-boundary check (the #60 lesson)

Run against the real SPARK (device GUID `00000000-0000-0000-0000-9035ea1c2997`), using the slice-D fault injector to force a deterministic mid-probe drop:

1. **Reconnect recovers** -- `STEM_DEVICEUPDATER_FORCE_DROP_AFTER_SENDS=1`, `probe --device <guid>`: expect **reachable, exit 0** (the forced drop after the VER send is recovered by a reconnect).
2. **Budget 0 disables** -- same env var, `probe --device <guid> --probe-reconnects 0`: expect **unreachable, exit 3** (no reconnect).
3. **Pump is alive** -- the wire log shows **RX after the reconnect** (the exact thing that was dead in #68).
4. **Honest failure** -- a genuinely-absent device still **exits 3** after the budget.

Do not claim the ticket validated on CI alone.

## Residual risks

- The bench gate above is unproven until run on hardware (intermittent SPARK); this is `ValidationPending`, not a per-PR CI gate.
- `update`/`batch` deliberately do **not** reconnect mid-flash (out of scope, #60); their session-loss failure now flows via timeout -> send-`Error` instead of channel-completion (doc-only I1 rework, no engine change).
- The fault injector is debug-only and env-gated; it must never be enabled in a normal run (no CLI surface, off by default).

author: jleni
body:
## What

Closes e2e feature-coverage gaps surfaced by a cross-family (Claude + codex) audit of the suite.

**`scenarios/COVERAGE.md`** — a feature→scenario matrix of the 29 functional e2e scenarios, the gaps where a feature has no e2e coverage, and a prioritized backlog. Headline finding: the entire **remote/S3 + daemon + sync** half of the product has zero e2e coverage.

**Two new gate fixtures** for cc refusal classes that had no coverage (siblings of `e2e-c-passthrough`, asserting `max_entries_after = 0` across cold/warm/relocate):

- `e2e-cc-multi-source` — `cc -c a.c b.c main.c` compiles several TUs in one process; the per-TU cache can't key it, so it passes through and caches nothing.
- `e2e-cc-response-file` — `cc @args.rsp` hides the real flags behind `@file` at classification time; refused → passthrough → nothing cached. (Response files are how large Windows/cross builds stay under the command-line limit, so this contract is load-bearing.)

Both verified green through the `kache-scenario` gate harness.

## Scope note

The audit's config-toggle (`key_salt`/`ignore_env`/…) and `modified_input_guard` (#324) gaps do **not** fit the harness's fixed phase model (no "rebuild with different config" phase; the too-new guard is mtime-vs-build-start timing-dependent). `COVERAGE.md` records this — they stay in unit tests (`key_salt`/`ignore_env` effects are already covered in `src/cache_key.rs`).

## Not in this PR (prioritized in COVERAGE.md)

Remote-S3 round-trip (#1, needs a local S3), cross-machine dedup, daemon prefetch, platform restore modes, Rust edge-keys, and the remaining refusal classes (`-E`/`-S`, multi-arch).

No workspace/cargo code changed — fixtures + doc only.

author: fmxexpress
body:
## Why

The full-detail tool side-channel (originally PR #345) **never made it into `main`** when the stacked PRs were merged — I confirmed `main` has the collapsible cards (#344) but none of the side-channel code (`FormatToolDetailJSON`, `pasclaw-tool`, `pairToolDetails`). So expanding a tool card only shows the streamed one-line summary. This re-lands the side-channel **directly on current `main`** (not stacked), plus two UI tweaks you asked for.

## Full tool detail (re-land of #345)

- **Gateway:** `FormatToolDetailJSON` (`PasClaw.Gateway.ToolView`) builds compact one-line JSON for a call or result, size-capped (args 8 KB, result 16 KB, truncation flagged). The streamer emits it as a `: pasclaw-tool {json}` **SSE comment** after each visible call/result line. SSE comments are dropped by every OpenAI-compatible client, so the visible content stream is unchanged — only the PasClaw web UI reads the side-channel.
- **Web UI:** the SSE loop collects `pasclaw-tool` events; `pairToolDetails` aligns them to the `⏺` cards by call order (FIFO same-name match, correct for parallel duplicate calls). A card with detail expands to **full args** (pretty-printed JSON) and **full result/error**. Without detail (a turn reloaded from the server), it falls back to the streamed `⎿` summary.
- Detail is **live-only** — it rides SSE comments, which aren't part of the saved assistant message, so a reloaded turn shows the summary card.

## UI changes

- **Resizable session sidebar:** a draggable divider sits between the session list and the chat pane. Width clamps to 120–600 px and persists in `localStorage` (`pasclaw.sidebarWidth`).
- **Drop the "pasclaw" label** on assistant bubbles. The empty label cell is kept so assistant bubbles stay aligned with the "you" rows.

- `make test-toolview` passes, incl. `TestDetailJSON` (kind/name/full-value fields, error field, single-physical-line invariant so it rides one comment frame, size capping).

author: greatv
body:
This pull request introduces several improvements to the regression testing workflow, model download logic, and CLI usability for the project. The most significant updates include adding support for downloading models directly from Hugging Face, refactoring the regression workflow to allow flexible model selection, and enhancing the CLI with new options and clearer argument handling.

**Key changes:**

### Regression workflow improvements

* The GitHub Actions regression workflow (`.github/workflows/validation.yml`) now supports running either a typical subset of models or the full manifest, controlled by a new `full` input parameter. The workflow logic and cache keys have been updated to reflect this flexibility, and the job is renamed from `full-regression` to `regression`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c707f934fe56964ebe4e68cbf0eb00915fb01d8af63d6b37a06dbf365e9cf937R16-R20) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c707f934fe56964ebe4e68cbf0eb00915fb01d8af63d6b37a06dbf365e9cf937L52-R104) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c707f934fe56964ebe4e68cbf0eb00915fb01d8af63d6b37a06dbf365e9cf937L79-R151)

### Model download enhancements

* The `scripts/download_regression_models.py` script is refactored to support downloading models from Hugging Face repositories in addition to tar archives. This is enabled via a new `hf_repo` field in the model manifest, and download logic is split into `ensure_hf_model` and `ensure_tar_model` functions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-10ed8857e391106760bdd6ae7458b3bf31a8b968320678e2b0a5ff475b343c4dR19-R35) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-10ed8857e391106760bdd6ae7458b3bf31a8b968320678e2b0a5ff475b343c4dL40-R70) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-10ed8857e391106760bdd6ae7458b3bf31a8b968320678e2b0a5ff475b343c4dL125-R202) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-10ed8857e391106760bdd6ae7458b3bf31a8b968320678e2b0a5ff475b343c4dL151-R228) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-10ed8857e391106760bdd6ae7458b3bf31a8b968320678e2b0a5ff475b343c4dL197-R265)
* Several new models with `hf_repo` references are added to `scripts/regression_models.json`, enabling direct download from Hugging Face for these models.

### Dependency and manifest management

* A `[dependency-groups]` section is added to `pyproject.toml` to define a `regression` group, keeping regression dependencies consistent and easier to manage.

### CLI improvements

* The CLI argument parsing in `src/cli.rs` is enhanced: a new `TargetOpset` enum allows specifying `--opset auto`, and a new `--optimize` flag is introduced for ONNX graph optimization level. Tests are updated to cover these new options. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b2812f19576dd53d0c35b107a322f58a00fce6977f4b5976e1961853982af3ccL1-R23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b2812f19576dd53d0c35b107a322f58a00fce6977f4b5976e1961853982af3ccL14-R47) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b2812f19576dd53d0c35b107a322f58a00fce6977f4b5976e1961853982af3ccL35-R76) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b2812f19576dd53d0c35b107a322f58a00fce6977f4b5976e1961853982af3ccL55-R108)

### Internal code quality

* Minor improvements and code organization in the Rust codebase, such as importing the optimizer in `src/converter/export.rs` and marking unused functions with `#[allow(dead_code)]`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f9ba6b628991d6dedce81011a20b59ff5e8b37d51badfa687bbb50dbbf250b14R7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f9ba6b628991d6dedce81011a20b59ff5e8b37d51badfa687bbb50dbbf250b14R723)

author: wenhaomin
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3 — video playback position resets to 0 when switching browser tabs.

**Root cause (two-layer):**

1. `useVideo` had TanStack Query's default `refetchOnWindowFocus: true`, so returning to the tab triggered a refetch. A new presigned URL → new `src` prop on `<video>` → browser resets `currentTime` to 0.

2. Even with that disabled, the browser fires a spurious `timeupdate` event with `currentTime=0` as part of the `emptied` sequence when `src` changes. The `onTimeUpdate` handler was unconditionally writing to `lastPlaybackTimeRef`, so the ref got zeroed out before `onLoadedMetadata` could restore the saved position.

**Changes:**

- `features/videos/hooks.ts`: `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` on `useVideo` — prevents the refetch entirely on tab focus.
- `routes/videos/$videoId.tsx`:
  - `updateVideoTiming`: only writes to `lastPlaybackTimeRef` when `time > 0`, so spurious `timeupdate(0)` during src change can't erase the saved position.
  - `restoreVideoTime` on `onLoadedMetadata`: seeks the video back to the saved position after a src reload.
  - `syncVideoTime` on `onDurationChange`: updates display state without touching the ref.

## Test plan

- [x] Playwright test confirms ✅ PASS: position is preserved after simulated src reset
- [x] Manual: open a video, play to some time T, switch tabs and return — video resumes at T
- [x] Manual: seek to beginning (t=0), switch tabs — video stays at 0 after return

body:
## PokerEval — Phases 1–3

This branch holds the full project to date. The newest work is **Phase 3 (self-play RL)**; Phases 1–2 are included since `phase1-eval-suite` is the cumulative working branch.

### Phase 3 — Self-play RL harness (this round)
A principled response to Phase 2's negative result. Learner trains against a **periodically-refreshed frozen snapshot of itself**; reward = **chips at showdown** (no solver oracle); GRPO advantages are **deal-conditioned** (G hands per fixed deal, so card luck cancels). Eval reuses Phase 2's `evaluate_policy` unchanged, so exploitability-vs-CFR stays directly comparable.

- New package `src/pokereval/rl/selfplay/`: `game.py` (Leduc hand stepper + fixed-deal replay), `rollout.py` (learner-vs-frozen-opponent, illegal→fold), `train.py` (GRPO loop, opponent refresh, eval reuse).
- `backend.snapshot()` frozen-opponent sampler; shared `build_state`/`node_to_state` engine helpers (DRY with the synth generator).
- `rl-selfplay` CLI command + `make selfplay-smoke` (offline) / `selfplay-train` (live, gated behind `--live` + billing pre-flight).
- Built and validated **fully offline** (mock backend + CFR solver) — design spec `docs/specs/2026-06-23-selfplay-design.md`, plan `docs/plans/2026-06-23-selfplay.md`.

### Status / scope
- Full suite: **104 passed, 1 skipped**.
- The offline suite proves loop *mechanics*; the exploitability-reduction claim requires the gated `--live` run on a funded Tinker account (currently billing-blocked).

### Earlier phases (context)
- **Phase 1:** Kuhn/Leduc/Hold'em eval suite — CFR/Nash solver, exploitability metric, verifiable + LLM-judge graders, leaderboard.
- **Phase 2:** RLVR on Tinker — clean negative result (single-step RLVR vs a Nash oracle collapses to a deterministic modal policy and *raises* exploitability across two reward designs), motivating Phase 3.

author: chazmaniandinkle
body:
Third cluster from the codebase audit (`AUDIT-2026-06-24.md`): **reconcile-contract**, low-risk subset. Security shipped in #396, resource leaks in #397.

This PR takes the four findings that are unambiguous correctness/efficiency fixes with **no change to reconcile semantics**. The contract-semantics items from the same cluster are deferred to review-required follow-ups (see below) since they touch worktree/ledger state and provider state machines.

## Fixes

**1. `reconcile.GetProvider` recursive-RLock deadlock** — `pkg/substrate/reconcile/registry.go`
The unknown-name error path called `ListProviders()`, which takes a second `RLock`. `sync.RWMutex` is not reentrant: once a writer (config-reload `RegisterProvider`/`UpsertProvider`) is blocked waiting, Go's RWMutex stops admitting new readers, so the re-`RLock` deadlocks the calling goroutine permanently. Fixed by building the name list inline under the already-held lock. Regression test verified to hang against the buggy code.

**2. `cogdoc_review.FetchLive` unguarded by `Enabled`** — `pkg/cogdoc_review/reconciler.go`
A disabled pipeline still did an O(corpus) `WalkDir`+YAML parse and a 3s Ollama HTTP probe on every ~30s tick. `ComputePlan` already short-circuits on `!Enabled` (reading only `CorpusSize`/`OllamaReachable` for metadata), so `FetchLive` now returns a zero-value `liveState` when disabled. Directly relevant to the original "kernel eating CPU" report.

**3. `reconcile_daemon` swallowed LoadState errors** — `internal/engine/reconcile_daemon.go`
`state, _ := reconcile.LoadState(...)` hid JSON corruption / permission faults and silently reset lineage serials. Now captured and `slog.Warn`ed on the non-`IsNotExist` error (LoadState maps a missing file to `(nil, nil)`), mirroring the existing `WriteState` warning. Error behavior is otherwise unchanged (continue with nil state).

**4. `decision_lineage` unchecked type assertions** — `internal/engine/decision_lineage_reconciler.go`
`ComputePlan`/`BuildState` did `config.(*DecisionLineageConfig)` / `live.([]Decision)` without comma-ok, so a non-daemon caller (test/CLI) passing the wrong type panicked and crashed the daemon. Now returns an error, mirroring `WorktreeReconciler.ComputePlan`.

## Deferred to review-required follow-ups (touch reconcile/worktree contract)
- **WorktreeReconciler stays HealthDegraded after alarm acknowledged** (`worktree_reconciler.go:648`) — high value (re-degrades + LLM-escalates every ~30s, burning API budget) but mutates worktree-reconcile alarm semantics.
- **EvalProvider.ComputePlan destructive write** (`eval/provider_impl.go:487`) — `ComputePlan` (contractually pure) clears a sidecar file; fix threads triggers through `FetchLive`/live state.
- **MLXSupervisedProvider never converges during model load** (`provider_mlx_supervised.go:236`) — needs a starting-state/cooldown in the provider state machine.
- **Per-cycle subprocess batching** (`local_runner.go` `ps`, `pin/pin.go` `git`) — perf, needs argv-match-semantics-preserving refactor.

## Tests
- `registry_test.go`: deadlock regression under concurrent writers (bounded deadline; confirmed it fails against the buggy code).
- `reconciler_test.go`: disabled pipeline skips the corpus walk (corpus_size 0 vs >0).
- `decision_lineage_reconciler_test.go`: wrong-live-type returns error, not panic.

`go test -race` green for all touched packages. (Pre-existing unrelated local failure `TestBuildRouterRegistersMLXSupervisedType` — live LM Studio auto-discovery — passes in CI.)

## Key Features

### Anti-Hallucination List
Prevents AI from using non-existent or deprecated functions:
- regexmatch, regex - Don't exist (use find, split, contains instead)

- Array manipulation patterns

- find() returns 0 (not -1) when not found
- find() is 1-indexed

- Short-circuit evaluation (use if, not and)
- tostring() vs touniformstring()

## Architecture

Clear file role separation:
- **function-reference.md** - Function catalog (what exists, how to call)
- **expressions.md** - Architectural patterns (when/why to use)

Loading strategy:
1. Always load function-reference.md first (Step 1 in SKILL.md)
2. Load expressions.md for architectural guidance
3. Check anti-hallucination list before using functions

## Validation

Functions validated against Appian 26.5 documentation:
- ✅ find() - Confirmed returns 0, 1-indexed
- ✅ regexmatch() - Confirmed doesn't exist (404)
- ✅ index() - Signature validated, gotchas added

author: vadika
body:
**WIP / draft — M0 of VM snapshot & restore (HVF-first). Tracking #748.**

This opens the snapshot/restore work for review at the **M0 design gate**. It
contains the backend-neutral seam only — no capture or restore logic yet (every
body is `todo!()`). I'd like sign-off on the design below before writing M1
capture code.

## What's in this PR

`src/vmm/src/snapshot/mod.rs` (+ a one-line module decl). 

- **One** polymorphic trait, `Snapshottable`, for devices (the only genuinely
  polymorphic case — iterated as trait objects).
- A shared, **arch-keyed** `VcpuState` that KVM and HVF both fill in — no
  hypervisor name appears in the type. This is the "seam must not leak HVF
  specifics" bar from #748.
- Free fns `write_mem_image` / `cow_clone` for guest RAM and disk CoW, hiding
  the platform primitive (`MAP_PRIVATE` / `clonefile` / `FICLONE`) from callers.
- GIC + per-vCPU capture attach to existing types (`IrqChipT`, the per-backend
  `Vcpu`) rather than new traits. Those KVM-side stubs follow on a Linux host
  where the KVM path compiles.

## Design note (M0 deliverable)

### Seam 
One new trait; everything else is an inherent method, a free fn, or an extension
of an existing trait, because everything else has a single or cfg-split impl. No
`Snapshottable`-style interface with one implementation.
- vCPU state is **arch-keyed, not hypervisor-keyed** — `VcpuState::Aarch64{ gp,
  sysregs, simd, icc, vtimer }` is identical whether KVM or HVF fills it.
- GIC is an opaque `Vec<u8>` blob on the existing `IrqChipT` — whether the bytes
  came from `hv_gic_state_get_data` or a KVM VGIC dev-attr dump is invisible.
- Memory is `MAP_PRIVATE` of a file — a POSIX primitive, not macOS-specific.

### On-disk format
Directory: `manifest.json` (serde_json, the contract) + `memory.img` (raw guest
RAM, `MAP_PRIVATE` base on restore) + `vmstate` (hand-rolled versioned binary:
vCPU regs/sysregs/SIMD/ICC/vtimer, GIC blob, per-device state). `manifest` and
`vmstate` versioned independently; loader rejects mismatches with a clear errno,
never half-loads. vmstate is hand-rolled because it's a register dump — never
JSON.

### Minimal device set (M1)
virtio-blk, virtio-vsock, virtio-rng, RTC (PL031), console. Each captures its
virtqueue indices (`next_avail`/`next_used`/`ready`) + MMIO transport state at a
quiescent point. Host fds/threads are rebuilt on restore (re-open image, restart
workers); vsock seeds an `OP_RST` per live connection (ignition's model).

### Memory model
`MAP_PRIVATE` of `memory.img`, MAP_PRIVATE` of a file is demand-paged by the kernel,
so idle RSS stays well below full RAM without userfaultfd. (Note: the ignition
reference uses `MAP_PRIVATE` + eager diff overlay, not `MAP_SHARED`/UFFD as #748
loosely describes.)

### Capture trigger
`krun_start_enter` stays **blocking** — its main thread is the live device
backend event loop, not idle; returning would strand it, and it's the 2.0
lifetime contract embedders depend on.
- **Model A (default, M1):** host-driven. Embedder runs the blocking enter on a
  thread it owns and calls `krun_snapshot_request` out-of-band (or
  `krun_snapshot_create`, the blocking enter-wait-serialize-exit flavor).
  Readiness detection is the embedder's. Zero core change.
- **Model B (deferred):** guest-signaled via a reserved vsock port. Needs a
  libkrunfw/init convention — kept pluggable behind an internal
  `CaptureTrigger` 

### Clone safety (M3, ships with restore)
vmgenid-style generation bump on restore + `krun_set_entropy_seed`, so two clones
from one base diverge in RNG/identity. Not deferred past restore.

### Out of scope
KVM backend (design-compatible, later series), virtio-fs/gpu/TSI.

## Open question for maintainers
The **capture-readiness trigger** (Model A vs adding B, and whether B's vsock
convention is acceptable in the libkrunfw init path) — @mtjhrc's call per #748.
Everything else above I believe is settled; happy to adjust.

## Milestones
M0 seam (this PR) → M1 HVF capture + minimal devices → M2 restore + lazy CoW +
reconfig whitelist → M3 clone safety → M4 hardening/tests/docs.

author: rbaumier
body:
Follow-up to #6026 (merged as #6038). A self-review of the merged change found one real regression plus two minor issues; this PR fixes all three.

## Context
#6038 seeded the TanStack Start bootstrap basenames (`client.tsx`/`ssr.tsx`/`server.ts`) as framework entry points so `unused-file` stops flagging them, and added `is_tanstack_only_bootstrap_entry` so the broadened `is_framework_entry_point` does not over-exempt those basenames in `no-side-effects-in-initialization` (whose `is_tanstack_start_entry` keeps the exemption depth-aware: only at the conventional `app/` location).

## Findings fixed

**major — `app/ssr.tsx` wrongly flagged.** `is_tanstack_only_bootstrap_entry` suppressed `ssr.{ts,tsx}` from the broad framework-entry exemption, but the depth-aware re-exemption `is_tanstack_start_entry` only recognized `client`/`router`/`server` — not `ssr`. So in a TanStack project even a legitimate `app/ssr.tsx` with a top-level side effect (e.g. `initZodLocale()`) was flagged. Fix: add `ssr` to `is_tanstack_start_entry` (recognized stem + `/app/ssr.` and the explicit `app/ssr.{ts,tsx}` equality arms), so `app/ssr.tsx` is re-exempted while `src/utils/ssr.tsx` stays flagged.

**minor — speculative suppression set.** Trimmed `is_tanstack_only_bootstrap_entry`'s `matches!` to exactly the seeded basenames (`client.tsx`/`ssr.tsx`/`server.ts`). The prior superset (`client.ts`/`ssr.ts`/`server.tsx`) could only suppress exemptions the profile never grants — a misleading no-op.

**minor — bare `setup.ts` uncovered.** In `unused-file`'s `is_test_file`, a bare `setup.ts` (stem `setup`, since `file_stem` strips the extension) matched neither `stem.starts_with("setup-")` nor `stem.starts_with("setup.")`. Added a `stem == "setup"` arm and corrected the comment.

## Tests
- `allows_tanstack_start_ssr_entry_issue_6026` — `app/ssr.tsx` exempt (would fail before this PR).
- `flags_ssr_tsx_outside_app_dir_issue_6026` — `src/utils/ssr.tsx` still flagged (depth-aware negative space).
- `bare_setup_file_is_not_flagged_issue_6026` — bare `src/setup.ts` exempt by `unused-file` (would fail before this PR).

## Verification
- `cargo test --bin comply`: 16825 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --bin comply`: zero warnings on touched modules (`unused_file`, `no_side_effects_in_initialization`); pre-existing repo warning count unchanged.

author: loic-slamcore
body:
When a timed-out worker receives SIGABRT, a core dump may be in progress by the time the next heartbeat check runs. Sending SIGKILL at that point truncates the dump, making post-mortem analysis impossible.

This change adds a new `--worker-abort-timeout` config option (defaults to 0 to preserve existing behaviour). When set to a positive value, the SIGKILL signal is only sent if (at least one condition fulfilled):
* the process is not actively creating a core dump
* the new timeout is exceeded

author: amankoli09
body:
Closes #266 
### Description
This PR implements reliable, signed webhook delivery for invoice state transitions. It wires up the existing background worker queue to automatically dispatch webhooks whenever an invoice transitions to a new state (e.g., `pending` → `approved`).

**Changes include:**
- Added a new job handler `src/jobs/webhookDelivery.js` to process webhook deliveries asynchronously with exponential backoff.
- Integrated `enqueueWebhookDelivery` inside `src/services/invoiceStateMachine.js` so a delivery is enqueued immediately after an audit log is created.
- Exported the `sortKeys` utility to ensure deterministically sorted JSON payloads for reliable signature validation on the client side.
- Wrote a comprehensive test suite `tests/webhooks.delivery.test.js` covering transient retries, permanent dead-lettering, HMAC signature verification, and security boundaries.
- Updated `README.md` with a detailed **Webhooks** section explaining signature verification, payload structures, retry policies, and security practices.

### Security Notes
- **Constant-time signature verification:** Signature comparison strictly uses `crypto.timingSafeEqual` to mitigate timing attacks.
- **No secrets in logs:** Target URLs and Webhook secrets are deliberately excluded from standard `info` logs; they are scoped safely during the worker job processing.
- **Replay Protection:** We enforce a strict 5-minute `TOLERANCE_MS` tolerance check on timestamps within the payload signature header (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<signature>`).
- **Fail-safe Transitions:** Asynchronous webhook enqueue failures are caught and logged so they never bubble up to rollback or fail an underlying invoice state transition.

Fixes #2646

## What this fixes

Cross-references to a `[discrete]` heading — or to an inline/phrase anchor (`[[id]]`, `anchor:id[]`,
`[#id]#text#`) — whose **ID contains characters outside Windows-1252** (e.g. Cyrillic) produced
**dead links** in the PDF. References to regular section headings (`==`, `===`) with the same kind of
ID already worked.

The cause is an asymmetry left behind by #308:

- **References** encode the destination name with `derive_anchor_from_id`, which returns
  `0x<utf8-hex>` for any value that is not `ascii_only?` (the `:xref` case uses
  `<a anchor="#{derive_anchor_from_id refid}">`).
- **Sections** register their destination with the *same* derived name (`convert_section` calls
  `derive_anchor_from_id sect.id` and passes the result to `add_dest_for_block`), so they match.
- **Block destinations** (`add_dest_for_block`) and **inline-anchor destinations**
  (`convert_inline_anchor` / `convert_inline_quoted`, registered by
  `InlineDestinationMarker.render_behind`) registered the **raw** id instead.

For a non-ASCII id this means: registration = raw UTF-8 bytes, reference = `0x<utf8-hex>` → the names
don't match → dead link.

## The change

Route destination *registration* through the same `derive_anchor_from_id` that *references* already
use, at the points where the destination name is emitted:

| Location | Path |
| --- | --- |
| `add_dest_for_block` | all block destinations (covers `[discrete]` headings via `convert_floating_title`, and any block with a non-ASCII explicit id) |
| `convert_inline_anchor` — `:link` | inline link with `id=` |
| `convert_inline_anchor` — `:ref` | inline anchor (`[[id]]`, `anchor:id[]`) |
| `convert_inline_anchor` — `:bibref` | bibliography anchor (`[[[id]]]`) |
| `convert_inline_quoted` | phrase anchor (`[#id]#text#`) |

`derive_anchor_from_id` is **idempotent** for values that are already derived or ASCII-only (it returns
them unchanged), so this is a no-op for everything that already worked — sections (already derived),
`toc`, `pdf-anchor`, and every ASCII id. Only non-ASCII block/inline anchor names change, which is
exactly the broken case.

Internal, raw-on-both-sides destination names are deliberately **left untouched** so they keep
matching their (also raw) references: the `_bibref_ref_` citation backlinks, the `_footnoteref_` /
`_footnotedef_` footnote backlinks (integer-suffixed, always ASCII anyway), and index-term anchors
(registered raw and looked up raw by the index).

> Note on scope: the issue describes `[discrete]` headings and `[[id]]` / `anchor:id[]` anchors. The
> fix also covers the phrase anchor `[#id]#text#` (`convert_inline_quoted`), because it shares the
> identical root cause and the existing dest spec already treats `[[details]]` and `[#details]#details#`
> as equivalent inline-anchor forms. If you'd prefer to keep the PR strictly scoped, that one line can
> be dropped — but the bug is present there too.

## Tests

Added two specs in `spec/xref_spec.rb`, next to the existing
`should reference section with ID that contains non-ASCII characters` example:

- `should reference discrete heading with ID that contains non-ASCII characters`
- `should reference inline anchor with ID that contains non-ASCII characters` (covers both
  `[[id]]` and `[#id]#text#` forms)

Each asserts that the registered destination name **and** the link annotation's `/Dest` are both the
hex-encoded id, i.e. they match. Both specs **fail before** this change (the destination is registered
under the raw-bytes key) and **pass after**.


## CHANGELOG

Added an entry under `== Unreleased` → `Bug Fixes::` in `CHANGELOG.adoc`.

author: rightrootpark
body:
💡 **What:** Removed `stream.DataAvailable` check in the network receive loops of both `Contrul_tester` and `Contrul_tester_WinForms`. Directly awaited `stream.ReadAsync()` instead to read packet streams synchronously but without blocking the main thread.

🎯 **Why:** The codebase previously polled `DataAvailable` alongside `Task.Delay(10)`. This created an artificial packet arrival delay (jitter) between 0 to 10ms (averaging ~5ms), severely hampering reliable real-time processing and causing unnecessary CPU spin cycles.

📊 **Impact:** Reduces packet arrival jitter from ~4.9-5.7ms down to ~0.5-1.0ms. Eliminates polling overhead and uses native OS async completion ports.

🔬 **Measurement:** Hooked up standard test client and observed delta time between packet events. Additionally added a journal entry regarding avoiding polling anti-patterns to `.jules/bolt.md`.

body:
## Summary
Detects ERROR and WARN keywords in CloudWatch logs from dbt tasks and sets the appropriate log level before forwarding to Logtail/Better Stack. This enables proper alerting on dbt run failures.

## Changes
- Add logLevelDetector module to detect log levels and strip ANSI codes
- Modify logtail forwarder to include level in payload when detection enabled
- Add ENABLE_LOG_LEVEL_DETECTION env var (default: true)
- Strip ANSI escape sequences from messages before sending to Better Stack

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: ERROR lines tagged as error level
- AC2: WARN lines tagged as warn level  
- AC3: All other lines default to info
- AC4: ANSI codes stripped from message and before level detection
- AC5: Feature can be disabled via environment variable

## Testing
- 11 new tests for logLevelDetector module (all passing)
- 7 new tests for forwarder integration (all passing)
- 18 total tests passing

## Risk

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**

Changes the Logtail/Better Stack payload shape for every plain-text log line and defaults detection on for all deployments.

> **Overview**

- Introduces keyword-based level tagging (`ERROR` / `WARN` → `error` / `warn`, else `info`) before HTTP ingestion.
- When enabled (default), ANSI escape codes are stripped from plain-text messages; structured Powertools messages are unchanged.
- Operational concern: lockfile format upgrade may break CI (`pnpm` 8 in workflow vs lockfile v9); verify install + `pnpm run validate` on CI before merge.
- Alerting behavior changes: dbt summary lines containing `ERROR=` are elevated to `error` level; non-dbt log sources may see new `level` fields unless disabled via env.

author: snajpa
body:
## Summary

Refs #843.

This first slice teaches `tidefs-placement-planner` to admit placement candidates through storage-intent roles instead of treating `TierGoal` as the whole model. It adds a planner-local hard-gate evaluator over `tidefs-storage-intent-core` records so storage intent can distinguish sync intent, cache-only serving trials, authoritative hot serving, durable full placement, cold/archive, geo/remote, and repair/relocation roles.

The evaluator consumes compiled policy, receipt, evidence-query, media-capability, trust/domain, data-shape, allocator/layout, prediction, cost/wear, and prefetch/residency records as inputs. Missing, stale, compacted, contradictory, refused, or unknown producer evidence is preserved as typed refusal/degraded/conservative state rather than scored as an ordinary preference.

Existing `TierGoal` behavior is left intact; the new API records `TierGoal` as a legacy hint only when it is supplied.

## Issue Boundary

This PR does not emit fsync receipts, implement transport measurements, add operator UI, move authority, retire receipts, or activate product-facing placement claims. Open evidence producers named by #843 remain non-blocking for this first slice because absent or unusable evidence fails closed through typed planner reasons.

The #957 media-native convergence matrix remains an authority reference: durable/media-role legality is consumed through storage-intent media-capability predicates before device or media labels can satisfy a role.

author: srejoye
body:
## What type of PR is this?
Bug fix

## Description
`consumeTokenQuota` performed a **read → check → increment** across three separate Redis round-trips. Any two concurrent requests for the same `userIdOrIp` key could read the identical stale counter, both pass the quota check, and both write their token increment — allowing up to `N × tokensRequired` tokens to be consumed before the counter reflected any of them. This is a textbook TOCTOU (time-of-check / time-of-use) race condition.

## Fix
Replace the three round-trips with a single `redis.eval()` call that runs a **Lua script atomically on the Redis server**. Redis serialises all commands and guarantees no other client command executes while the Lua script is running, so the check-and-increment is race-free by design.

**Script contract** — returns `[allowed, usedTokens, ttlSec]`:
- If `current + needed > limit` → `[0, current, TTL]` (denied, no write)
- Otherwise → `[1, newTotal, TTL]` (allowed, INCRBY already applied)

Additional fixes bundled in the same change:
- `EXPIRE` is now only set when the key is **first created** (`after == needed`), not on every request — avoiding a subtle TTL-reset race under concurrency.
- TTL is now aligned to **midnight UTC** (seconds to next day boundary) instead of a rolling 48-hour window, matching the `YYYY-MM-DD` key naming convention already in use.
- Fail-closed error handling is preserved.

## Related issues
Closes #3872

## Changes
- `backend/src/app/middleware/rate_limit.store.ts` — replace non-atomic GET / INCRBY / EXPIRE with a single `eval(QUOTA_LUA, ...)` call
- `backend/src/__tests__/rateLimitStore.test.ts` — four new tests: allow path, deny path, single-eval assertion (proves atomicity at the call-site level), 10-concurrent-burst simulation, Redis error fail-closed

## Screenshots or screen recording
N/A — backend logic change with unit test coverage.

## Added to documentation?
No documentation change required.

author: darth-sipid
body:
## Summary

Fixes an iOS crash where archiving a message and then sending the app to the background could kill it a second or two later (reported on **0.10.29**, TestFlight). The fix replaces the message list's per-row swipe mechanism on touch platforms; **macOS is unchanged**.

## Root cause

The shared `.ips` is a **scene-update watchdog termination**, not a logic crash:

```
exception: EXC_CRASH (SIGKILL)
termination: FRONTBOARD 0x8BADF00D
  "scene-update watchdog transgression: ... exhausted real (wall clock)
   time allowance of 10.00 seconds"
  ProcessVisibility: Background   WatchdogEvent: scene-update
```

The faulting (main) thread backtrace is pure SwiftUI display-list layout — `_ShapeStyle_RenderedShape.render`, `Color.ResolvedHDR.==`, `renderKeyedText`, `ViewGraph.updateOutputs`, `_UIHostingView.layoutSubviews`, `CA::Transaction::commit`. So iOS killed the app for spending **>10s on the main thread rendering the message list during the forced background snapshot.**

The folder had **fewer than 30 messages**, so volume isn't the cause. The cost is structural: `SwipeActionRow` gives each row native `.swipeActions` by embedding a **single-row `List`** (a `UICollectionView`-backed scroll view) inside the outer `ScrollView`/`LazyVStack`. Laying out a stack of those is expensive, and archiving (which mutates the list) followed by the synchronous background scene-update pushed even a small folder's relayout past the watchdog. (This is the same fragility 0.10.29's `@ScaledMetric` row-height change was already working around — "the per-row SwipeActionRow List began scrolling its own clipped content.")

Watchdog/hang terminations are `bug_type 309`; they don't appear in TestFlight's **Crashes** organizer, which is why the report looked missing. (The app's MetricKit collector is the other place it may have been recorded.)

## Empirical confirmation

An auth-free harness replicated `ScrollView → LazyVStack → ForEach(0..<n) → row` and timed cold synchronous layout of 14 visible rows in the simulator:

| Row type | median | max |
|---|---|---|
| embedded-`List` (before) | **42.6 ms** | 62 ms |
| hand-rolled `SwipeRow` (after) | **14.2 ms** | 17 ms |

~3× faster — and it *undercounts* the gap, because it excludes each embedded List's own async `UICollectionView` layout (the hand-rolled row has none). No AttributeGraph cycles; it's raw layout cost. The simulator is too fast to fire the 10s watchdog itself (and doesn't enforce it the same way), so **on-device is the final gate.**

## Fix

- **`SwipeRow`** (new, touch platforms): hand-rolled swipe via `ZStack` + `DragGesture`, no nested scroll view. Leading = mark read, trailing = dispose (destructive), drag-to-rest-open, full-swipe-to-fire with a haptic, snap-back, tap-to-close. Vertical scroll preserved via `simultaneousGesture` + an axis lock.
- **`messageRow`** platform-splits: **macOS keeps native `.swipeActions` (`SwipeActionRow`)** so the two-finger trackpad swipe is untouched; iOS/iPadOS/visionOS use `SwipeRow`.

Verified in the simulator that rows render correctly at rest and revealed (red Archive on trailing swipe, blue Read on leading swipe), with matching 16pt insets and separators.

## Testing

- `scripts/build-apple.sh all` — swiftlint `--strict`, macOS, iOS, visionOS all ✅
- `CabalmailKit` `swift test` — 268 tests, 0 failures ✅
- Simulator: resting + revealed render confirmed via screenshots.
- ⚠️ **On-device feel not yet validated** — gesture smoothness, haptics, and scroll/swipe arbitration can only be judged on a device. Please exercise archive-swipe + background on TestFlight before promoting to `main`.

## Summary

Three changes from today's Zack-pool investigation. The diagnosis: Zack's `zoho_user_id` only matches 22 contacts in Zoho. Henry's matches 2,137. The matching layer itself is fine — the gap is that customers owned by **former reps** (Andre Saunders, Brad Camp) never reach Zack because their Zoho Owner field still points at the former rep's user ID.

This PR ships the mechanism to fix that and raises the LTV gate.

### 1. `zoho_user_id_aliases` field in rep YAMLs

New optional list. The orchestrator treats every listed Zoho user ID as belonging to that rep when building the per-rep customer pool. Updates `zoho_user_to_rep_id_map` to register primary + every alias.

Use case: former reps whose books have been verbally reassigned but whose Owner field in Zoho hasn't been mass-updated. Cheaper than mass-updating Zoho contacts; reversible by editing one YAML.

### 2. Raise `min_lifetime_spend_cents` to $2,000

Per Henry — `200000` cents replaces `100000`.

### 3. `scripts/dump_zoho_owners.py`

Reads `.cache/zoho/contacts.json` and prints every distinct Owner (`owner_id`, `owner_name`, `contact_count`) sorted by count desc. Pre-populates the haystack so the operator can find a former rep's Zoho user ID without clicking through Zoho admin.

Usage:
```bash
uv run python -m sync.zoho_crm           # populate cache
uv run python -m scripts.dump_zoho_owners
```

## What's still required from Henry

Zack's YAML carries an empty `zoho_user_id_aliases: []` with a TODO comment for **Andre Saunders + Brad Camp's user IDs**. Two paths:

- **Paste them in chat** (find at Zoho CRM → Setup → Users → click user → URL ends with the ID)
- **Run the dump script** after the next dispatch and grep for the names

I'll do a follow-up commit dropping the IDs into `config/reps/zack.yaml` once you have them.

author: rcshoemaker
body:
## Summary

Adds two `Get-*` functions to `Functions/PS-Get.psm1`:

- **`Get-PowerShellHealth`** - a read-only diagnostic for managed Windows endpoints. It inspects the things that most often break Windows PowerShell 5.1: engine version, .NET Framework, execution policy (all scopes), language mode, TLS / strong crypto, `PSModulePath`, the PowerShellGet / PackageManagement / NuGet / PSGallery stack, PSReadLine, logging policy, WinRM, profiles, system-drive free space, console encoding, session errors, and pending reboot. Prints a color-coded report by default, or emits result objects with `-PassThru` for CSV / RMM ingestion.
- **`Get-DotNetFrameworkVersion`** - maps the `NDP\v4\Full` `Release` DWORD to a friendly version using Microsoft's documented minimum thresholds (verified against Microsoft Learn).

Each check is isolated in its own `try/catch`, so one failure never aborts the rest of the report. Both functions are safe to run unelevated (a few checks report more detail when elevated).

## Review fixes applied during integration

This started as a standalone script; the following were addressed while folding it into the module:

- **Removed the standalone scaffolding** (`#Requires`, file header, and the `$MyInvocation.InvocationName` auto-run trailer). Left in, that trailer would run a full health report on every `Import-Module` (i.e. every `irm ps.mauletech.com | iex`). The useful header context was folded into the function help.
- **Session-error check** now snapshots `$Error.Count` at function entry, so it reports pre-existing errors rather than the noise generated by the health check's own `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` probing.
- **.NET threshold** raised to `461808` (4.7.2) so PASS/WARN matches the "4.7.2 or newer recommended" message.
- **TLS check** treats `SystemDefault` (value `0`) as INFO instead of a false WARN on modern OSes where the OS negotiates the protocol.

## Housekeeping

- Replaced 6 U+2014 EM DASH characters in pre-existing `PS-Get.psm1` comments with hyphens to satisfy the repo's ASCII-only rule for `.psm1` files (comments only, no behavior change).

## Notes

- Validated structurally (pure ASCII, balanced braces, tab indentation, clean insertion boundaries); a live PowerShell parse was not possible in this environment, as `pwsh` is not installed.
- The module's Authenticode signature is intentionally stale on this branch; `code-signing.yml` re-signs on merge to `main`.

author: rayondemiel
body:
## What & why
  Access-controlled IIIF datasets/spectra returned 401/403: the plugin fetches them
  directly, outside Mirador's auth. This PR makes them **reuse Mirador's own IIIF Auth
  1.0 session** — one sign-in unlocks protected images *and* their datasets (no second
  login, no parallel token store). Shipped as the optional `mirador-xyviewer/mirador-auth`
  subexport, the only place coupled to Mirador's auth-state shape.

  #13: resolve auth API authentification IIIF 1.0 

  ## What it does
  - **Read side** — attaches `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on dataset fetches *and*
    protected downloads when a Mirador token matches: the resource's **declared** auth
    service (spec-correct, works cross-origin) or **host-inheritance** (same origin).
    Silently re-acquires the token on reload.
  - **Write side** — a "Sign in" affordance drives the IIIF Auth 1.0 login (origin-checked
    popup + token iframe) for resources that declare an auth service, then auto-retries.

  ## Security model
  - **Origin scoping** — `trustedOrigins` is optional: omitted → host-driven (a token is
    reused only on its issuing origin); an explicit list enables cross-origin reuse /
    cookies; `[]` → deny-all. Anti-exfiltration gate on declared services.
  - **SSRF blocklist** (defense-in-depth) — only public-unicast hosts receive a credential
    or login; private / reserved / loopback / link-local IPs and special-use internal names
    are refused; extensible via `{ deny, allow }`.
  - **https-only** (loopback for local dev), origin-checked token replies.

  ## Scope & limitations
  - IIIF Auth **1.0/0.x** only (matches the Mirador 4 bundle); Auth 2.0 degrades to the
    manual affordance. Manifest/annotation/search auth is deferred.
  - The blocklist is a *secondary* guard — origin scoping + CORS remain primary; a client
    blocklist can't stop DNS-rebinding.
  - Also includes `fix(annotations): never rewrite IIIF Content Search responses`.

  ## Tests
  - TDD throughout; full suite green (518 tests). The host-driven scoping and SSRF blocklist
    went through an adversarial multi-agent review + re-verification.
  - Docs: `docs/IIIF-AUTH.md` (developer guide) + README section.

body:
https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-95096

## What Is Being Fixed

`LAR._importSite` had a hardcoded default of `importProcessStatus = "Successful"`, which caused every test calling `importSiteCP` without explicitly passing a status to silently assert a "Successful" import. When the import engine completes with errors — even for errors entirely unrelated to what a test is verifying — all such tests fail for the wrong reason.

Six tests were broken: `ExportImportSiteWithMappedImage`, `ExportImportWithExportTemplate`, `ExportImportSiteWithFragmentReferenceToNonExistentImage`, `ExportImportPortletWithADT`, `ExportImportGlobalDDMStructureViaInstances`, and `ExportImportGlobalPagesViaInstances`. The previous fix (liferay-headless/liferay-portal#3906) addressed only `ExportImportSiteWithMappedImage` by explicitly passing `"Completed With Errors"`, but left the default in place and the other five tests still broken for the same underlying reason.

## How It Is Being Fixed

The default `importProcessStatus = "Successful"` is removed from `_importSite` and the `importProcessStatus` parameter is dropped from both `_importSite` and `importSiteCP` entirely. An import completing with errors is not inherently a test failure — the error may be completely unrelated to the behavior the test is verifying — so no test should have a status assertion imposed on it silently. Status is now only asserted when a test explicitly requests it.

For the two tests that had no meaningful content assertion beyond the removed status check (`ExportImportWithExportTemplate` and `ExportImportSiteWithFragmentReferenceToNonExistentImage`), a proper assertion is added: navigate to Site Builder → Pages on the imported site and verify the expected page appears in the page tree, retrying up to five times with a refresh to handle any rendering lag after import. The remaining tests already have direct functional assertions: the via-instances tests assert the absence of a `PortletDataException` in the console, and `ExportImportPortletWithADT` asserts the ADT behavior on the imported page directly.

author: nanako0129
body:
## Summary

`to_epoch` shelled out to `date` for every ISO 8601 timestamp. With the default
`limit5h`+`limit7d` segments that is 1-2 `date` forks on every render, on every
platform, that the segment gate never removes. Replace the canonical `...Z` UTC
shape with pure integer date math (days-from-civil); a timezone offset, reduced
precision, or an out-of-range date falls back to `date`.

This is a per-render fork removal: it speeds up a single session, and the saving
compounds under concurrent sessions (each renders on a 1s timer, so the forks
contend for CPU).

## Measured

Per-render, single session (60 renders):

| environment | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| macOS bash 5.3 | 55 ms | 45 ms |
| macOS bash 3.2 | 53 ms | 44 ms |
| Windows Git Bash | 158 ms | 120 ms |

The same saving under concurrent renders (wall-clock per N-render batch). The
per-render win is already present at N=1; the absolute gap widens with N as the
removed forks stop contending for CPU:

| N | macOS 5.3 | macOS 3.2 | Windows Git Bash |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 68 -> 54 ms | 70 -> 57 ms | 159 -> 124 ms |
| 2 | 70 -> 58 ms | 77 -> 66 ms | 209 -> 163 ms |
| 4 | 89 -> 72 ms | 92 -> 79 ms | 255 -> 209 ms |
| 8 | 125 -> 105 ms | 142 -> 112 ms | 392 -> 339 ms |

Date forks per render drop from 2 to 0 on bash 4.2+/Git Bash/Linux (where `printf
'%(...)T'` already makes the clock and `NOW` fork-free), and from 4 to 2 on bash 3.2.

## Correctness

The fast path runs only for exactly `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` (optional `.fraction`,
optional `Z`) with in-range, real calendar fields. A tz offset, minute precision,
or an impossible date falls through to `date`, matching the old behavior on both
GNU and BSD date. `test/test-epoch.sh` asserts result- and return-code-parity with
the old date reference across epoch boundaries, leap years, the 2100 century
non-leap, the 32-bit boundary, fractional seconds, +/- offsets, fraction+offset,
minute precision, and impossible dates. Passes on bash 3.2.57, 5.3.15, and Git
Bash GNU date.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash -n` passes
- [x] All 8 test suites pass on bash 3.2 and 5.3
- [x] Canonical `...Z` shape verified fork-free (0 date forks/render via a date wrapper)
- [x] Parity verified on Git Bash GNU date (offsets applied correctly)

## Guidelines

1. Rebase before opening a pull request
2. If you are sending several unrelated fixes or features, use a branch and a separate pull request for each
3. If possible try squashing everything in a single commit. This is particularly beneficial in the case of feature merges since it allows easy bisecting when a problem arises

author: scala-steward
dfuch
body:
The issue was observed on a local run in PacketSpaceManagerTest: org.opentest4j.AssertionFailedError: nextDeadline should not be after 250ms from now! ==> expected: but was: at org.junit.jupiter.api.AssertionFailureBuilder.build(AssertionFailureBuilder.java:151) at org.junit.jupiter.api.AssertionFailureBuilder.buildAndThrow(AssertionFailureBuilder.java:132) at org.junit.jupiter.api.AssertFalse.failNotFalse(AssertFalse.java:63) at org.junit.jupiter.api.AssertFalse.assertFalse(AssertFalse.java:36) at org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertFalse(Assertions.java:239) at PacketSpaceManagerTest$SynchronousTestDriver.run(PacketSpaceManagerTest.java:856) Investigation suggests that this is caused by a race condition where `packetSent` was invoked while the transmitter task was running: `packetSent` will only reschedule the transmitter if there is no deadline, that is, if it observes that `deadline == Deadline.MAX`; But if `deadline` is already in the past, which is typically the case when the transmitter task is running, then there's no guarantee that the transmitter task will actually end up rescheduling itself with a new deadline. It may not if it thinks there is nothing pending. The transmitter will then remain unscheduled until something else happens that causes it to be rescheduled. In a typical HTTP/3 request/response exchange chances are high that "something else" will happen, which explains why even if `packetSent` fails to reschedule, there might not be any observable consequence (outside of PacketSpaceManagerTest). However, there is no guarantee. The fix is to always call PacketSpaceManager::reschedule, which will compute a new prospective deadline which the timer queue can then reliably use to decide whether the selector should be woken up to take into account the new deadline. A new testPacketSent() test that deterministically fails without the fix is added to PacketSpaceManagerTest. --------- - [x] I confirm that I make this contribution in accordance with the [OpenJDK Interim AI Policy](https://openjdk.org/legal/ai). --------- ### Progress - \[x\] Change must be properly reviewed (1 review required, with at least 1 [Reviewer](https://openjdk.org/bylaws#reviewer)) - \[x\] Change must not contain extraneous whitespace - \[x\] Commit message must refer to an issue ### Issue * [JDK-8386985](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8386985): PacketSpaceManagerTest failed with AssertionError; A race condition may cause packetSent to mistakenly skip rescheduling of the transmitter task (**Bug** - P4) ### Reviewers * [Daniel Jeliński](https://openjdk.org/census#djelinski) (@djelinski - **Reviewer**) ### Reviewing

author: roboomp
body:
## Repro

Setting any role to `ollama-cloud/deepseek-v4-pro` (or `-flash`) makes every chat request 400 against `https://ollama.com/api/chat`:

```
max_tokens (1048576) exceeds model's maximum output tokens (65536) for model deepseek-v4-pro
```

The wire request carries `options.num_predict: 1048576`. Confirmed by feeding a stale-cache `Model<"ollama-chat">` spec (`maxTokens: 1048576`, no `omitMaxOutputTokens`) through `streamSimple` with a mock fetch — the captured body shows `num_predict = 1048576` going out untouched. See [issue #3392](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/3392) for the reporter's `~/.omp/agent/models.db` row.

## Cause

`packages/ai/src/providers/ollama.ts` `createChatBody` builds `options.num_predict` straight from the caller's `options.maxTokens` whenever `model.omitMaxOutputTokens` is falsy. The catalog generator (`packages/catalog/scripts/generated-policies.ts:211`) and the load-time policy (`packages/coding-agent/src/config/model-registry.ts:1665`) both set `omitMaxOutputTokens: true` for `provider: "ollama-cloud"`, but those are policy layers — the wire layer has no clamp. Anything that bypasses the policy reaches the wire:

- Stale `models.db` rows persisted by discovery runs predating `omitMaxOutputTokens` normalization (16.1.3).
- Custom `modelOverrides` entries re-setting `omitMaxOutputTokens: false`.
- Future regressions in the registry merge/policy chain.

The cached spec carries `maxTokens: 1048576` (the bundled catalog value, equal to the model's context window — not its output cap), and `stream.ts:802` flows it into `options.maxTokens` (`options?.maxTokens ?? model.maxTokens ?? undefined`). Ollama Cloud 400s anything above 65536.

## Fix

- `packages/ai/src/providers/ollama.ts` — introduced `OLLAMA_CLOUD_NUM_PREDICT_CAP = 65_536` and `resolveNumPredict(model, requested)`, which clamps every `provider: "ollama-cloud"` request to that cap. `createChatBody` now routes `num_predict` through it before serialization, so even when the load-time `omitMaxOutputTokens` policy never normalized the spec the wire request stays inside Ollama Cloud's hard limit. Self-hosted `ollama` (and any other `ollama-chat` provider) is bypassed and remains unclamped.
- The existing `model.omitMaxOutputTokens` short-circuit is preserved — the clamp is additive defense, not a replacement.

Per-model caps weren't introduced: Ollama Cloud's 65536 ceiling is uniform across the cloud-served models we've probed, and the constant carries a JSDoc anchor (`#3392`) so the next bump is a one-line edit.

## Verification

`bun test packages/catalog/test/ollama-cloud-output-caps.test.ts` — 7/7 pass, including two new `#3392` regressions:

- "clamps num_predict at the Ollama Cloud 65536 output-token cap" — drives a stale-cache spec (`maxTokens: 1_048_576`, no `omitMaxOutputTokens`) through `streamSimple`, asserts the captured request body's `options.num_predict === 65_536`.
- "does not clamp num_predict for self-hosted ollama" — local `ollama` provider spec with `maxTokens: 131_072` round-trips at 131_072 (no `provider: "ollama-cloud"` ⇒ no clamp).

Cross-checked side-effect surfaces: `bun test packages/ai/test/proxy.test.ts packages/ai/test/ollama-thinking-disable.test.ts packages/ai/test/stream-markup-healing.test.ts` — 64/64 pass.

Fixes #3392

author: aleskalfas
body:
Closes #269

## Summary

Feature #268 / Task #269: make the lifecycle-state **READ** map-aware so a `derive`-bound `state` resolves from the adopter's substrate (open/closed + a `Blocked` label) instead of kit `state:*` labels — the DEC-033 detection-predicate swap for brownfield. **Closes the SIBLING GAP #265's write side documented** — with this, derive-bound brownfield state works **end-to-end (read + write)**.

- **One canonical fix point:** `infer_current_state` is the single state-read home (the engine detectors + the descendant walk + move-issue all delegate). Making *it* map-aware (optional `substrate_map` kwarg, default `None` = today exactly) made the whole detection path map-aware at one point — below the content-free engine (DEC-033 D5).
- **The derive arm** (`_lib/axis_labels.py`): `derive_state` (closed⇒done; open+Blocked⇒blocked; open⇒open — ADR-026 §5 reduced state set), `state_derive_binding`, `has_blocked_label`, `resolve_read`, `BLOCKED_LABEL_NAME`.
- **Wedge closed:** a stray leftover `state:todo` on an open issue is **ignored** (derive reads only open/closed+label) — pinned through the engine `detect_state`.
- **Silently-wrong-position bug found + fixed:** `state_is_active` would `ValueError` on the derived `open`/`blocked` ids and silently drop an open-ish child from the cascade walk — now they count active; `done`=kit `done` unchanged.
- Read/write agreement + DEC-034 fold tested through real paths; milestone→backlog skipped under derive (resolving `backlog` would be the bug — the open-ish collapse can't distinguish it).

## Honest scope (critic finding #7)

`detect_state(…,"blocked")` here proves the *predicate* resolves a blocked position; it does **not** prove the *engine* surfaces `blocked` end-to-end — that depends on the adopter's `workflow.yaml` listing a `blocked` state. **Engine-side `blocked`-state registration is the adopter-workflow / Feature concern (#268 wave), not #269.** Noted in the test module docstring so the green test isn't read as end-to-end engine coverage.

## Test plan

- [x] **Greenfield position byte-identical** (the load-bearing bar): a frozen (open/closed × milestone × labels, incl. a two-`state:*`-label row pinning first-match-wins) grid vs an **independent hand-transcribed oracle** (`_pre_269_infer`, not a call into the code under test); the existing `test_pm_lifecycle_rebind_parity` truth-table still green.
- [x] Derive read: no-state-label issue → open/closed-derived (not "no position"); stray `state:todo` ignored; closed→done; open+Blocked→blocked. Read/write agreement (close writes no kit label under derive); DEC-034 fold (closed child→done counts).
- [x] 1277 pm/process tests pass; lifecycle/process/substrate subset 499 green. `pkit decisions validate` (115) · `pkit migrations check-diff --include-working-tree --base origin/main` clean.

## Doc impact

- The derive read arm in `axis_labels.py`; the map-aware `infer_current_state` (single read home) + the `state_is_active` fix; engine detectors + move-issue thread the map. pm capability **0.28.0 → 0.29.0** (read-path behaviour under a present map; no backbone change).
- A comment pins the intentional derive forward-cascade no-op (don't "fix" the ValueError-tolerant `_state_is_behind` into a crash). The architect offered an optional ADR-026 §5 clarifying sentence on the milestone-skip; deemed the code comment sufficient (its agreed nicety-not-gap).

## Reviewed

`critic` (SHIP — parity byte-identical + oracle independent; wedge closed with no leak-back; the `state_is_active` fix correct; read/write + fold tested through real code; finding #7 scope note folded in) + `architect` (genuine DEC-033 predicate swap, engine contract unchanged; single-fix-point right; hardcoded-`Blocked` + milestone-skip both ruled correct; **no escalation**).

author: elianddb
body:
Reading a git-backed table file went chunk by chunk, and because git cat-file cannot serve a byte range, each read re-streamed the whole object from the start. Fetching a large table spawned thousands of git processes and stalled.
- Spool a git-backed table file to a local temp file on open and serve its chunk reads locally
- Look up the sizes of a chunked object's parts in a single `git cat-file --batch-check` call
- Detect an early reader close by end of stdout, so a partial read is torn down the same way on every platform
Fix #11236

## What & why
Owner wants **«больше упражнений»**. This adds a new **production** exercise type: **transform-the-sentence** — rewrite a given sentence per a grammar instruction (→ past simple / negative / passive / reported speech). It **reuses the build-the-sentence tile UI + word-position grading**, so it's low-risk and fully **offline-gradable** (no LLM in the grade path).

## Changes

- **`_grammar_generators.py`** — `TRANSFORM_SCHEMA` + `_gen_transform_the_sentence` (model returns `instruction` + `source` + the single correct `target`; rejects a no-op transform, missing parts, or an over-cap target); registered in `_GENERATORS`. Seals `{t:"transform-the-sentence", sentence: target}`.
- **`_grammar_grading.py`** — `transform-the-sentence` shares the `build-the-sentence` branch (normalized full-match `correct` + word-position partial credit).
- **`_grammar_prompts.py`** — `EXERCISE_TYPES` weight **10**.
- **`schemas.py`** — `ExerciseOut.instruction` field (without it `response_model` drops it).

### Mobile

Free-text/LLM grading (this type is deterministic by design; `free-text` stays disabled), voice, the dialog brief, altering existing types, new topics.
